docs.title: Sidebar does not remember original width when it is forced to narrow due to a smaller window
docs.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

 
 
- VS Code Version: 1.92.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.22631

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Make sure the sidebar has a normal (non-minimal) width
2. Resize the window to be very small, so that the sidebar is forced to shrink
3. Resize the window to a larger size again

Expected result: The sidebar grows to be as wide as it was before you made the window smaller

Actual result: The sidebar stays at the smaller size

This is relevant if you usually work with maximized windows, but sometimes drag the windows between multiple monitors. During the dragging phase, the window shrinks to the last size. If this size is small for some reason, it shrinks the sidebar. When you drop the window on the other monitor's top border, the window maximizes again, but the sidebar is tiny.

Many other applications (like e.g. WebStorm or the Windows Explorer) behave like the "expected result".

docs.title: Restore local model selection (ability to disable models) in VS Code Copilot Chat
docs.body:
### Summary
Until the most recent update, Copilot Chat in VS Code allowed users to manually manage which language models were enabled or disabled on their machine. This was extremely useful for avoiding models that produced poor results. However, since the introduction of the **Auto model selection** feature, this option has been removed and is no longer available.

### Problem
- The previous **local model selection** feature is gone, and users can no longer persistently disable models they do not want to use.
- The current **Auto** mode ignores local preferences and sometimes uses models that I do not want.
- The **model picker** only allows temporary manual selection, but there is no persistent local control.
- Users without organization admin rights cannot use Copilot Policies to block models globally.

### Why this matters
- Developers need control over model quality without requiring org-level admin permissions.
- Some models may be slower, less accurate, or unsuitable for specific workflows.
- The removal of local model selection reduces flexibility and negatively impacts developer experience.

### Expected behavior
- Provide a way to **locally manage model availability** in VS Code settings (e.g., `settings.json` or like before), so that Auto mode and manual selection respect this configuration.

docs.title: 📌 Feedback: Make completions behavior less aggressive / more configurable
docs.body:
We’ve heard ongoing feedback that GitHub Copilot’s completion suggestions can feel overly aggressive or intrusive at times.

This issue aims to consolidate and track all related requests around customizing when and how completions are triggered. If you've landed here, you're likely looking for a way to make Copilot feel more tailored to your workflow.

## 📢 Configurable delay setting now available in VS Code Insiders

Adding the following to [your settings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/settings#_settings-json-file) lets you control the delay (in milliseconds) before a suggestion appears after you start typing (e.g., I have set below 3 seconds):

```json
"editor.inlineSuggest.minShowDelay": 3000,
```

Caveats:
- This currently works only in VS Code Insiders + with latest pre-release version of the GitHub Copilot and GitHub Copilot Chat extensions
- This will end up in delaying both [completions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/ai-powered-suggestions#_inline-suggestions) and [next edit suggestions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/ai-powered-suggestions#_next-edit-suggestions)
- This feature is still under development, and we’ve noticed that the interaction between completions and NES behaves a bit differently with this setting. While we’re investigating, we'd value your feedback!

docs.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

When Copilot Chat in VSCode experiences an error from the model, it presents a scary error message to the user and stops, inviting the user to click retry. docs.title: Shared Copilot Chat history across multiple workspaces/projects
docs.body:
I often work with multiple copies of the same workspace in order to use GitHub Copilot on different branches simultaneously. Each copy of the project is opened as a separate workspace.

For example, I may have several local clones of the same repository, each checked out to a different branch so Copilot can help with separate tasks in parallel.

The problem is that Copilot Chat history is stored per workspace. As a result, chats related to the same logical task become fragmented across multiple project instances.

A typical scenario:

I work on several branches in parallel using separate workspace copies.

Each workspace has its own Copilot Chat history.

After restarting my computer, I reopen several project folders.

Then I need to manually search through each workspace to find the chat where a specific discussion happened.

This becomes inconvenient when trying to continue a conversation started earlier, because I may not remember which workspace contained that chat.

Suggested improvement

It would be very helpful to have an option for shared Copilot Chat history across multiple workspaces/projects, for example:

a global Copilot Chat history

or the ability to access chats across workspaces

or linking chats to a repository rather than a specific workspace folder

This would make it much easier to continue conversations when switching between different branches or project

docs.title: Expose `chatSessionResource` to `LanguageModelChatProvider.provideLanguageModelChatResponse()`
docs.body:
Language Model providers registered via `lm.registerChatModelProvider()` have no way to know which chat conversation a request belongs to. The only parameter that could carry this is `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions`, which currently includes `requestInitiator`, `modelConfiguration`, `modelOptions`, and `toolMode` (but no conversation/session identity).

I've been working around this in my provider by using heuristics (scanning message history for embedded markers) to maintain conversation continuity, but it's been fragile and error-prone.

### Precedent: Tools already have this

`LanguageModelTool.invoke()` receives `toolInvocationToken`, which at runtime is an `IToolInvocationContext { sessionResource: URI }`. The proposed `chatParticipantPrivate` API also exposes `chatSessionResource` on tool prepare/invoke options. Chat participants get `sessionResource` on `ChatRequest`.

The LM provider is invoked from the same chat session infrastructure, but the session identity is dropped before reaching the provider.

### Proposed change

Add `chatSessionResource?: Uri` (and optionally `chatRequestId?: string`) to `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions` — either in the existing `chatProvider` proposed API or as a new proposal.

The internal plumbing already exists. The change would thread `sessionResource` through:

1. `extHost.protocol.ts` `$startChatRequest` args (line ~13

When running a larger Copilot agent job, the job sometimes appears to get stuck for a long time, with repeated tool/execution activity and no clean completion. docs.body:
## Summary

Sometimes when I open a chat session, VS Code silently restores stale agent-edit content into open files, marking them dirty. **If the file has been modified since the chat last persisted its state, saving the now-dirtied buffer will overwrite those newer changes — i.e. silent data loss.** This happens even for files edited entirely inside VS Code.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a chat, have the agent edit a file. Call this content **S1**. Don't Keep/Undo.
2. Close the chat.
3. Reload VS Code.
4. Edit the file (in VS Code) and save it. Call this content **S2**.
5. Reload VS Code again.
6. Open the chat.
7. **The file's editor buffer is replaced with S1 and marked dirty.** Saving (or autosave) overwrites S2 on disk with S1 — the user's edits from step 4 are lost.

docs.title: Support cron-like scheduling syntax for automations
docs.body:
Feature request: Support cron-like syntax for automation scheduling

Describe the feature you'd like:

Add first-class support for cron-like scheduling expressions for automations so users can specify exactly when an automation should run (e.g., cron expressions or a cron-like shorthand). This enables more control than simple interval or trigger-based schedules.

Why this is useful / Use cases:
- Run automations at specific times (daily/weekly/monthly) or on complex schedules (e.g., weekdays at 18:00, first Monday of the month).
- Let agents schedule follow-up runs (e.g., land telemetry, set a timer for a few days, wake up and re-check telemetry) without manual intervention.
- Support timezone-aware schedules and optional jitter/backoff for distributed runs.

Proposed behavior and details:
- Accept standard cron expressions (with an optional seconds field) or a constrained cron-like syntax in automation definitions.
- Allow timezone specification per schedule (UTC by default).
- Provide a UI to validate and preview next run times for a given expression.
- Support persistence of automation state across runs so scheduled automations can reuse context if desired (optional toggle).

Examples:
- "0 18 * * 1-5" — run at 18:00 on weekdays
- "0 0 1 * *" — run at midnight on the first of every month

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- Keep existing interval and event-based triggers;

docs.title: Remote-SSH: Agent Session changed-file diff opens working-tree side as local Windows path, not vscode-remote:// URI
docs.body:
## Summary
When opening a diff for a file from the **Chat/Agent Sessions "changed files" list** while connected via **Remote-SSH**, VS Code fails to open the working-tree side of the diff with:

```
The editor could not be opened because the file was not found.
Unable to read file '\home\<user>\<repo>\<path\to\file>'
(Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file '\home\<user>\<repo>\<path\to\file>')
```

Note the **backslashes** and the **missing `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<host>/` authority** — the client is treating a remote POSIX absolute path as if it were a local Windows path, instead of constructing a proper `vscode-remote://` URI. The file exists and is perfectly readable on the remote host; opening it directly via Explorer/`Ctrl+P` works fine. Only the diff/editor opened from the agent session's changed-files entry fails.

This looks like the same class of bug as the older, now-closed #166937 ("Remote SSH: unable to resolve nonexistent file" — Source Control "WorkingTree" diff), but reproduced against the newer native **Agent Sessions / Chat** changed-files diff instead of classic Source Control, and on a current build, so I'm filing fresh rather than reopening.

## Environment
- VS Code version: `1.135.0` (commit `08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5`, quality `stable`)
- Client OS: Windows 11
- Remote: Remote-SSH (`remoteAuthority=ssh-remote+<host>`) to a Linux host

>[!IMPORTANT]
> _October 22 Update:_ Before commenting, please review the latest updates from the team below https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/339363#issuecomment-6346982654

---

As we continue investing in more agentic workflows and improving Copilot, the way changes are made, reviewed, and accepted has evolved. We removed the **Keep** and **Undo** controls for individual changes in chat as part of a shift toward reviewing the overall changes from an agent task, with the intent of simplifying review for longer, multi-file workflows.

We recognize that this removed useful checkpoints for incremental, file-by-file review, and that reviewing the overall result does not replace those workflows for everyone.

Changes should still be visible and reviewable **per turn, per session, and per branch**. 

A similar `changes` flow also still exists via the `changes` pill above the chat input. Clicking on this pill opens up the diff editor, which allows you to revert certain lines or edits. 

This issue is a central place to collect feedback on **granular control over Copilot changes, keep and undo**. We’d like to understand when and how you review changes, whether you can easily inspect them at the scope you need, and where you need more control over accepting or reverting them.

docs.title: Chat Customizations: group environment items by storage source
docs.body:
## Problem

The Chat Customizations editor currently mixes two different concepts at the same hierarchy level:

- **Workspace**, **User**, **Extensions**, **Plugins**, and **Built-in** describe where a customization is stored and who owns it.
- Provider group keys such as `remote-host` and `remote-client` describe which side supplied the customization to the active agent. They currently render as **Remote** and **This Computer**.

This makes the list difficult to understand. **Remote** can mean an Agent Host environment that is actually running on the same computer, while **This Computer** can contain items synced into another environment. The location-oriented terminology will become even less useful as VS Code transitions away from the Local agent harness and standardizes on the Copilot harness.

## Proposal

Use storage/ownership as the primary grouping axis for customizations:

- Workspace
- User
- Extensions
- Plugins
- Built-in

Preserve execution provenance on each row with a dedicated, accessible treatment instead of creating parallel environment groups. For example, a row could indicate that it was discovered in the **Agent Environment** or **Synced from This Computer** while still appearing under its Workspace, User, Extension, Plugin, or Built-in owner.

This should work consistently whether the active Agent Host runs locally, through a tunnel, or in another remote e

docs.body:
Anthropic's [Preserved thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking) say each thinking block's signature is tied to everything that came before it in the conversation. If anything earlier in the history is different from when the block was created, that block and the later ones get rejected.

I think Copilot may be rebuilding the history differently from what it originally sent when it replays it in a long tool loop. I haven't found where that happens.

When Copilot rebuilds the history, it should keep it identical to what was sent before, so a long tool loop doesn't fail partway through. If it still fails, retrying once without the rejected thinking block would be better than resending the same request.

docs.title: Agent Host: remote prompts with command-… source missing from VS Code chat
docs.body:
In VS Code 1.142.0 using the Copilot harness over Remote-SSH, prompts sent through GitHub.com reach the agent and receive responses, but the user prompts do not appear in VS Code's chat history.

### Reproduce

1. Start a Copilot Agent Host session.
2. Enable `/remote on`.
3. Open the session on GitHub.com and send a prompt.
4. Check VS Code: the remote user prompt is missing.

Expected: both the prompt and response appear in VS Code.

### Evidence

The session log records incoming remote prompts with:

```json
{
  "type": "user.message",
  "data": {
    "source": "command-<id>",
    "content": "Testing"
  }
}
```

The [Agent Host handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L7359) appears to skip these events:

```ts
if (e.data.source && e.data.source.toLowerCase() !== 'user') {
    return;
}
```

During the remote test, Agent Host also logged:

```text
Markdown delta emitted with no active turn; dropping
```

The older CLI integration explicitly handled command-sourced user messages in [microsoft/vscode#312428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/312428). The Agent Host path may need equivalent handling.

docs.title: Sessions list rows overlap after observing chat details re-enters the tree splice
docs.body:
In the Agents window, the sessions list sometimes renders rows on top of each other ("ghost" rows that stay at stale positions until the window reloads). Once it happens, the renderer log fills with `TreeError [SessionsListTree] Tree element not found` from scrolling, expanding sessions, and sticky scroll.

 

## Root cause

Rendering a chat row re-enters the sessions list tree while it is splicing:

1. Expanding a session splices its chat rows into the list (`ListView._splice` → `insertItemInDOM` → `renderElement`).
2. The row's `autorun` reads a peer chat observable wrapped by `_withDetails`. Its first observer acquires chat details, which synchronously opens the session-state subscription (`_onFirstReference` → `_ensureSessionStateSubscription`) and applies the subscription's cached state.
3. Since #342624, `_applyChatCatalogFromState` fires `onDidChangeSessions` when that state reorders the session's chats.
4. `SessionsList.refresh()` → `update()` → `tree.setChildren()` runs synchronously inside the outer splice. The tree model applies the new children, but `ListView.splice` throws `Can't run recursive splices.`, so the view keeps rows the model no longer knows → overlapping rows and the follow-up `Tree element not found` errors.

Stack from Insiders (`5170ebe`), abbreviated:

"Feature" request.

The integrated terminal grows in functionality, to the point that it could soon become very useful standalone, as its *own app*. docs.title: Agent Host (Copilot harness): stale pending changes cannot be kept or dismissed after the file was edited later (were updated after they were shown)
docs.body:
**Environment:** VS Code 1.144.0 (2c33b50), Windows x64, Copilot harness (agent host)

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a Local harness session, let the agent create/edit a file. Do not keep the changes yet.
2. Switch to the Copilot harness. The pending changes UI briefly disappears, so the edits can't be kept.
3. Keep editing the same file (in later sessions and/or manually).
4. Later, the old session's changes pill/working set shows the file again.
5. Click **Keep** (or stage the file in Source Control).

### Actual
```
Could not keep changes to <file>: The changes to '<file>' were updated after they were shown. Try again.
```
This repeats after reloading the window. There is no way to dismiss the entry without **Undo**, which would revert later work.

### Expected
**Keep** should accept the current on-disk contents (or the entry should drop out once the file has diverged), or there should be a "Dismiss" / "Clear pending changes" action.

### Notes
- The stale state lives in the session's agent host database (`file_edits` rows + `agentHost.changes` metadata); `reviewed_files` stays empty.
- Several older sessions show this kind of stale change counter.
- Workaround: with VS Code closed, delete `file_edits` rows and reset `agentHost.changes` to zero.
- Possibly related: #339363

docs.title: Git - treat tracked discard paths literally
docs.body:
Fixes #346864.

Discarding changes in a tracked file named `[target]` also overwrites edits in a sibling file named `t`: Git interprets the selected filename as a pathspec, although the UI confirms discarding only `[target]`.

Pass `--literal-pathspecs` for checkout operations that receive file paths. Add a regression through the public Git extension API that verifies the selected file is restored and the other file keeps its edits, including paths with spaces.

Related: #133566 and #324378. The existing PR addresses untracked-file deletion with `git clean`; this fixes the tracked-file checkout path.

Validation:

- The new extension API regression fails on unchanged production code and passes with the fix.
- Git extension integration suite: 91 passing, two existing disabled tests.
- The unchanged three-step workbench scenario fails before the fix and passes afterward: the confirmation names `[target]`, only that file is restored, and `t` retains its edits.
- Git extension compilation/type checking and targeted ESLint pass.

Validated on macOS arm64 with Git 2.55.0. The regression uses filenames supported on Windows as well as POSIX; the Windows suite was not run locally.

docs.title: fix: preserve logger ownership across windows and replacements
docs.body:
This PR is needed for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/334242
### Details When two windows register the same log file, main remembers only the last window. Closing that window can remove the surviving window's logger. Delayed logger notifications can also remove a replacement that a client has already created for the same resource. ### Change Track window and global owners independently, release only the departing owner, and dispose the logger after its final owner leaves. Preserve current local registrations when processing mirrored additions and removals. ### Before Closing the second window removed a shared logger and dropped the surviving window's next message. Queued removal and addition notifications could dispose a replacement logger and stop its logging and log-level updates. ### After Both window-close orders preserve the remaining owner. Replacement loggers keep writing and receive log-level changes. Removing the final owner still disposes the logger.

docs.title: Opening a named pipe (FIFO) in the editor fails with “Unavailable (FileSystemError)” since 1.139
docs.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

 
 
- VS Code Version: 
- OS Version: 

Steps to reproduce

1. Create a FIFO and keep a writer attached: mkfifo /tmp/p; (echo "A=1" > /tmp/p &). Or mount a 1Password Environment as a local .env file (1Password serves it as a FIFO).
2. Open the path in VS Code (File > Open File, or Quick Open).

Actual: `Unavailable (FileSystemError): An unknown error occurred. Please consult the log for more details.`

Expected: The contents are read, as in 1.138 and earlier, and in Cursor.

Analysis: `DiskFileSystemProvider.openFileForRead()` in `src/vs/platform/files/node/diskFileSystemProvider.ts` throws `FileSystemProviderErrorCode.Unavailable` (“File is not a regular file”) whenever `!stat.isFile()`. It was introduced in e0bfcd60b41, “Improve named pipes (#336687)”, first shipped in 1.139.0. Before that, `readFile` used `promises.readFile(filePath)` and the stream path opened with 'r', which worked for FIFOs. The accompanying test only covers a pipe without a writer, but the check rejects all FIFOs, including ones with an active writer.

Impact: 1Password Environments local .env mounts (macOS/Linux) can’t be opened in VS Code.

Suggested direction: Allow FIFOs when the open succeeds under O_NONBLOCK and data is available. Or at least surface the “not a regular file” message instead of a generic unknown error.

docs.title: Preserve replacement text in large Replace All
docs.body:
At the find-highlight limit, Replace All reinterprets literal dollars and treats native replacement callback metadata as captures. For example, replacing regex `x` with `$1` in 20,000 matching lines currently inserts match offsets; this change inserts literal `$1` on every line, consistent with smaller inputs.

Fixes #346872.

Pass only the whole match and capture arguments to the replacement builder, preserving unmatched capture positions as empty strings. Escape literal dollars before native static replacement so the parsed text is inserted literally while retaining that fast path.

Add seven cases at both two matches and `MATCHES_LIMIT + 1`, covering literal dollars, escaped references, missing/unmatched captures, named groups and two-digit capture fallback.

explorer.excludeGitIgnore: workspace root folder is hidden when its name matches an unanchored pattern in its own .gitignore
docs.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

 
 
- VS Code Version: 1.145.2 (c4453f8ea430795f941c1b2ff6c9321135a74a02)
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.2 (arm64)

 

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `"explorer.excludeGitIgnore": true` setting
2. Create a folder `foo` (any name) containing a `.gitignore` with the single line `foo` (an unanchored pattern, as is common for ignoring a built binary named after the project).
3. Open a different folder, then use **File > Add Folder to Workspace...** to add `foo` as a second root.
4. Observe that `foo` is shown in the Explorer.
5. Expand `foo`.

## Expected

`foo` stays in the Explorer. Git only applies the pattern to paths inside the repository, so the root is never ignored.

## Actual

the `foo` root disappears from the Explorer as soon as it is expanded. After a window reload it shows again until it is expanded. If a file from `foo` is opened, the root reappears showing only that file and `.gitignore`.

Setting `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` to `false` avoids the problem.

## Analysis

`IgnoreFile.gitignoreLineToGlob` turns a pattern without a `/` into `**/foo`. `ExplorerFilter.isGitIgnored` evaluates it against the absolute resource path, and the glob reduces to a basename check. Once `.gitignore` is visited and the ignore tree is populated, the root folder's own basename matches `**/foo`, so the root is treated as ignored.

The chat message composer already has a split picker with Add to Queue, Steer with Message, and Stop and Send. That is a UI pattern to reuse for comment submission, not a capability that already exists on the comments Submit control ([chat picker](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6bab64e2d12b04d04c0d99c27ff166023efd1dda/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatQueuePickerActionItem.ts#L203-L247), [comments Submit action](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6bab64e2d12b04d04c0d99c27ff166023efd1dda/src/vs/sessions/contri

---

## Background

Masked credentials let an agent use a credential without exposing its real value inside the sandbox. Environment variables named in `chat.agent.sandbox.credentials.envVars` are replaced with placeholders inside the sandbox. For HTTPS requests, the sandbox can replace the placeholder with the real value only when the destination matches that variable's `injectHosts` list.

Hosts not listed should receive the placeholder, not the real value. This setting protects only the variables explicitly configured for masking; it does not automatically mask every environment variable. Network access is separate: listing a host in `injectHosts` does not itself grant permission to connect to it.

Fixes a flaky test that failed Monday's 05:00 UTC insider [494123](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=494123): `CopilotAgent › external chat discovery › a session reported as changed after its validation is retried instead of retired`. ```
publishedAtStartup: ['validated', 'revalidating']   // expected ['revalidating']
armed: false                                          // the stat stub did fire

The product behaves correctly. The race is in how the test orders its steps.

The intent is that this happens during `revalidating`'s **validation**, after `validated` was validated, so `validated` must be retried rather than published.
- Both sessions used the same working directory, so project resolution is shared and only the **first** session waits in `getRepositoryRoot`. `started` resolves as soon as `validated` gets there.

Bumps pnpm from 12.16.0 to [12.17.0](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.17.0) by updating the `packageManager` field in every `package.json` that pins it (13 files). Local installs, the dev container and CI (`install-pnpm.yml`, the `setup-pnpm` action) all read the version from this field, so it now lives in the same place as before.

Notes for reviewers:

- No lockfile changes: a full `pnpm install` with pnpm 12.17.0 left every `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.
- The preinstall check (`checkPackageManager` in `build/lib/pnpm.ts`) accepts the pinned version or a newer 12.x release, so contributors still on pnpm 12.16.0 are now asked to upgrade (`npm install -g pnpm@12.17.0`). The workspace sets `pmOnFail: ignore`, so pnpm doesn't switch versions automatically.
- The `node_modules` cache keys hash `packageManager`, so the first CI runs after this change will miss the cache and do full installs.

## How to test

- `npx -y pnpm@12.17.0 install` at the repository root: passed (`Done in 50.2s using pnpm v12.17.0`), with no tracked files changed.
- `getPinnedPnpmVersion()` returns `12.17.0`; `checkPackageManager()` accepts pnpm 12.17.0 and rejects 12.16.0 with the upgrade message: verified with a local Node script.
- The pre-commit hygiene hook passed.

docs.title: build: rerun failed unit and integration tests in the product build
docs.body:
The GitHub pull request workflows rerun failed tests with `--rerun-failed-files 2`. This PR does the same for the Azure Pipelines product build. The CI build stays unchanged.

### What changed

- `steps/product-build-{linux,darwin,win32}-test.yml` get a `VSCODE_RERUN_FAILED_TESTS` parameter, which defaults to `false`. When it is `true`, a compile-time `iif` adds ` --rerun-failed-files 2` to the same five commands that the PR workflows rerun:
  - Unit tests (Electron)
  - Unit tests (node.js)
  - Unit tests (Browser)
  - Agent Host E2E tests
  - Integration tests (Electron). The flag reaches only the node.js integration tests; the extension host suites are not rerun, as in the PR workflows.
- Only the product build test job templates (`{linux,darwin,win32}/product-build-*-test.yml`) set the parameter to `true`. CI jobs reach the same steps through `product-build-*-ci.yml` → `steps/product-build-*-compile.yml`, which does not pass the parameter. With `false`, the `iif` expands to an empty string, so the CI command lines are unchanged.
- Web/remote integration tests and smoke tests are not rerun, as in the PR workflows.
- `test/unit/README.md` and the `integration-tests` skill now mention that the product build uses reruns.

### Notes for reviewers

- The runners do the rerunning. They rerun only the failed tests (or whole files when more than 50 fail) in a fresh window or process

## Problem

Sections 1 (built-in extension dependencies), 2 (root `node_modules`) and 5 (platform-specific packages) list packages by reading the top level of each `node_modules` folder, and they skip dot folders. With the isolated linker, the top level holds only the install root's direct dependencies. Everything else lives in the virtual store, `node_modules/.pnpm`.

On an isolated install of `main`, the current scanner finds **378 entries instead of 1,863**:
- Section 1 finds licenses for 171 packages instead of 1,148.
- Section 2 finds 104 instead of 560.
- Section 5 finds 8 platform-binary parent packages instead of 16.

- **New `collectInstalledPackages(nmDir)`:** it lists the top-level packages as before. docs.body:
The move to pnpm 12 (#344791) added `packageManager` to every pnpm install root. Since then, seven of those roots have become members of other workspaces (#345794, #345795, #345797, #345827, #346069, #346255), but their `package.json` kept the field. This removes it from those members:

- `remote/web` (member of `remote`)
- `build/rspack`, `build/vite` (members of `build`)
- `extensions/copilot/chat-lib` (member of `extensions/copilot`)
- `extensions/markdown-language-features/test-workspace/checkbox-count-extension` (member of `extensions`)
- `src/vs/sessions/test/e2e`, `test/componentFixtures/playwright` (members of the root workspace)

`packageManager` now remains only in the six install roots that have a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: the repository root, `build`, `remote`, `extensions`, `extensions/copilot` and `test/sanity`.

Why the members don't need it:

- pnpm reads `packageManager` from the workspace root's manifest, and most install roots set `pmOnFail: ignore`.
- The build scripts and CI (`build/lib/pnpm.ts`, `installPnpm.ts`, the `setup-pnpm` action, the devcontainers) read only the field of an install root.
- Corepack walks up to the nearest `package.json` that declares `packageManager`, so members resolve their root's version.

Note for reviewers: `computeNodeModulesCacheKey` hashes the `packageManager` of every directory, so this changes the node_modules cache key once

docs.title: Inbox: Mark Session as Done needs two clicks to remove the row
docs.body:
- VS Code Version: 1.146.0-insider (142e5584a76358bbb4fb687d8a0d2f4e859a6767)
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.2 (arm64)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In the Agents window, enable `"chat.agentSessions.inbox.enabled": true` and open **Inbox**.
2. Click the checkmark (**Mark Session as Done**) in the trailing actions of a row.

### Actual

The row does not go away. The checkmark has to be clicked a second time.

### Expected

One click moves the session to Done and removes the row.

### Notes

- After a successful action, the view intentionally keeps the row for about 1.5 s with "Action taken", and ignores further clicks on it (`runRowAction` in `inboxNotificationsView.ts`). Needing a second click therefore means the row stays or comes back after that.
- Possibly related: `markSessionDone` stores the row's current `occurrence`, and the row stays in Done only while that still matches (`inboxNotificationsService.ts`). `occurrence` combines the session status, last turn end, and notification IDs. A change to any of them right after the click would return the row to its previous tab.

docs.title: Engineering - package production dependencies with either pnpm linker
docs.body:
This is part of the pnpm migration. It lets product packaging work with `nodeLinker: isolated` while shipping exactly the same `node_modules` layout. The repo stays on `hoisted`, and the artifacts don't change. Follows #346742, #346749, #346758, #346762, #346781 and #346907.

## Problem

`getProductionDependencies` (`build/lib/dependencies.ts`) reads where each package is installed from the `hoistedLocations` that pnpm's hoisted linker records in `node_modules/.modules.yaml`. Under `isolated` it throws ("must be installed with nodeLinker: hoisted"). Every consumer also globs those folders directly, and under `isolated` they don't exist: packages live in pnpm's virtual store (`node_modules/.pnpm/<id>/node_modules/<name>`). The affected consumers are:
- desktop, server and web packaging
- the Copilot and shared built-in extension dependencies
- the source-map upload
- the symbol scan

## Change

- **`build/lib/pnpmHoist.ts` (new):** computes the hoisted layout from the lockfile. It's a port of the hoister pnpm uses (pnpm 12's `real-hoist`, itself a port of Yarn's `@yarnpkg/nm` hoister), plus the rules that reproduce pnpm's output on our lockfiles:
  - importer dependencies are taken in name order;
  - the provider of a peer is the nearest ancestor that depends on it, as in pnpm's `real-hoist` (Yarn's hoister only looks at the parent);
  - a package can't be hoisted past the packa

docs.title: test: use a fixture for the Markdown rich editor diagnostics test
docs.body:
Refs #343832

`Markdown editor pull diagnostics › validates and clears diagnostics with only a custom-editor tab open` keeps failing in the Linux `Remote` integration run. The `No header found: 'missing'` warning is never cleared after the edit, most recently in main CI build 494170. This PR stops the test from racing a file watcher event. The underlying server bug is described below so it can be fixed separately.

## What happens

The test creates its Markdown file with `workspace.fs.writeFile` and opens it in the rich editor right away. The language client forwards file watcher events to the server through a 250 ms debounce (`_fileEventDelayer` in `vscode-languageclient`). Over a remote connection, the watcher event for the new file can reach the server after the test's edit.

In `vscode-markdown-languageserver` 0.5.0, `VsCodeClientWorkspace` handles a `Changed` (or `Created`) event for a cached document by calling `openMarkdownDocumentFromFs`. That re-reads the file and **replaces** the cache entry with a new disk-only document, dropping the in-memory one. Every later diagnostics pull is then computed from the old on-disk text, so the warning keeps coming back until the next edit. Locally, the event arrives before `didOpen` and is ignored, which is why only Remote fails.

I couldn't reproduce the remote timing locally, so I drove the server's real `VsCodeClientWork

docs.title: tasks: fall back to untyped lookup for task handles
docs.body:
Fixes #336152

Follow-up to #336159

Retry task-handle resolution without activating unrelated providers when the typed lookup misses. A task definition's type can differ from its provider registration type, so the fallback resolves the handle from tasks already known to the task service. The known-task lookup preserves workspace and user-task matching, and the fallback remains skipped when workspace trust was denied. Task matching consistently ranks extension tasks last and preserves order among equal ranks.

## Testing

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadTask.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/test/browser/abstractTaskService.test.ts` — passed (23 tests), covering typed lookup/fallback behavior, denied trust, workspace/user precedence in both `getTask` lookup phases, and stable equal-rank ordering.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `pnpm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/test/browser/abstractTaskService.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run compile` — passed before these follow-up changes.
- Code OSS runtime check — earlier change verified typed task execution and a mismatched definition-type fallback; the later known-only fallback and ordering refinements were validated with focused unit tests.

docs.title: Locate markdown tokens in CRLF documents when rewriting links
docs.body:
### Problem
`rewriteMarkdownLinks` finds each token in the source with `markdown.indexOf(token.raw, cursor)`. marked's `Lexer.lex` turns `
` and `` into `
` before tokenizing, so in a document with CRLF line endings the `raw` of any multi-line token, such as a fenced code block, can't be found. The fence is skipped and never recorded as a code range. The next link's lookup then matches the lookalike *inside* the fence. The result is that the sample in the code block gets rewritten, and the real link is left as it was:

```ts
rewriteMarkdownLinks('```
[a](./x.txt)
```

[a](./x.txt)', { rewriteLink: () => 'REWRITTEN' })
// before: '```
REWRITTEN
```

[a](./x.txt)'
// after:  '```
[a](./x.txt)
```

REWRITTEN'
```

`findDefinitionRanges` uses the same lookup, so for CRLF input it returns no definition ranges. Chat model output is normally LF. CRLF reaches these callers mainly through text from outside the model, for example agent-host sessions on Windows (`stateToProgressAdapter`) and imported conversations.

### Change
Both lookups now go through one locator, built once per call by `createLocator`. It normalizes the source's line endings the way the lexer does (`
` and `` become `
`), finds each token's `raw` with a single `indexOf` on that copy, and maps the offsets back to the source. So each `

docs.title: nes: don't place a next edit on a document that changed during the request
docs.body:
Fixes #331652. Supersedes #331657.

The NES inline completion provider maps the suggested edit and the request cursor onto the live `TextDocument`. If the document changes while the provider waits (after the fetch, during the minimum response delay, or while waiting for diagnostics NES), both refer to an older version. When the document lost lines, `toInlineSuggestion` read the cursor's line and threw ``Illegal value for `line` ``. #325278 made this reachable, because the advanced path now always reads the cursor's line.

- `InlineCompletionProviderImpl` records `document.version` at request time. It returns no suggestion, with the existing `docChanged` status, if the version has changed by the time the result is ready. Core already drops results for an outdated version (`canceled:documentChanged` in `inlineCompletionsSource.ts`), so no suggestion that could be shown is lost. The NES provider already did this for changes during the fetch itself.
- The VS Code `toInlineSuggestion` adapter returns `undefined` for a cursor line past the end of its live document instead of throwing. The shared classifier is unchanged, because chat-lib passes the cursor and edit from the same snapshot.
- Adds a regression test that fails with the reported error without the adapter guard.

docs.title: agentHost: Look up Basic proxy credentials from the client
docs.body:
A standalone Agent Host on the same network as its client, such as a WSL host used from the Agents window on Windows, gets the proxy from the client through `vscode/resolveProxy`. It has no way to get the proxy's Basic credentials, though. Electron strips credentials from `http.proxy`, and mirroring them into the host's settings would write them to disk in WSL.

This adds a host → client reverse request, `vscode/lookupProxyBasicAuthorization`, over the existing `vscode.clientProxy` capability. Its shape matches the Copilot SDK's upcoming `network.authenticateBasic` callback, so the runtime can later be served by the same request.

- **Protocol** (`clientProxyProtocol.ts`): params `{ proxyUrl, realm?, attempt }` and result `{ username?, password? }`, with validators.
- **Client** (`agentHostProtocolClient.ts`, `agentHostClientProxy.ts`): answers through `IRequestService.lookupAuthorization`, so it uses the same stored credentials and login dialog as the window's own proxy authentication. It only answers for proxies it resolved for the host (system/PAC proxy or `http.proxy`), and not at all when `http.useLocalProxyConfiguration` is off. This matters because `ProxyAuthService` returns the credentials of `http.proxy`, or else of a proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`, for any host on the first attempt, so while either has credentials only that proxy qualifies. Unsupported proxy URLs

agentHost: Keep Mission Control lanes open for oversized chat snapshots
docs.body:
A VS Code client connected to a GitHub environment (Mission Control) kept losing its connection whenever it had a large chat open.

## Why

The relay's chunking codec rejects any single message larger than 32 MiB, the reassembly limit that relay receivers enforce. A long chat's `subscribe` snapshot was larger than that (more than 32.5 MiB in a local reproduction). `MissionControlProtocolServer._publish` threw before queueing, and the lane's `send()` closed the lane without logging a reason. The host's only trace was `[ProtocolServer] Client disconnected`. The client then reconnected, subscribed to the same chat again and lost the lane again, about every 30 seconds.

Relay connections could not avoid the limit, because windowed state-channel delivery (#345886) was disabled for relay transports on both the host and the client.

## What changed

- **Windowed delivery on Mission Control relays.** Large snapshots and actions are sent as `channel/frame` fragments within the window, well under the relay limit.
  - Windowed delivery counts every message's size. The spec measures the received text, but a relay does not keep a message's text. Both relay transports (`WebPubSubRelayTransport` on the client, `MissionControlLane` on the host) therefore measure each relayed message by its `JSON.stringify` serialization, computed lazily when first read. That equals what a `JSON.stringify` send

docs.title: Preserve targets when overwrite source is missing
docs.body:
Fixes #346975

An overwrite-enabled move or copy currently deletes its existing destination before discovering that the source is missing. Stat the source immediately before the destructive deletion so the operation fails while preserving the destination.

The check stays in the actual overwrite operation. Preflight must continue to allow sources created by earlier edits in a batch; atomic moves and case-only renames retain their existing paths.

Eight new regressions cover move/copy, same/cross provider and file/nonempty-folder targets. All eight fail before the fix and pass afterward. Validation also passed 41 disk move/copy tests, 11 atomic/in-memory checks, 12 symlink overwrite combinations and targeted ESLint.

An actual extension-host reproduction on installed VS Code 1.145.2 loses the destination in all four public-API cases; patched main preserves all four while still reporting `FileNotFound`. This is bounded protection for an already-missing source, not a general transactional-copy guarantee.

docs.title: Serialize rapid virtual document refreshes
docs.body:
Fixes #346976

Three rapid virtual-document refreshes can resume from the same pending operation, allowing a slow second response to overwrite the newer third response. Queue refreshes by document URI and wait for the main-thread update acknowledgement before starting the next refresh for that document. Independent documents can still refresh concurrently.

Queued callbacks also check that their provider is still registered before starting. This avoids reporting `unsupported uri-scheme` when a provider fires a change event and immediately disposes its registration. Refreshes that already started retain their existing completion behaviour.

Regression coverage checks same-document ordering, independent-document progress, rejection recovery, unchanged and empty content, document closure and provider disposal. The new fire-then-dispose and pending-queue regressions fail on `034e957` through the normal unexpected-error check and pass with the registration guard. Dispose-before-fire and in-flight-only controls pass on both versions.

- The original ordering bug reproduced in installed VS Code 1.145.2; the new disposal regressions were verified against the source branch.

docs.title: Overlapping background tasks share and dispose each other’s problem markers
docs.body:
Overlapping background tasks can use or dispose another terminal's problem-start marker.

The affected sequence is:

1. Start a watch cycle in terminal A.
2. Start a watch cycle in terminal B before A finishes.
3. Finish A with errors, or finish it without errors while B's cycle remains active.

When A reports errors, its buffer decoration receives B's marker. When A finishes without errors, it disposes B's marker. Each terminal should retain its own marker for its own watch cycle.

`TaskTerminalStatus` keeps one `_marker` field for the whole manager, although `addTerminal` installs separate problem-collector callbacks for each terminal. B's callback overwrites the reference subsequently used by A's callbacks.

I reproduced both outcomes through the production status manager and `WatchingProblemCollector` line-data pipeline with real in-memory xterm instances. Both regression cases fail on unchanged main and pass when the marker is scoped to its terminal registration. The exact task-status and collector sources from stable 1.145.2 fail the same checks under the test harness.

Runtime: main 1.147.0, macOS arm64. This is a marker-ownership reproduction; a packaged-stable visual-decoration run was not performed.

docs.title: Deleting a shared chat-created file leaks or prematurely disposes its entry
docs.body:
Deleting a file shared by two loaded local chat editing sessions does not consistently release each session's reference to its modified-file entry.

The affected path is:

1. Chat A creates a file through a text edit.
2. Keep A loaded and let chat B edit that same file, so both sessions share its entry.
3. Delete the file, or undo its creation in A.

With ordinary deletion, both working sets drop the entry, but the original text model and one file watcher remain alive. With undo, A already removes and releases its reference before the deletion notification; its callback releases it again. B then retains an entry whose original model has been disposed.

Expected: each session removes and releases only the reference it currently owns, leaving no file entries, original model or watcher after deletion.

Two synthetic regressions through `ChatService`, real local-session/request models and streamed `textEdit` handling reproduce these outcomes on main 1.147.0. They use local model/deletion fixtures and no live chat provider. A reference-ownership guard in the deletion callback makes both pass. The four relevant implementation files are byte-identical in stable 1.145.2.

Validation was on macOS arm64. This establishes resource retention and stale working-set state; it is not a measured heap-size or live-model/UI result.

docs.title: Reusing an unresolved restored browser tab loads its old URL
docs.body:
A restored Integrated Browser tab reused before its first resolution can load the saved URL instead of the newly requested URL.

The affected scenario is an inactive browser tab restored after a restart. For example, its saved URL is `http://localhost:3000/previous`, and an extension reuses it with:

```js
await vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.action.browser.open', {
  url: 'http://localhost:3000/requested',
  reuseUrlFilter: 'http://localhost:3000/**'
});
```

If the tab has no native model yet, navigation updates the input's pending URL. Its resolver subsequently creates the native view with captured `data.url`, still pointing to `/previous`.

Expected: native creation uses `/requested`. Actual: it receives `/previous`, and the resolved input reflects that old destination.

Confirmed through the registered command, real lazy input and workbench service, recording the native creation request. The focused regression fails on unchanged main; an exact stable 1.145.2 service-module replay fails identically. Using the current pending URL, with the same scheme normalization as normal navigation, passes the case and a bare-localhost compatibility control.

Runtime: main 1.147.0, macOS arm64. This is a command/service-level reproduction; a full application restart and Chromium navigation were not exercised.

docs.title: Notebook reload and save overwrite changed output metadata
docs.body:
Reverting and later saving a notebook can write stale output metadata back to disk, even though the cell source and output data were unchanged during reload. Related to #168923.

Confirmed in installed **VS Code 1.145.2 Stable** (`c4453f8ea430795f941c1b2ff6c9321135a74a02`) and current main on macOS arm64, using the public notebook API and `.ipynb` serializer.

1. Open an `.ipynb` with one code cell and two PNG display outputs. Set their `metadata["image/png"]` dimensions to 10 and 11.
2. Make the notebook dirty by adding a marker to its persisted document metadata through `NotebookEdit.updateNotebookMetadata`. Keep cell source and output data unchanged.
3. Rewrite the file externally with output dimensions 20 and 21.
4. Execute `workbench.action.files.revert`.
5. Edit the cell source, save the notebook and read the actual file.

Expected: the document-metadata marker is reverted, the source edit is saved and output dimensions remain 20/21.

Actual: the marker and source behave correctly, but saving restores the old dimensions 10/11. The retained cell's output metadata was not updated during reload.

There are two omissions: the same-output-count shortcut selects item-only updates, which retain metadata, and the multi-output sequence comparison ignores metadata too. Comparing metadata in both decisions makes the public reload/save regression p

docs.title: Keep task problem markers scoped to each terminal
docs.body:
Fixes #346990

Concurrent background tasks currently share one problem-start marker. One terminal can therefore decorate from another terminal's marker or dispose it when its own watch cycle finishes without errors. Keep the marker in each terminal registration's existing disposable scope.

Two regressions exercise overlapping watch cycles through the real problem collector and in-memory xterm markers. Both fail before the fix and pass afterward. All 20 checks in the four nearby task suites, targeted ESLint and the core no-emit typecheck pass. Exact stable 1.145.2 task-status/collector sources reproduce the failures under the same test infrastructure.

docs.title: Release shared chat file entries on deletion
docs.body:
Fixes #346991

When two chat editing sessions share a created file, ordinary deletion leaves the borrowing session's reference unreleased. Undoing creation can instead release the creating session's reference twice, leaving the other session with a disposed entry.

On deletion, remove and release the entry only if the session still owns it. This releases borrowed references and respects undo's earlier release.

The two regressions assert both working sets, original-model disposal and watcher counts. Both fail before the fix and pass afterward. All 63 editing-service/checkpoint tests, targeted ESLint and the combined core no-emit typecheck pass. Stable 1.145.2 has the same affected implementation; validation uses synthetic local chat sessions rather than a live model endpoint.

docs.title: Use pending URLs when restoring browser tabs
docs.body:
Fixes #346992

Reusing an unresolved restored browser tab updates its pending URL, but native creation still uses the captured saved URL. Read the current pending URL when resolving the tab.

Reuse normal navigation's scheme normalization so bare destinations such as `localhost:3000/requested` continue to receive `http://`. The helper contains the existing normalization unchanged and serves both paths.

The registered-command regression fails before the fix. A second case preserves bare-localhost behavior. Both cases and all 58 tests across six nearby files pass, along with targeted ESLint and the combined core no-emit typecheck. Validation covers the native creation request; a full restart/Chromium UI run was not performed.

docs.title: Preserve notebook output metadata during reload
docs.body:
Fixes #346993

Reloading a retained notebook cell can discard changed output metadata and later save the stale values over the file. Select full-output edits when metadata differs, and compare canonically serialized metadata as part of a string sequence identity. LCS then checks the full metadata string when its fast hashes collide, preserving fractional numbers and distinct strings while ignoring metadata key order and regenerated output IDs.

One- and two-output working-copy regressions cover reload/save preservation. Public `.ipynb` Revert/Save tests independently change fractional widths and hash-colliding labels (`Aa` → `BB`), then verify the saved file after a subsequent source edit. They also verify that Revert removes an unsaved document-metadata marker, so a skipped reload cannot pass.

Validation: 74 nearby notebook/output checks, 39 `.ipynb` tests with one existing skip, extension compilation, targeted ESLint and the core no-emit typecheck. The original metadata-loss workflow reproduces in installed VS Code 1.145.2; the additional string-collision workflow fails on the previous PR head and passes with the full string comparison.

docs.title: Reconcile hidden lines after boundary insertions
docs.body:
Inserting a newline at the end of a hidden line can leave the new line hidden even after folding recomputes a range that excludes it. The inserted projection inherits hidden visibility, while the tracked decoration and both range caches can remain unchanged.

Invalidate the outer hidden-area cache after structural model changes and reconcile projections when an insertion inherited hidden visibility. The existing no-edit shortcuts remain.

Related to #136867. The verified reproduction uses a public workspace edit while the caret remains on the collapsed header:

```python
def foo():
    pass
print("end")
```

After folding the function, insert `"\n"` at zero-based position `(1, 8)` using `workspace.applyEdit`, without moving the caret or toggling folding. Stable 1.145.2 keeps only gutter lines `[1, 4]` visible; patched main correctly shows `[1, 3, 4]`. Both retain the collapsed body and save the same four-line text. This establishes the boundary-edit case; the original Insert Line Above command was not established as fixed.

Validation:

- The editor regression fails before the fix and passes afterward; 122 neighbouring tests pass.
- The same public-edit scenario fails its visibility assertions in installed 1.145.2 and passes in patched Code OSS, with independent document, caret and folding controls.
- Targeted ESLint, the client typecheck and final focused test pass.

docs.title: Revert reloads a stored file working copy when the file did not change on disk
docs.body:
Fixes #180193

## Problem

File: Revert File on a notebook clears the dirty state but leaves the edited cells on screen, unless the file changed on disk after it was opened. Notebooks resolve their files through `StoredFileWorkingCopyManager`, so this affects every notebook type.

`StoredFileWorkingCopy.revert()` calls `forceResolveFromFile()`, which calls the resolver that the manager gives the working copy with `{ forceReadFromFile: true }`. That resolver calls `this.resolve(resource, { ...options, reload: { async: false } })`. `doResolve()` takes `forceReadFromFile` from `options.reload.force` and ignores the top-level option, so the working copy is resolved without forcing a read. `resolveFromFile()` then sends the cached etag. For an unchanged file, the file service answers `FILE_NOT_MODIFIED_SINCE`, and the working copy keeps the edited model.

Text files are not affected: `TextFileEditorModel.forceResolveFromFile()` goes through the text file manager, which passes `forceReadFromFile: true` to the model unchanged.

## Change

The resolver now passes `forceReadFromFile` on as `reload.force`.

## Tests

Added `revert reloads contents when the file did not change on disk` to `storedFileWorkingCopyManager.test.ts`. The existing tests did not catch this, for two reasons. The `StoredFileWorkingCopy` tests use a resolver that calls `workingCopy.resolve(options)` directly, withou

docs.title: Associated untitled Save replaces binary destinations without confirmation
docs.body:
Saving an untitled editor associated with a file path can silently replace a binary file created at that path after the editor was opened.

Reproduction in an isolated normal VS Code window:

1. Open an associated untitled draft for a path that does not exist and enter some text.
2. Create a small binary file at that path externally.
3. Save the draft.

In installed **1.145.2**, the binary destination is overwritten without the expected Replace/Cancel confirmation. Save returns `true` and the untitled source is cleared/closed. A text destination created the same way correctly prompts.

Expected: ask before replacing the existing destination. Cancel should preserve its exact bytes and keep the source open and dirty.

The target resolver detects binary/too-large content, deletes it and retries before reaching the associated-untitled overwrite confirmation. On retry the target no longer exists, so the prompt is skipped. This combines the behaviours introduced for #67946 and #88687.

Normal-window comparisons with a 23-byte binary fixture verify the failure in Stable and the corrected Cancel, retry/Replace, text-target, missing-target and ordinary-Save behaviour in patched development. Too-large coverage uses bounded error injection rather than a huge-file experiment. Approved-replacement write failures remain a separate, pre-existing limitation.

docs.title: Selective Git stage-all commands stage unrelated files when their selection is empty
docs.body:
The built-in Git commands **Stage All Tracked Changes** and **Stage All Untracked Changes** can stage files outside the requested category when the eligible selection is empty.

In a disposable repository with one committed file:

1. Leave tracked files unchanged, create an untracked file and wait for Git status to refresh.
2. Run **Git: Stage All Tracked Changes**. The untracked file becomes staged, although there are no tracked changes to stage.
3. Reset that test index and remove the untracked file. Modify only the tracked file and wait for status.
4. Run **Git: Stage All Untracked Changes**. The tracked modification becomes staged, although there are no untracked changes.

Expected: both commands leave the index unchanged when their category is empty.

Both cases reproduce through the public commands in installed VS Code **1.145.2** on macOS arm64. Independent Git CLI status, cached diffs and index entries confirm the changes. Patched main leaves both indexes unchanged and retains eligible staging behaviour, including a partially staged control.

The filtered URI arrays reach `Repository.add([])`, whose intentional meaning is whole-repository staging (`git add -A -- .`). The command handlers need to avoid that call for an empty selection. Regression coverage includes `mixed`, `separate` and `hidden` untracked-file settings; the packaged-stable comparison used `mixed`.

Stage All Tracked Changes and Stage All Untracked Changes pass an empty filtered list to `Repository.add`, which stages the entire repository. Guard those two calls when their category has no files, preserving the low-level `add([])` contract used by ordinary stage-all operations.

Eight real-command regression/control cases cover mixed, separate and hidden untracked-file settings. Six fail before the fix. docs.title: TypeScript document symbols can stay stale after a document is closed and reopened
docs.body:
The TypeScript navigation-tree cache can return symbols from a closed document after the same URI is reopened with different content.

Reproduction:

1. Open a TypeScript file containing `export const original = 1;`.
2. Request its document symbols with `vscode.executeDocumentSymbolProvider`.
3. Close the document and wait for `workspace.onDidCloseTextDocument` / `isClosed`. Closing a tab alone does not necessarily dispose the document immediately.
4. Change the file externally to `export const updated = 2;`, then reopen it and request symbols again.

In installed VS Code **1.145.2**, the active editor's public document text is the updated declaration, but the returned symbol remains **`original`**. The reopened document is a different object at version 1. No delete/recreate is needed.

Expected: the provider returns `updated`.

The cache matches URI and version, which collide across document lifetimes. An independent public-API comparison using Stable's packaged built-in TypeScript extension reproduces this; patched main returns the correct symbol. Validation was on macOS arm64 and does not claim a visual Outline check.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

docs.title: Stopping port forwarding leaves concurrent tunnel connections open
docs.body:
**Stop Forwarding Port** can leave established connections active when more than one connection uses the built-in Node tunnel.

Related to microsoft/vscode-remote-release#2237. The older fix handles a single connection; this is the uncovered concurrent-connection case.

Reproduction through `TunnelService.openTunnel` / `closeTunnel`:

1. Open one forwarded port and establish two clients through it.
2. Complete the normal protocol handshake and exchange data on both clients.
3. Close the tunnel.

Expected: both established clients close. Actual: only the newest client closes. If the first client disconnects before the tunnel is closed, the remaining client stays open too. A one-client control passes.

`NodeRemoteTunnel` keys disposal callbacks by `localSocket.localAddress`, which is shared by connections accepted on the same listener. A later callback replaces the earlier one, and one connection's cleanup can remove another's entry.

A bounded fixture reproduces this on current main using only ephemeral loopback sockets and the real protocol handshake. It records client close events and `destroyed` state; no private connection method is called. The affected implementation is byte-identical in **1.145.2**. This does not claim packaged-stable UI execution, third-party tunnel-provider behaviour or pending-handshake disposal.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

- https://gith

docs.title: Track forwarded tunnel connections by socket
docs.body:
Fixes #347032

Related to microsoft/vscode-remote-release#2237.

Connections on the same tunnel listener share `localAddress`, so the disposal map retains only the most recent callback. Key it by socket identity and remove each socket's entry on close. Existing registration guards and graceful shutdown remain.

The regression fixture opens/closes the actual tunnel service, completes the real protocol handshake over ephemeral loopback sockets and exchanges data before teardown. A single-connection control passes on base; two concurrent connections and disconnecting one before stopping forwarding fail. All 31 selected checks pass after the fix.

Client compilation/typecheck and targeted lint, including explicit lint for the new fixture, pass. The 1.145.2 implementation is identical. Pending-handshake disposal and a packaged workbench/remote-host scenario are outside the validation claim.

docs.title: An older keybindings read can restore a previous profile's shortcuts
docs.body:
An older asynchronous `keybindings.json` read can overwrite a newer completed reload, including restoring a previous profile's bindings after a profile switch.

A deterministic workbench regression uses this sequence:

1. Profile A binds F8 to `workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility`; hold one read of A's keybindings pending.
2. Switch to profile B through `UserDataProfileService.updateCurrentProfile`. B binds F8 to `workbench.action.togglePanel`.
3. Complete B's read and dispatch F8: it correctly toggles the panel.
4. Complete A's older read and dispatch the same F8 event: it now toggles the sidebar, without another profile or configuration change.

Expected: both dispatches after switching use profile B's command.

The loader applies every completed read without checking whether a newer reload superseded it. An older failed read can similarly clear newer bindings, and an old success can restore bindings after a newer empty-array read.

Verified on main `cf2ba5544aee93ccde676d6290a42bcfe7d915b7` (1.147.0 development) with the real workbench resolver, normal profile/file notifications and controlled file-read completion in the test harness. The affected source is identical in **1.145.2**. Packaged-stable execution and reliable manual timing are not claimed.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

- https://github.com/sameerihs/vscode/blob/4be1228f4b9486a650238810578aed6af2

docs.title: Ignore superseded user keybinding reloads
docs.body:
Fixes #347034

An older user-keybindings read can finish after a newer reload and replace its bindings, even restoring a previous profile's commands. Track a reload generation and ignore superseded successes or failures before applying data or notifying consumers.

Four regressions cover profile switching, overlapping filesystem reloads, an obsolete missing-file result and a newer empty configuration. The workbench case dispatches F8 through the real resolver and demonstrates the command reverting to the old profile. A sequential-edit control remains green.

All four regressions fail before the fix. The focused checks, 117 neighbouring tests, targeted ESLint and client typecheck pass. Reproduction controls I/O completion; 1.145.2 applicability is established from identical source rather than a packaged-app timing claim.

docs.title: Refresh Quick Pick rows when selection mode changes
docs.body:
Fixes #209132

Changing `canSelectMany` on a visible Quick Pick updates the widget mode without rebuilding its rows, leaving selection behaviour in the previous mode. Refresh rows on actual mode changes while preserving active/checked state and suppressing intermediate list events.

Keep mode refreshes separate from item assignments so they preserve pending one-shot `itemActivation`. Explicit property confirmations remain distinct from mode-only restoration, and same-value assignments do not rebuild the list.

All 151 selected tests pass, including 31 focused mode/activation checks. Coverage includes filtered and reverse transitions, round trips, hidden/deferred item population, `NONE`/`SECOND`/`LAST` activation, one-shot reset, acceptance and unchanged-mode controls. Client builds, typechecking and targeted ESLint pass.

The missing multiple selection was also reproduced through the public API in installed 1.145.2. The current follow-up is validated by the widget/service tests above.

docs.title: build: hold gated artifacts until their tests have run
docs.body:
Publish released artifacts before the tests that gate them had run.

**Cost (last 30 days of def 111, 770 publishing builds):** 126 builds published 230 gated artifacts with `Job <name> is not part of this run` while that platform's tests were part of the run. In 30 of those builds, a gating test then failed, and in 28 its gate never passed. That includes 8 scheduled insiders (for example 490339, 491462, 492813, 493876) and the releasing insider 493858. 224 of the 230 artifacts are the Linux x64 and macOS arm64 CLIs, whose CLI jobs finish long before the tests. The other 6 are 494123's Linux x64 artifacts, which were published after a Linux stage retry, 10 minutes before the retried tests passed.

**Mitigation until now:** the automatic `Release build` step only runs when Publish succeeds, and Publish fails when any stage fails. So none of these were released automatically. The exposure was a release owner releasing a partially published build, which then included an artifact whose platform tests had failed. The Windows x64 CLI was never affected, since it comes from the Sign job, which starts after the test jobs exist.

**Cause:** `getGatingJob` only looked at `Job` records. A job only gets a `Job` record once it's scheduled, so a test job that still waits for its compile job, or one that a stage retry reset, looked the same as a job that isn't part of the run (`missing`

### References stay in the References pill

- Three ExP scorecard links recorded as references collapsed into one stray `ExP 13d3ffbb` pill next to the `4 Experiments` group.

docs.title: Fix #346870: Copilot Agent Host: steering waits for notification-started turns to finish
docs.body:
Fixes #346870

### Description

When a background subagent finishes, its completion notification creates a fresh parent turn in `CopilotAgentSession` via `_handleSystemNotification`.

Previously, notification-created turns left `sdkSendInvoked` as `false`. Consequently:
1. `CopilotAgentSession.hasRunningTurn` (which requires `this._hasSentTurn && this.currentTurn?.sdkSendInvoked === true && this._isExecuting`) evaluated to `false`.
2. When steering arrived while the parent agent was executing following a subagent completion notification, `CopilotAgent.sendSteeringMessage` rejected immediate delivery because `hasRunningTurn` was `false`.
3. The steering message remained queued in the host, delaying consumption until the turn completed.

This PR sets `turn.sdkSendInvoked = true` when creating turns from turn-starting system notifications, and also marks `turn.sdkSendInvoked = true` upon receiving `user.message` events in `_handleUserMessage`. This preserves SDK-dispatch readiness so steering messages can enter the running conversation immediately.

### Verification

- Added unit test in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`:
  - `delivers steering during a notification-started turn after background agent completes`
- Added unit tests in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts`:

docs.title: build: fall back to the npm registry for electron.d.ts
docs.body:
`Prepare Electron types` and the `pnpm install` postinstall download `electron.d.ts` from the Electron GitHub release. During GitHub incidents that download fails, and in the last 48 h it failed **9 Code OSS PR CI jobs** on unrelated PRs (7 `Compile & Hygiene` first attempts plus 2 `Install dependencies` attempts on #346817). Every one passed on a later retry.

## What failed

- Two incident windows: Nov 8 08:50–12:05 UTC and Nov 9 05:25–08:10 UTC.
- 7 hits got `HTTP 504` on all 3 attempts (step took about 13 s). The other 2 got `TimeoutError` on all 3 attempts of 30 s each (about 92 s).
- `download()` makes 3 attempts with a fixed 1 s delay, so it rides out only a couple of seconds of trouble. A longer backoff wouldn't help much against an outage that lasts hours.

## The change

If the GitHub download fails, `electron.d.ts` is extracted from the `electron` npm package instead, fetched with `npm pack electron@<version>` from the repository root. That's a different source, and `pnpm install` already depends on it. Going through `npm` means it uses the registry, credentials and CA settings the checkout and user `.npmrc` configure. The fallback is held to the same pinned checksum from `build/checksums/electron.txt`, so it can only produce the exact file we expect. I checked that `package/electron.d.ts` in `electron-43.8.6.tgz` is byte-identical to the release asset (`fd8aeab…488a

docs.title: Resetting NotebookController.supportedLanguages to undefined leaves execution restricted
docs.body:
`NotebookController.supportedLanguages` documents both `undefined` and `[]` as supporting all languages. Resetting a previously restricted controller to `undefined` leaves the old restriction on the main thread, and excluded cells still do not execute.

Steps:

1. Create/select a synthetic notebook controller with `supportedLanguages = ['javascript']`.
2. Open a notebook with a TypeScript cell. Executing it correctly produces no output while restricted.
3. Set `controller.supportedLanguages = undefined`.
4. Select the same controller and execute the cell again.

Expected: the execution handler runs and supplies the output/success state. Actual: the handler remains filtered out; output is empty and execution success is undefined. Repeating the same workflow with `supportedLanguages = []` works.

The reset is sent as an undefined DTO property, which JSON transport omits. The main thread interprets the absent value as no update.

The public regression uses the API suite's synthetic controller to copy cell source to output; it runs no real kernel or external provider. The `undefined` case fails and the `[]` control passes in both the development build and installed **VS Code 1.145.2** (`c4453f8ea430`), on macOS arm64.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

- https://github.com/sameerihs/vscode/blob/9f9afff1fabafc40fdbe089931408ba215b239b5/src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/extHo

The real JSON API-bridge regression and public notebook execution regression fail before the fix; explicit-empty-array controls pass. The public regression also reproduces in installed 1.145.2.
