docs.title: RelativePattern file watchers receive events from another scheme or authority
docs.body:
A watcher created with a URI-based `RelativePattern` can receive events from another URI scheme or authority when the filesystem paths match.

Reproduction:

1. Register filesystem providers and expose resources with the same path under distinct schemes, for example `left:/root/file.txt` and `right:/root/file.txt`.
2. Create a watcher using `new vscode.RelativePattern(vscode.Uri.parse('left:/root'), '**/*')`.
3. Emit create/change/delete events for `right:/root/file.txt`.

Expected: no event reaches the watcher rooted in `left:/root`. Actual: those events reach it. The same problem occurs with distinct authorities under one non-file scheme, such as `demo://one/root/file.txt` and `demo://two/root/file.txt`.

Relative event matching uses `uri.fsPath`, which loses the scheme and, for these non-file URIs, the authority. The public regression uses registered providers and registration barriers, checks actual watcher events and includes ignore/disposal controls. Unit controls cover path and authority casing and ordinary string-pattern workspace behaviour.

Reproduced through the public API on 1.147.0 development sources at `cf2ba5544aee`, macOS arm64. The affected 1.145.2 source is identical; packaged stable and other platforms were not run.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

- https://github.com/sameerihs/vscode/blob/98914d2b01c43e7cfb8636602b7c23e6809a6355/src/vs/workbench/

docs.title: Scope relative watchers to URI namespaces
docs.body:
Fixes #347069

Check a relative watcher's base URI scheme and authority before applying its path glob. Retain existing path-casing, string-pattern workspace, ignore-event and disposal behaviour.

The unit and registered-provider API regressions fail before the fix. All 124 selected unit tests and 16 API tests pass afterward; three watcher API cases also pass on repeat. Client typechecking, API extension compilation and targeted ESLint pass. Pending-watch cancellation/disposal work in #343811 concerns a separate path.

docs.title: Terminal.processId never resolves when a Pseudoterminal closes synchronously in open
Resolve terminal readiness before PTY callbacks
docs.body:
Fixes #347071

Fire synthetic-terminal readiness before entering extension callbacks. A synchronous close in `Pseudoterminal.open` can then remove listeners without leaving the public process-ID promise unresolved.

The production service-chain regression fails before the ordering change; its deferred-close control passes. Both pass afterward while preserving output, exit status and cleanup. All 80 selected tests and the GC-dependent disposal check pass, along with client typechecking and targeted ESLint.

docs.title: Save and Retry writes to the new profile after switching profiles
docs.body:
A pending **Save and Retry** action can write to a different profile after the current profile changes.

Sequence:

1. In profile A, leave a valid settings file with unsaved edits.
2. Trigger a user-configuration update that offers **Save and Retry** for that dirty file.
3. Switch to profile B before invoking the action. B can also have its own unrelated unsaved draft.
4. Invoke the original notification's **Save and Retry** action.

Expected: retry the original edit against A's original file/JSON path. Actual: the callback reconstructs the operation using the current profile, writes the requested value into B and can save B's unrelated draft. A does not receive the requested edit.

The same target drift occurs for standalone user configuration files. This is a sequential reproduction; it does not require overlapping I/O or a timing race.

Regression tests execute the actual configuration editing service with memory-backed profile files, cover both settings and standalone writes, and retain a no-switch control. Both regressions fail against development source `cf2ba5544aee` (1.147.0, macOS arm64). The affected 1.145.2 source is identical. No actual global settings or packaged-stable UI were used.

Regression coverage in the prepared fix:

- https://github.com/sameerihs/vscode/blob/ef4d76cede1e954e26ff909bbd204cdc98881cab/src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/test/browser/conf

docs.title: Keep configuration retries on their original file
docs.body:
Fixes #347073

Queue configuration retries with the original operation so switching profiles cannot retarget Save and Retry to another file or JSON path. Reuse the existing write/error handling and fresh validation for settings and standalone configuration.

Two sequential regressions fail before the fix; both and the no-switch control pass afterward. All 243 selected tests pass with seven existing pending tests. Client typechecking and targeted ESLint pass. Tests use memory-backed profiles and await model cleanup.

docs.title: Multi-cursor snippet transforms leave stale selections and typing overwrites transformed text
Track snippet selections after all transforms
docs.body:
Fixes #347075

Complete all snippet moves/transforms before reading final placeholder selections from tracked ranges. This preserves primary-cursor order while avoiding selections captured before another snippet edits an earlier document position.

Five focused cases cover both cursor orders, LF/CRLF multiline transforms and undo/redo; four fail before the fix. All 180 snippet tests pass with one existing pending test. Client typechecking and targeted ESLint pass. This addresses the command/completion insertion path.

docs.title: Per-conflict merge resets combine with earlier edits in the undo stack
docs.body:
Per-conflict reset/remove operations do not consistently have their own undo boundary. Resetting to base can combine its removal with preceding typing, and two consecutive Remove actions can become one undo step.

The action sequence for the second case is:

1. Open a merge with two conflicts and accept a resolution for each.
2. Remove the accepted resolution from the first conflict.
3. Remove the accepted resolution from the second conflict.
4. Undo once.

Expected: restore the second resolution while the first remains removed. Actual: the two removals can be undone together. In the preceding-typing case, the manually typed resolution can become unavailable as a separate undo/redo state.

`setState` removes the old result diff before its existing leading undo stop and skips both stops when the replacement is the base state. The real conflict actions call this path; their inline-link handlers do not add the missing boundary.

Eight action/undo tests use the actual merge model and shared undo services, covering both diff algorithms and handled-state controls. Four regressions fail on unchanged development source `cf2ba5544aee` (1.147.0, macOS arm64). Relevant production blobs are identical in 1.145.2. This is model/action-path validation, not a packaged-stable UI recording.

Historical context: #158864 and #166606. This finding concerns per-conflict actions rather than resetting

docs.title: Keep merge conflict undo steps separate
docs.body:
Fixes #347077

Move the existing undo stops around the complete conflict-state change, including old-diff removal and return to base. Reset/remove then remains separate from preceding typing and neighbouring conflict actions.

Four regressions fail before the fix; all eight action/undo cases pass afterward with legacy and advanced diff algorithms. The complete 28-test merge-editor suite and six neighbouring undo tests pass, as do client typechecking and targeted ESLint. The test fixture shares the undo services used by the models and guarantees disposal.

docs.title: Git API migration consumes an unrelated stash when all source changes are excluded
docs.body:
The public Git extension API can consume an unrelated stash when the source worktree contains only untracked files excluded by the migration options.

Safe reproduction using a temporary repository and linked worktree:

1. Commit `tracked.txt`.
2. Make a staged change to it and create an unrelated stash.
3. Leave only an untracked `untracked.txt` in the source worktree.
4. Open both repositories through `vscode.git`'s `getAPI(1)` and await their `status()` calls.
5. Call `target.migrateChanges(source.rootUri.fsPath, { deleteFromSource: false })`, omitting `untracked`.

Expected: no changes are eligible, so both worktrees and the stash remain unchanged.

Actual: the existing stash is applied to the target, restored into the source index and removed from the shared stash stack. With `deleteFromSource: true`, it is applied to the target and removed. Without an existing stash, the same input throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'index')`. Both mixed and separate untracked-file presentation reproduce it.

The preflight counts untracked resources even when the subsequent stash excludes them. Git succeeds without creating a new stash; migration then treats the existing top stash as the newly created one.

This is an API case. The normal migration UI explicitly passes `untracked: true`. Real-Git API regressions cover copy/move, both resource presentations, no prior stas

docs.title: Skip Git migrations without eligible changes
docs.body:
Fixes #347079

Filter migration resources according to the untracked option before the empty/conflict preflight. When only excluded untracked files remain, return without creating or consuming a stash.

Five real-Git API regressions fail before the fix; three eligible-change controls pass. All 20 selected tests pass afterward with two existing skips, and Git extension compilation and targeted ESLint pass. Unchanged fixtures also emit handled deferred-refresh ENOENT warnings during teardown; the final runs have no unhandled rejection or timeout.

This addresses the public API's excluded-untracked case. The standard migration UI already includes untracked files.

docs.title: Block failed background task prerequisites
docs.body:
Related to #70283

A background prerequisite that fails or is terminated before readiness can still release its dependent command: terminal shutdown emits balancing `Inactive` events, and the dependency waiter treats them as success. Preserve the earlier `ProcessEnded` outcome before that synthetic inactivity can settle the waiter.

Two public `tasks.executeTask` regressions fail on unchanged main while three controls pass. The fixed API selection passes all seven cases, including two existing dependency controls; task unit suites pass 105 tests with five existing pending tests. Client typechecking, API extension compilation and targeted ESLint pass. Processes and files are bounded test fixtures.

This addresses exit-before-readiness handling, a subset of #70283 rather than general watcher-diagnostic error gating. It overlaps the waiter touched by #345960 but is complementary to that PR's completion-cache and subscription cleanup. Its full production composition has not been executed; any rebase combining the changes should retain that cleanup and rerun the dependency tests.

Fixes #347089

The sparkle split button of the agent status widget showed focus outlines after plain mouse interaction (ring around the chevron while the menu is open, ring around the whole button after it closes). See the issue for the full analysis.

Changes in `agenttitlebarstatuswidget.css`:

docs.title: build: retry the Agent SDK npm ci when the native package is skipped
docs.body:
`Agent SDK: build + upload` fails now and then because `npm ci` silently skips the SDK's native binary package. The existing guard in `package.ts` catches it, but nothing retries, so one bad download fails the whole test job. That job gates publishing in official builds. Main CI had 5 hits in 30 days:

| Build | SDK and target | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 494272 | codex, win32-x64 | native package skipped (`added 1 package` instead of 2) |
| 491629 | (`npm ci` itself) | `npm error code ETIMEDOUT`, `npm ci exited 196` |
| 491050 | codex, darwin-arm64 | native package skipped |
| 485953 | claude-agent-sdk, darwin-arm64 | native package skipped |
| 484481 | claude-agent-sdk, linux-x64 | native package skipped |

The hits span two SDKs, three platforms and both agent pools. In each case the same tarball built fine in other jobs at the same commit.

## Why

The native binary is an optional dependency (for example `@openai/codex-win32-x64`), and it's the large download. npm doesn't fail when an optional dependency can't be fetched. It just leaves it out without a warning.

## The change

- `buildOne` now runs `npm ci` and the native-package check through `installWithRetry`: up to **3 attempts, waiting 10 s and then 30 s**, and deleting `node_modules` between attempts.
- It retries only when the native package is missing or `npm ci` exits non-zero. Other errors, such as `npm` failing t

docs.body:

Copying a running notebook cell shares its mutable output-item array. Later stream appends can therefore change the saved output of the unexecuted copy. Give each cloned output its own array while retaining the existing item buffers.

Two model/command regressions and a public API regression cover appending and saving. The API test uses a synthetic controller, Copy Cell Down and the existing serializer, then checks the written bytes. It fails on unchanged main and packaged stable 1.145.2 and passes with the fix.

Validation on macOS: 111 neighbouring unit tests pass with five existing pending cases; all 11 Notebook Kernel API tests pass. Client/API compilation, client typechecking and changed-file lint pass.

docs.body:

Concurrent group closures can each see another owner of the same dirty editor and skip confirmation. Await group closures in sequence so the final owner receives the save/discard/cancel prompt.

The regression exercises the shared-input case through the bulk-close actions, including cancellation. Focused and neighbouring editor tests, client compilation, client typechecking and changed-file lint pass.

docs.title: Fix webview messages with many buffers
docs.body:
Related to #137757

Extension-to-webview messages spread their binary buffers into RPC arguments. At 254 distinct buffers, the one-byte argument count overflows; messages can fail or arrive with corrupted binary data. Send the buffer array in `SerializableObjectWithBuffers` and unwrap it at the receiver.

This completes the opposite direction from the historical fix. Tests cover the argument-count boundary, offsets, shared backing buffers, empty buffers and legacy serialization.

Native extension/page echo checks reproduce the failure in installed 1.145.2 and verify the fixed transport, including 253–257 and 1,024-buffer cases. Focused tests, client compilation/typechecking and changed-file lint pass on macOS.

docs.title: Preserve chat history during session disposal
docs.body:
Related to #321290

Queued saves can outlive the chat model they serialize and overwrite saved history with cleared data. This change protects two related disposal orderings:

- Exclude models pending disposal from additional asynchronous autosaves, while preserving the synchronous session-index update.
- Give each final-reference disposal attempt its own identity. If a model is released, reacquired and released again before the first save finishes, the first completion must not dispose the model or clear the later attempt's pending state. The current attempt keeps the model alive until its save settles.

Reacquiring a reference still cancels pending disposal and makes the model eligible for autosave. Save failures retain the existing log-and-dispose policy.

### Validation

The release/reacquire/release regression uses the real `ChatService`, `ChatSessionStore` and `FileService` over an in-memory filesystem, with a history refresh queued between the disposal saves. On the previous PR head, both JSONL and flat storage restore an empty transcript and empty history. Both pass with the ownership fix.

The focused run passes 14 cases, including the original six autosave/storage-backend controls, reference reacquisition, synchronous index persistence and overlapping disposal success/failure cases. All 585 tests across the five neighbouring chat suites pass. Fresh client output, clie

docs.title: Cancelled custom-editor backup completion deletes the newer recovery backup
docs.body:
## Description

A custom editor provider may finish an older backup after VS Code cancels it. If a newer backup has already completed, the extension host currently calls `delete()` on that newer backup when the older operation returns. Stored recovery metadata still refers to the newer, now-deleted backup.

The `backupCustomDocument` API permits a provider to finish work after cancellation, so this is reachable with a supported asynchronous provider.

## Reproduction

Use an editable custom editor provider that returns distinct backup IDs and whose `CustomDocumentBackup.delete()` removes the corresponding backup:

1. Open a custom document and fire its normal `onDidChangeCustomDocument` event.
2. Wait for backup A to start, then leave its provider promise pending.
3. Make another edit and fire another change event for the same document.
4. VS Code cancels A and starts B. Complete B and wait for its recovery metadata to be stored.
5. Complete A without rejecting cancellation.

**Expected:** the backup referenced by current recovery metadata remains available. A's unused result must not replace or delete B.

**Actual:** B's deletion callback runs, A becomes the retained backup and the stored recovery ID still names B. Recovery through that ID can no longer find the latest backup.

## Evidence

Reproduced against source commit `bc922197bf3432ed7ab3d21a8d3cd8fbbc3c79f8` on macOS ar

docs.title: Disk file provider reports success after a partial native write
docs.body:
An unbuffered write through the IPC-backed disk filesystem provider can resolve successfully even when the operating system writes only part of the input. The returned file stat reports the smaller size, but the operation does not reject.

## Reproduction

I reproduced this on macOS with Node 24.22.1 against source commit `bc922197bf3432ed7ab3d21a8d3cd8fbbc3c79f8`, using only a temporary regular file and an asynchronous serialized loopback channel:

1. Run a throwaway child process with a 1,024-byte `RLIMIT_FSIZE`. Ignore `SIGXFSZ` in that child so an attempted write beyond the limit reports `EFBIG` instead of terminating the process. Leave the parent process limits unchanged.
2. Register the production IPC-backed disk provider with `FileService`, using a `vscode-remote://loopback/...` URI mapped to the temporary file.
3. Call `await fileService.writeFile(resource, VSBuffer.wrap(Buffer.alloc(2048, 65)))`.
4. Inspect the returned stat and the file contents.

**Expected:** Either all 2,048 bytes are written, or the operation fails. It must not acknowledge a partial file as a successful write.

**Actual:** The promise resolves, the returned stat has `size: 1024` and the file contains only the first 1,024 bytes. Without the child file-size limit, the same call writes all 2,048 bytes.

The OS write is real, not mocked. This is a service/IPC reproduction, not a claim that an SSH sess

docs.title: Complete partial writes in the disk provider
docs.body:
Fixes #347125

The disk provider discards the byte count from a native write and can acknowledge success after writing only part of the buffer. Advance the file and buffer offsets until all bytes are written or an error is raised.

Four regression cases cover ordinary, append and atomic writes, failure propagation and lock recovery. They fail before the fix and pass afterward. The neighbouring unit selection passes 65 tests with two platform skips, and 117 relevant disk integration tests pass. Client compilation/typechecking and changed-file lint pass.

A bounded native macOS reproduction limits a child process to a 1,024-byte file: a 2,048-byte request changes from false success to `EFBIG`, while an unlimited control succeeds. Errors can still leave a partial file after a non-atomic write. Stable source parity was checked; packaged stable and live SSH were not run.

docs.title: Global and scoped terminal environment mutations replace each other
Combine global and scoped terminal mutations
docs.body:
Fixes #347127

When one extension modifies the same variable globally and for a workspace, the merged collection drops one contribution. Retain both scopes, apply globals before workspace contributions and distinguish their identities when diffing collections.

Shell integration must preserve that composition too. Omit deferred operations superseded by a later shell-enabled replacement, keep process-only replacements separate and reconstruct PATH prefixes in their effective process-creation order.

Regression tests cover both registration orders, replacements and additive operations, deferred replay, mixed application stages and PATH replay. The original and newly exposed cases fail before their fixes and pass afterward.

Validation on macOS: 165 unit tests pass with 11 conditional/platform skips; seven native terminal API tests pass. The unmodified Bash replay probe, client/API compilation, full client typecheck and five-file lint pass. Both original production files match stable 1.145.2; packaged stable and native fish were not executed.

docs.body:
Fixes #236999

Follow-up to #346305. Verification found that the minimap still halves with the **default** `editor.minimap.scale` at `window.zoomLevel: -0.0000002` on a Retina screen.

## Problem

#346305 made the minimap scale for a pixel ratio below 2 equal to `max(scale, floor(scale * pixelRatio))`. With scale 3 this reduced the drop at DPR 1.9999998 from 6 to 5. But with scale 1 it still gives `floor(1.9999998) = 1` instead of 2, so the minimap halves (120px → 60px). Scale 1 is the default, so most users still see the bug.

## Change

`_computeMinimapScale` now adds a small tolerance (`+ 0.125`) before the `floor`. A pixel ratio a little below a whole step stays at that step, so DPR 1.96 or 1.9999998 renders like DPR 2. The scale still has to be an integer for the character renderer, so it still steps at some pixel ratio. The steps now sit about 6% below the whole values instead of exactly at them, so a tiny zoom change no longer crosses one. At pixel ratios of 1 and 2 and above, nothing changes.

| pixel ratio | 1 | 1.25 | 1.5 | 1.75 | 1.96 | 1.9999998 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scale 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | **2** (was 1) | **2** (was 1) | 2 |
| scale 2 | 2 | 2 (was 3) | 3 | 3 | **4** (was 3) | **4** (was 3) | 4 |
| scale 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 5 | **6** (was 5) | **6** (was 5) | 6 |

docs.title: test: skip the floating connected footer stroke test in WebKit
docs.body:
`ModernUIContribution › floating connected footers paint through the strip to the rounded card perimeter`, added in #347040, fails in WebKit on all 12 of its cases (`strokeVisible: false`, `true` expected). It failed deterministically in main CI 494297 and 494318. Only the macOS arm64 `Unit Tests (Node.js, Browser & Copilot)` job runs WebKit, and that job gates the macOS arm64 and universal builds, so the 23:00 UTC insider would lose them.

This skips only that test when `isSafari`, with a TODO for the author. Chromium still runs it.

## Why WebKit differs

To let the connected footer's stroke paint in the floating card's 1 px border, `connectedPaneTabs.css` gives the card `overflow: clip; overflow-clip-margin: border-box`. WebKit doesn't support `overflow-clip-margin` (`CSS.supports('overflow-clip-margin', 'border-box')` is `false` there), so it clips at the padding edge and hides the stroke in the border. This affects Safari on the web only. Desktop runs on Electron (Chromium).

A `clip-path: inset(0 round <radius>)` fallback paints the stroke in both engines, but the card's corner radii vary by layout, so that fix is left to the author. The TODO points at it.

## Validation

- Local Playwright WebKit on main: 110 passing, 1 failing, with the same assertion as CI. With this change: 110 passing, 1 pending.
- Chromium: 111 passing.
- eslint clean.

CI and the pre-commit hook now lint with [oxlint](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter.html) instead of ESLint: oxlint runs the rules of `eslint.config.js`, reports the same problems, and lints the full repository about five times faster. `eslint.config.js` stays the configuration, and ESLint stays for the editor and the Copilot extension's lint; `pnpm run eslint` is removed. - `eslint-js/*` and `ts-eslint-js/*`: ESLint's and typescript-eslint's own implementations of the rules that oxlint lacks (`no-restricted-syntax`, `no-buffer-constructor`, `naming-convention`, `no-restricted-imports`), loaded through adapters in `.eslint-plugin-local/adapters/`. docs.title: sessions: wait for startup providers before resolving a handed-off folder
docs.body:
Fixes #346833

## What changed

When the Agents window opens from an editor window with a local folder, `AgentsWindowWorkspaceHandoff` polls `ISessionsManagementService.resolveWorkspace` and accepts the first provider that resolves the folder. The Cloud provider (`default-copilot`) accepts local `file:` folders and registers shortly before the local agent-host provider (both are `AfterRestored` contributions, Cloud first in import order). If the handoff resolves inside that gap, `selectWorkspace` → `_reconcileWorkspaceEnvironment` pins the composer to **Cloud**, overriding the default that would pick **This Computer** for a local folder, and the handoff never revisits it.

The handoff now waits, before resolving a folder, until the contributions instantiated after restore have been created (`IWorkbenchContributionsRegistry.whenRestored`), which is when the startup session providers have registered. This applies to every folder handoff path (Open Agents Window, the title-bar button, and draft handoffs).

## Why this is safe

- No change to provider logic, environment defaults, or the composer.
- `whenRestored` always settles; the existing cancellation and 15 second timeout still apply, and the wait is skipped once it has settled.
- The added delay is short: in local testing the folder applied ~130 ms after the local provider registered.

## Problem

docs.title: agentHost: allow uninstalling MCP servers mirrored from the upstream registry
docs.body:
Fixes #346415

## Problem

Uninstalling an MCP server that GitHub's MCP service mirrors from the upstream MCP registry (for example Figma MCP Server, `urn:air:registry.modelcontextprotocol.io:com.figma.mcp:mcp`) failed with "The customization removal did not complete."

When VS Code confirms an owned MCP uninstall, `prepareUninstall` required the confirmation's `provenance.authority` to equal the host taken from the registry ID. For mirrored servers these differ: the registry host is `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io`, but the server is served by `api.mcp.github.com`. The check failed, the confirmation handler answered `cancel`, and `assertApplied` reported a generic error with no cause.

## Changes

- **Uninstall confirmation:** removed the registry-host comparison and the now-unused `isMatchingInstallationAuthority`. The authority now only has to be a non-empty string. `McpUninstallPlan` and `McpInstallationSummary` don't include provenance, so there's no reliable value to compare it against. The confirmation is still tied to the exact installation by its installation ID, identity, config key, user scope, media type, expiry, owned-secret count and restore/shared-auth flags. Install is unchanged; it already compares against the provenance in the runtime's plan.
- **Diagnostics:** when an install or removal ends with an unexpected outcome, the error now includes the SDK outcome

docs.title: ci: run the Linux Electron smoke tests in four shards with measured suite durations
docs.body:
Runs the Linux Electron smoke tests in Code OSS PR CI in **four** shards instead of three, and rebalances them from measured suite durations. This follows lszomoru's suggestion. Windows and macOS are unchanged.

## Why

Over 30 clean first-attempt PR runs from Nov 8–9, the three Linux shards' jobs took 4.98, **5.53** and 4.99 min (p50). Their test time was 207.5, 246.5 and 222.5 s, plus about 85 s of setup per job. The balancer in `test/smoke/src/shard.ts` used estimates that no longer match:
- `Data Loss (insiders -> insiders)` was 100 s and takes 105 s at p50 (one run was 134 s). `Agents Window (SSH Dev Container AgentHost)` was 50 s and takes 58 s.
- `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` has runnable tests, so it counted as 20 s, but in PR CI it skips itself without a stable build and takes 0 s.
- Unlisted suites counted as 20 s, while the unlisted Linux suites take 8–12 s.

## Change

- `shard.ts`: Linux gets its own duration table, built from the p50 of each suite over those 30 runs (rounded to 5 s, with `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` at 0), and a 10 s default. Windows and macOS keep the previous table and the 20 s default, so their shards are assigned exactly as before.
- `pr-linux-test.yml`: adds `electron-smoke-4` and sets all four Linux jobs to `SMOKE_SHARD_TOTAL: '4'`, named `Electron-Smoke (shard N/4)`. Windows stays at three shards in `pr-win32-test.yml`, w

docs.title: Engineering - switch GitHub Actions to the pnpm store cache
docs.body:
This is part of the pnpm migration. Like #346965 did for Azure Pipelines, the GitHub Actions jobs stop caching `node_modules` archives: they restore a pnpm store from the cache and always run `pnpm install`, which then only downloads the packages that the store doesn't have.

A cached `node_modules` folder only works with the layout of the linker that created it. With pnpm's isolated layout (#347200), its packages are links, which are junctions with absolute targets on Windows: the 7-Zip archives of the Windows jobs would store a copy of each target, or a path that breaks when the archive is extracted in another folder. The pnpm store has no such links once its `projects` links are removed.

## Changes

- **`.github/actions/restore-pnpm-store` (new):**
  - Computes the key with `build/azure-pipelines/common/computePnpmStoreCacheKey.ts`, the same script as Azure Pipelines. The key covers the platform, pnpm version, cache salt and the lockfiles of every install root, behind a prefix that names the install roots the job installs.
  - Points pnpm at a store beside the workspace (`../.pnpm-store`), where the workspace images keep it. That's on the workspace's volume, so pnpm can hard link from it, including the Dev Drive of the Windows jobs. pnpm's metadata cache sits inside the store.

docs.title: build: run the flaky smoke tests once a day at 06:00 UTC
docs.body:
The Flaky Tests pipeline (def 700) ran at 03:00 and 16:00 UTC. Each run takes about 5 hours, so it held about 3 of the 20 shared macOS agents during the 05:00 and 17:00 UTC insiders. This moves it to once a day at 06:00 UTC, which keeps it off both release slots and saves about 3 macOS agents for 5 hours a day. The Monday stable run moves to 06:00 too, with its branch and `always` settings unchanged. Its display name is what switches the run to stable quality, so the matching string in `VSCODE_QUALITY` changes with it.

**Overlap with the 05:00 UTC insider** (last 10 weekday 05:00 insiders):
- The insider's own macOS build, sign and test jobs got agents by 05:44 in 9 of 10 builds. The exception was Oct 27 (489688), where the last two started at 06:25.
- The 2 macOS sanity test jobs run after Publish and started after 06:00 in all 9 builds that ran them, and after 06:30 in 7. So 06:30 wouldn't avoid them either. They need 2 agents, and the Flaky Tests run takes about 3 of 20, so the two fit side by side.
- 06:00 also finishes about 11:00, before the 11:00 UTC insider's macOS jobs get going. A later start would overlap it more.

Validation: the ADO pipeline preview of def 700 on this branch compiles, with `cron: "0 6 * * *"` and `"0 6 * * 1"`, and the stable switch matches the new Monday display name.

docs.title: Connector suggestions do not account for existing MCP servers
docs.body:
## Problem

Connector suggestions can show a tip for an integration that the user already has through an existing MCP server. The suggestions are not aware of existing MCPs, resulting in redundant recommendations and confusion about whether additional setup is needed.

## Reproduction scenario

1. Have an existing MCP server configured for a service that is also available as a connector.
2. Encounter a connector suggestion for that same service.
3. The suggestion recommends the connector without acknowledging the existing MCP integration.

## Expected behavior

Account for existing MCP servers when generating connector suggestions and deduplicate equivalent integrations. If the intent is to move users from an existing MCP to a connector, present that as an explicit migration path rather than suggesting that the integration is missing.

## Context

This also needs to fit the migration story for users who already have the corresponding MCPs configured.

Versions, platform, and logs were not provided in the report.

docs.title: Engineering - fix saving the pnpm store cache in GitHub Actions
docs.body:
Follow-up to #347205.

## Problem

The `Code OSS (pnpm store)` workflow never creates the pnpm store caches. This affects Linux and every other store. The `Save pnpm store cache` step of `save-pnpm-store` passes `path: ../.pnpm-store` to `actions/cache/save`, which rejects paths with `..` segments. The action only logs a warning and saves nothing, so the step still succeeds:

```
[warning]Invalid pattern '../.pnpm-store'. Relative pathing '.' and '..' is not allowed.
```

`actions/cache/restore` doesn't validate paths in the same way, so it only reports `Cache not found`. As a result, `Detect Missing Caches` reports `pnpm-store-linux`, `pnpm-store-windows`, `pnpm-store-copilot-linux`, and `pnpm-store-copilot-windows` as missing on every push. The `Compile`, `Windows`, `Copilot (Linux)`, and `Copilot (Windows)` jobs then run each time (for example, [run 42719442065](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/42719442065)). `component-fixtures.yml` and `css-order-scan.yml` also use `save-pnpm-store`, so their stores are never saved either.

## Fix

The store stays beside the workspace, where the jobs and the workspace images keep it. Only the cache operations go through `.build/pnpm-store`:

- `restore-pnpm-store` restores the cache to `.build/pnpm-store`, then moves it to `pnpm_config_store_dir`. The move is a rename on the same volume.
- `save-pnpm-store` moves the pruned

docs.title: chat: keep model picker selection motion consistent
docs.body:
Fixes #347188

Changing a model's effort, context, or speed in the model picker details sometimes slid the selection and sometimes snapped it, depending on the setting and direction. Saving a choice refreshes the details card, and that refresh rebuilt the segmented controls while the selection was still moving.

The card now waits for the selection to settle before it rebuilds, and combines any refreshes that arrive in the meantime. Values still apply right away. With reduced motion on there is no slide, so nothing waits. While a choice is still saving, the card keeps showing it, so a refresh can't put back an older value. If the settings or their choices change, for example a model with different effort levels, the card rebuilds right away instead of waiting.

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b027714-bcc0-49bc-a965-8930f353da57

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/349da338-9e27-4039-8512-6e4d33360e58

Both clips show GPT-6.1 Sol in the Agents window, changing effort, context, and speed in both directions.

### How to test

1. Open the model picker and open the details for a model with effort, context, and speed options, such as GPT-6.1 Sol.

When a window has a non-git folder open (for example the user home folder), Copilot's content exclusion check starts `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for each file it checks. Every call fails with `not a git repository`. In a large folder, this means **35–100 git processes per second**, kept up for minutes. CPU hits ~100% and the fan spins up. Windows Defender makes it worse by scanning every short-lived `git.exe`.

docs.title: agentHost: recover remote connections across sleep
docs.body:
Remote GitHub environment recovery can start while a laptop is suspended. If fetching an identity token fails, the client can incorrectly treat it as protocol incompatibility, stop retrying, and display misleading version-upgrade guidance.

- Pause reconnect attempts, liveness probes, credential retry waits, and recovery budgets during reported OS sleep. Resume bounded recovery after wake while the network returns, preserving the logical client and session state.
- Retry transient credential and trusted-key acquisition failures. Keep genuine authentication rejection and unsafe encryption non-retryable, without classifying them as protocol-version mismatches.
- Re-arm the watchdog for handshakes interrupted by sleep, preserve authentication recovery guidance, and retain server-upgrade support for real protocol mismatches.
- Hold successful in-flight recovery steps until wake without consuming another attempt, retain terminal rejections during suspension, and preserve host-advertised protocol versions and upgrade methods through the service.
- Add bounded sleep duration and recovery-stop attribution to existing connection-outcome telemetry, with focused regression tests and updated documentation.

The expected scenario is an existing GitHub environment connection surviving a lid-close, move to another Wi-Fi network, and wake without a false protocol-version warning or manual reco

docs.title: MicrotaskEmitter silently drops re-entrant events; emitters leak timers/queues on disposal
event: handle re-entrancy and cleanup on disposal in emitters
docs.body:
Fixes #347261

### Summary of Changes

1. **`MicrotaskEmitter` Re-entrancy Protection:**
   - Drains `this._queuedEvents` into a local snapshot variable before invoking `super.fire()`.
   - Any re-entrant `fire()` call now encounters an empty `_queuedEvents` array (`length === 1`), properly scheduling the next microtask turn and preserving delivery order in FIFO sequence.
   - Clears queue and guards microtask execution against `this._disposed`.

2. **Emitter Disposal Cleanup:**
   - **`DebounceEmitter`**: Overrides `dispose()` to clear any active `this._handle` timeout via `clearTimeout`, preventing pending timers from keeping the event loop alive and firing on disposed listeners.
   - **`PauseableEmitter`**: Overrides `dispose()` to clear `this._eventQueue` (LinkedList), and guards `resume()` and `fire()` against `this._disposed`.
   - **`MicrotaskEmitter`**: Overrides `dispose()` to clear `this._queuedEvents`.
   - **`Emitter`**: Changed `_disposed` to `protected` so subclasses can inspect disposal state without overhead.

### How to Test

Run the mocha test runner on the event test suite:
```bash
pnpm run test-node -- --run src/vs/base/test/common/event.test.ts
```

All 99 tests pass with zero leaks under `ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite()`.

Hygiene check:
```bash

```
Passes with 0 errors.

docs.title: Engineering - copy the styles of the KaTeX that the math notebook renderer bundles
docs.body:
The math notebook renderer of `markdown-math` bundles the KaTeX that `@vscode/markdown-it-katex` depends on (0.16.21), but its build copied `katex.min.css` and the fonts from the first `katex` folder above the extension. Since #347200 installs the extensions with pnpm's isolated linker, `extensions/node_modules` only links their direct dependencies, so that folder is the root project's `katex`, another version (0.16.22). The build now resolves `katex` from `@vscode/markdown-it-katex`, like esbuild does for the JavaScript.

Today the two versions differ only in the version string in the CSS, and their fonts are the same, but the styles and fonts should come from the bundled version: a change to the root's `katex` would otherwise change the notebook's styles too.

It was found while merging the install roots (#347258), and is split out so that it can go in first.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, in a clean checkout of `main` with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`:
- Before: `node esbuild.notebook.mts` in `extensions/markdown-math` wrote the CSS of 0.16.22, next to the bundled 0.16.21.
- After: the same command and `pnpm run gulp compile-extension-media-build` write `katex.min.css` and the 20 `woff2` fonts byte for byte as in `katex@0.16.21/dist`, the version in the bundled `katex.js`.

### Problem

In `extensions/terminal-suggest/src/completions/npm.ts` and `yarn.ts`, the shell command used to locate `package.json` in parent directories checked whether `$PWD` equaled `' / '` instead of `'/'`. When terminal suggestions run in a directory that has no ancestor `package.json`, `$PWD` reaches the filesystem root `/`, which never matches `' / '`. As a result, the loop never terminates and spawns runaway bash processes consuming 100% CPU.

### Fix

Correct the root directory condition in the generator scripts for both npm and yarn completions to match `[[ $PWD = '/' ]]`, consistent with `npx.ts` line 16 and `yarn.ts` line 395.

### Verification

1. Verified that `bash -c "until [[ -f package.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat package.json"` terminates immediately upon reaching the filesystem root when no `package.json` exists.
2. Verified that the syntax and quote escaping match existing sibling completion specifications.

docs.title: Engineering - declare chat-lib's postinstall when the extraction creates its sources
docs.body:
chat-lib (`extensions/copilot/chat-lib`) is a member of the root pnpm workspace, and pnpm runs the install scripts of every member on every install. chat-lib's postinstall copies static files (the tiktoken files and the tree-sitter WebAssembly files) next to the extracted sources, which only exist after `pnpm run extract-chat-lib`. So every install of the repository ran it and printed:

```
extensions/copilot/chat-lib postinstall$ tsx script/postinstall.js
│ chat-lib: no sources yet (run `pnpm run extract-chat-lib` in extensions/copilot), skipping postinstall.
└─ Done in 156ms
```

The checked-in `package.json` now leaves the script out, and `extract-chat-lib` declares it when it writes chat-lib's `package.json`; it already updates the dependencies there on every run. Nothing changes after an extraction:

- The pipelines that test, build and publish chat-lib run `pnpm --dir chat-lib run postinstall` after the extraction, as before.
- The published package still declares the postinstall and includes `script/postinstall.ts`.
- Installs after a local extraction run it again.

A local extraction now leaves the added script in `chat-lib/package.json`, like the dependency updates it can make there. It shouldn't be committed. The script keeps its check for missing sources, which can be deleted after an extraction, for example by `git clean`.

docs.title: GitHub environment (Mission Control) connections keep dropping
docs.body:
VS Code connections to a machine shared as a GitHub environment (Mission Control) keep dropping. Local logs show two separate causes; this issue tracks both.

### 1. Large chats cause a reconnect loop (fix in progress: #346977)

When the connecting client opens a chat whose state serializes to more than 32 MiB, the host cannot publish the `subscribe` response: the relay's chunking codec rejects any message over its reassembly limit ([chunking.ts#L114](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ffe08d127413e67baa2d3cf31a62bdfdcf218f71/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/webPubSub/chunking.ts#L114)). The lane's `send()` then closes the client lane without logging a reason, and the host only logs `Client disconnected`. The client reconnects, subscribes to the same chat again and drops again, about every 30 seconds while the chat is open. In a local reproduction, the chat's `subscribe` result was about 34 M characters.

Windowed state-channel delivery would split the snapshot into `channel/frame` fragments, but it is disabled for relays on both sides: the client offers no `flowControl` on relay transports ([agentHostProtocolClient.ts#L2076](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ffe08d127413e67baa2d3cf31a62bdfdcf218f71/src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts#L2076)), and the host declines relay clients ([protocolServerHandler.ts#L1311](https://github.com/microsoft

docs.title: agentHost: Answer the runtime's Basic proxy authentication through the client
docs.body:
Follow-up to #346967, which added the host → client `vscode/lookupProxyBasicAuthorization` request. This wires the Copilot runtime's own proxied requests to it through the SDK's new `network.authenticateBasic` callback (github/copilot-agent-runtime#37233), so a runtime behind a Basic-auth proxy gets its credentials from the Agent Host instead of from `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` or disk. This matters most for a WSL Agent Host started from the Agents window on Windows: the user logs in once in the Windows proxy login dialog, and the WSL runtime is served the same credentials.

- **Agent Host** (`agentHostProxyResolver.ts`, `copilotAgent.ts`): `lookupBasicAuthorization(proxyUrl, realm, attempt)` asks a local renderer first (the `http.proxy` setting, its stored credentials or its proxy login dialog), else a client sharing the host's network that advertises `vscode.clientProxy`, with the restrictions from #346967. The runtime's `network.authenticateBasic` callback calls it, mapping its `previousRejected` flag to attempt 2 (otherwise 1), so a rejected answer opens the login dialog instead of reusing the stored or `http.proxy` credentials.
- **`http.proxy` with credentials** (`copilotAgent.ts`): the Agent Host no longer sets a credentialed `http.proxy` setting as `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` in the runtime's environment. `resolveProxy` returns that proxy without its credential

docs.title: remoteTunnel: Report the renamed tunnel name immediately
docs.body:
Fixes #346974 (and #347043, closed as its duplicate).

## Problem

Renaming the tunnel from the Remote Environments editor writes `remote.tunnels.access.hostNameOverride` from the window and then asks the shared process for the name with `IRemoteTunnelService.getTunnelName()`. The shared process answers from its own `ConfigurationService`, which only reloads after its settings file watcher fires. The call therefore returns the previous name. With sharing off, nothing refreshes the name afterwards, so the editor stays one rename behind: renaming to `test1` keeps the old name, renaming to `test2` shows `test1`.

## Fix

`RemoteTunnelService.getTunnelName()` now reloads the configuration before reading the intended tunnel name. The reload fires the existing configuration change listener, so a running tunnel still restarts with the new name, and the later watcher reload finds no difference. The other `getTunnelName()` callers in `remoteTunnel.contribution.ts` get the same up-to-date value.

## Testing

- Added a regression test that only applies the written settings when the configuration is reloaded, as in the shared process. It fails without the fix (`old-name`) and passes with it.
- Manually verified in Code OSS with sharing off: before the fix, renaming showed the previous name. With the fix, renaming to `test1`, `test2` and `test3` showed each new name right away.

The unattended restart that applies a downloaded update while the screen is locked (`update.restartWhenIdle`) does not happen while a file is open in the built-in Markdown editor, even when the file is saved. docs.title: webview: don't block unattended restarts on custom text editors
docs.body:
Fixes #347305

The unattended restart that applies an update while the screen is locked is vetoed while a loaded webview retains its context (`webview.retainedContext`). The built-in Markdown editor retains its context only so that switching tabs is fast, so an open Markdown editor kept updates from being applied.

### Change

- `WebviewOptions` gets a `restorable` option: the webview can be recreated without losing anything, even though it retains its context.
- `MainThreadCustomEditors` sets `restorable` on the webviews of custom **text** editors and clears it on those of other custom editors. The content of a custom text editor is a text document, which is backed up and restored like that of any text editor, and the editor is reopened by its view type. Extensions pass custom editor webview options through unchecked, so the core always sets the option and an extension cannot declare its webview restorable.
- `WebviewUnattendedRestartParticipant` ignores restorable webviews.

Webview panels and views (for example the Simple Browser), custom (non-text) editors, the video player and MCP apps still block. Unsaved changes in a custom text editor remain covered by the working copy participant, which blocks while a change is not backed up yet or hot exit is off.

docs.body:
With a product icon theme that overrides `plus`, the comment add button in the editor gutter shows its background but no glyph. The hover rule in `review.css` takes the glyph character from the theme but then forces the `codicon` font, so the character comes from one font and the font from another:

```css
content: var(--vscode-icon-plus-content);
font-family: var(--vscode-icon-plus-font-family);
font-family: "codicon"; /* overrides the theme font */
```

### Changes

docs.title: build: compile Copilot in the platform Compile jobs
docs.body:
Builds the built-in Copilot extension in each platform Compile job, like the other built-in extensions, instead of sharing a VSIX from a separate Copilot stage. Removes the Copilot stage.

## Changes

- **Platform Compile jobs** (Windows, Linux, macOS, Alpine): after `core-ci`, a new template, `copilot/builtin-steps.yml`, replaces the VSIX download. It runs the Copilot `vscode-capi` mixin, imports the translations, extracts `telemetry.json` and runs `compile-copilot-extension-build`.
- **`compile-copilot-extension-build`** (`build/lib/extensions.ts`): builds Copilot, packages it with its own `pnpm run package` (the command the Copilot stage ran), and extracts the VSIX's `extension` folder into `.build/extensions/copilot`. The built-in extension therefore has the same files as the VSIX before. Local builds use the same task, so they now ship what CI ships instead of every production dependency. The existing step that replaces the native files with the target platform's (`prepareBuiltInCopilotRipgrepShim`) is unchanged.
- **Removed:** the Copilot stage from `product-build.yml`, `product-build-template.yml`, `product-build-ado-ci.yml`, `product-smoke-flaky.yml` and `sdk-validation-build.yml`, `product-copilot.yml` and `downloadCopilotVsix.ts`. The web build loses its VSIX download, since it doesn't ship Copilot. The smoke-flaky platform stages no longer wait for the Copilot stage.

docs.title: smoke: Tolerate the startup workspace handoff in selectLocalEnvironment
docs.body:
Fixes a flaky Agents Window smoke test: "Agents Window (local AgentHost, SDK sandbox) › Test Copilot CLI session via AgentHost (SDK sandbox)" timed out in `AgentsWindow.selectLocalEnvironment` (`locator.click: Timeout 30000ms` on the This Computer row). It started failing on `main` in the macOS product build smoke tests, both with and without the PAC proxy.

**Cause**

The smoke tests open the Agents window with a folder. Since #347182, the workspace handoff waits for the startup providers before selecting that folder. The composer can therefore show Cloud first and then switch to This Computer on its own. In the failing trace, the test opened the Environment picker while it showed Cloud, and then the handoff re-rendered the composer, which closed the picker. The single unbounded click on This Computer could not succeed after that.

**Change**

`selectLocalEnvironment` now follows the retry pattern of `selectDevContainer`:
- Each attempt is bounded.
- A failed attempt is retried.
- Escape is pressed only while the picker is still open.

The loop ends once the picker no longer shows Cloud, including when the handoff selected This Computer itself. Once the test makes a selection (environment or session type), the handoff is cancelled as a user change, so it cannot reset the composer later.

Follow-up to #346526: `remoteConnections.selectMethod` reported a stale `activeMethod` when the selection came from the Agents window title bar or the chat input.

Both toolbars registered the Remote Connections view item with `IRemoteTunnelService.onDidChangeTunnelStatus` as its re-render event, so every tunnel status change re-created the item and disposed its sharing state while `selectMethod` was still applying the selection. docs.title: Persist Copilot-owned plugin enablement in harness configuration
docs.body:
Copilot-owned plugin enablement should have one authoritative source: the Copilot harness configuration. Workbench and Agent Host overrides should not compete with global or repository decisions from the harness.

Installation scope and enablement scope are separate: plugins remain installed in the shared user cache, while a repository can override global activation through `enabledPlugins` in `.github/copilot/settings.json`.

### Intended behavior

- Support global and repository enablement for Copilot-owned plugins, without a separate session-only enablement state.
- Persist global decisions through the SDK plugin enable/disable API.
- Derive the target repository from the session/chat context, rather than passing an independent working directory.
- Until a public SDK repository-mutation API exists, isolate edits to the shareable `.github/copilot/settings.json` behind a helper with a replacement TODO.
- Preserve unrelated settings and surface malformed configuration, unsupported targets, and file conflicts explicitly.
- Leave standalone MCP enablement and other plugin providers unchanged.

docs.title: MCP Apps: agent-host sessions drop CallToolResult `_meta` from `ui/notifications/tool-result`
docs.body:
**What happens**
In Copilot agent-host chat sessions, an MCP App gets its `ui/notifications/tool-result` without the tool result's `_meta`. Normal chat sessions are fine: `mcpLanguageModelToolContribution.ts` passes the raw `callResult` as `mcpOutput`.

The agent-host path rebuilds the result in `toMcpCallToolResult` (`stateToProgressAdapter.ts`). It only adds `_meta` when `resultMetadata` is set, and that comes from `getSdkMcpResultMeta` (`mapSessionEvents.ts`). The TODO there says the pinned `@github/copilot-sdk` does not declare `mcpResultMeta` yet, so `_meta` is always missing.

**Why it matters**
The MCP Apps spec lets a server send UI-only data in the result's `_meta`, which keeps it out of the model's context. Without `_meta`, an app has nothing to render and its only option is to fall back to `content`/`structuredContent`. `structuredContent` is also given to the model as text.

**Repro**
1. Add an MCP server whose tool has `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and returns `{ content: [{type:'text', text:'summary'}], _meta: { 'example/card': {...} } }`.
2. Call the tool from an agent-host session (we saw this with Copilot Fusion auto-selecting a model).
3. In the app iframe, the `ui/notifications/tool-result` params have `content` but no `_meta`.

**Expected**
`_meta` passed through unchanged, the same as in normal chat sessions.

docs.title: Chat resources: show websites in the integrated browser
docs.body:
Part of #345427. Stacked on [#345428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345428); the diff against that branch is this PR's change.

[#345428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345428) lets a chat show the files its agent records as pills or above the chat input, rendered by their default editor. Agents also record websites, for example a page they are building or a preview of a pull request; there is no editor for a URL, so #345428 leaves them in the Artifacts list. This PR makes recorded websites chat resources as well.

- Shown above the chat input, a website is a page of the integrated browser, in its native view, laid out and clipped to the chat.

docs.title: add_artifact_or_reference accepts file URIs with the drive letter as host name
docs.body:
Agents on Windows sometimes record a file with `add_artifact_or_reference` using two slashes, for example `file://D:/repo/plan.md`. In a URI, what follows `//` is the host name, so this parses as host `D:` and path `/repo/plan.md`: a network path (`\\D:\repo\plan.md`), not the file on drive D. The tool accepts it, and the recorded entry points to a file that does not exist, so opening it fails.

Expected: the tool rejects such a URI with an error the agent can act on, naming the corrected URI (`file:///D:/repo/plan.md`).

docs.title: Reject file URIs with the drive letter as host name in add_artifact_or_reference
docs.body:
Fixes #347338

Agents on Windows sometimes record a file with `add_artifact_or_reference` using two slashes, for example `file://D:/repo/plan.md`. That parses with `D:` as the host name and names a network path, so the recorded entry pointed to a file that does not exist.

`add_artifact_or_reference` now rejects a `file` URI whose host name is a drive letter, like it already rejects plain file system paths, and the error names the corrected URI with three slashes (`file:///D:/repo/plan.md`), so the agent can retry right away.

A test covers the rejection and the suggested URI.

docs.title: ResourceMap copy constructor drops custom toKey comparator causing data inaccessibility and duplicate keys
map: preserve custom toKey and re-key on ResourceMap copy
docs.body:
Fixes #347343

### Summary of Changes

In `ResourceMap` (`src/vs/base/common/map.ts`), the copy constructor (`new ResourceMap(arg)`) cloned the internal map (`new Map(arg.map)`) but defaulted `this.toKey` to `ResourceMap.defaultToKey` rather than inheriting `arg.toKey`.

When `arg` was initialized with a custom key comparison function (e.g. `extUriIgnorePathCase.getComparisonKey`):
- All copied keys in `this.map` were hashed according to `arg.toKey`.
- Subsequent `copy.has(uri)` and `copy.get(uri)` calls hashed via `defaultToKey`, failing to match the internal keys.
- Calling `copy.set(uri, val)` inserted duplicate entries under `defaultToKey`.
- Providing an explicit new `toKey` (`new ResourceMap(arg, newToKey)`) failed to re-key existing entries.

### Changes:
1. **Preserve `toKey`:** When `toKey` is not passed, `this.toKey` defaults to `arg.toKey`.
2. **Re-key when comparator changes:** If `this.toKey !== arg.toKey`, entries are re-keyed via `this.set(entry.uri, entry.value)`. If `this.toKey === arg.toKey`, it maintains the fast `new Map(arg.map)` shallow clone.
3. **Tests:** Added unit tests in `src/vs/base/test/common/map.test.ts` verifying:
   - `ResourceMap - clone preserves custom toKey`
   - `ResourceMap - clone with new toKey re-keys entries`

docs.title: Fix materialized chat model reference lifetime
docs.body:
Fixes #347346.

After the first send materializes an untitled contributed chat, ChatService retains the acquired real-model reference indefinitely. Switching away leaves the old model and its Agent Host subscriptions alive, preventing idle eviction and retaining MCP processes even with `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_SESSION_RESIDENCY_LIMIT=0`.

Tie the temporary reference to the untitled model's lifetime: retain it across the first-send/UI handoff, then dispose it when the UI releases the untitled model. Also release it if materialization fails or the untitled model is disposed while the real session is loading. Give the reference an explicit diagnostic owner.

This preserves the handoff keep-alive needed by 6bc5ae80de9caffb21e9eb58e18b5ca24fa2d6e8 instead of disposing the model before the UI can acquire it.

Add four regression tests covering a completed response before UI takeover, abandonment without takeover, disposal during a pending load, and failure after loading. Update the existing re-target-mapping test to acquire the UI's real-model reference before releasing the draft.

### Validation

- Client transpilation: `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`.
- Full ChatService test file: **309 passing**, including all four new regression tests.
- Targeted materialization suite: **18 passing** (including the test runner's unexpected-error check).

docs.title: Allow users to configure the Agent Host session residency limit in Settings
docs.body:
### Feature request

Expose the Agent Host session residency limit as a discoverable user setting, for example `chat.agentHost.sessionResidencyLimit`, instead of requiring the `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_SESSION_RESIDENCY_LIMIT` environment variable.

### Motivation

The current default is 10 resident sessions. Each loaded SDK conversation can retain MCP connections and local server processes, so users need to choose the tradeoff between resource use and warm session switching. An environment-variable-only override requires launching VS Code from a specially configured environment and restarting the application. It is particularly inconvenient for macOS users launching from the Dock.

### Proposed behavior

- Application-scoped setting available in Settings UI and user settings JSON.
- Non-negative integer, with the existing default of 10.
- Zero allows eligible unobserved idle sessions to be released without retaining a warm session cache. It must not interrupt active turns, release subscribed sessions, delete history, or bypass existing release protections.
- Apply changes to the running Agent Host and reconcile eligible sessions when the limit changes.
- Preserve the environment variable as an explicit override for existing deployments and test harnesses.
- Document that this is a soft residency limit rather than an immediate process-count cap; SDK unload delays and other lifetime ow

docs.title: Chat resources: let the agent choose how the chat shows what it records
docs.body:
Part of #345427.

Chat resources ([#345428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345428), merged) let the user pin a file that the chat's agent recorded into a pill of its own and show it above the chat input. Often the agent knows best what to show: a status or plan file it keeps updating is worth having above the input right away. This PR lets the agent ask for that when it records the file.

 

## How it works

`add_artifact_or_reference` gets an optional `mode` per file:

```json
{ "type": "file", "label": "Bug #1234 status", "isArtifact": true, "uri": "file:///repo/status.md", "mode": "aboveInput" }
```

- `pinned`: the chat pins the file into a pill of its own, as the pin in the Artifacts list does.
- `aboveInput`: the chat also checks **Show Above Chat Input** for it and shows it.
- Without `mode`, the file is only listed, as before.

The mode is stored with the artifact. Each chat applies a request **once**, doing what the user would do, and remembers that it did (in workspace storage, per chat). So the user's later changes stick: unpinning or hiding the file stays that way until the agent records the file again with another mode. This keeps the shared pin state as it is; it has no "default" layer.

## Gating

- The agent host offers `mode` only while `chat.resources.enabled` is on. The setting is mirrored to the host as the root config key `chatResources`. A `mode`

docs.title: agentHost: keep reauthorized GitHub credentials instead of prompting sign-in
docs.body:
## Problem

A signed-in user could see **Sign in** on every pull request artifact pill, and it never went away, even though the GitHub token was valid.

The cause was a feedback loop:

1. A credential refusal for one PR artifact asks every connected client to authenticate the repository resource again.
2. Each client re-sends the **same** token. `onDidAuthenticate` reports this as a token change, so `GitHubCredentialService` replaced its healthy generation.
3. The replaced generation aborted its in-flight work with `GitHubRequestError(..., 'authentication')`. Fragment fetches waiting for that generation committed the abort as a real authentication failure.
4. Every PR artifact then reported a refusal and asked for authentication again, so steps 1–3 repeated. Each round also rescheduled all fragments, which overloaded the request queue ("GitHub request capacity exceeded").
5. The artifact only cleared its sign-in state once **every** fragment was `ready && complete`. With `checks` and `mergeability` overloaded, it never cleared.

## Fix

- **A reauthorization is a refresh, not a revocation.** When a token notification yields the token the current, resolved generation already holds, `GitHubCredentialService` keeps the credential and fires a new `reauthorization` invalidation reason. The PR resource and query services retry only entries or fragments that failed, which keeps same-t

Fixes #347037

## Problem

In the Agents window, after you open Inbox and go back to a chat, Inbox stays open as an editor tab in that chat's side panel. With per-chat layout (the default since #346836), the chat that was active when Inbox opened keeps showing Inbox on every later visit and after reload, even if you had closed its side panel. New drafts, and chats that have no editors of their own, also show Inbox beside them.

## Cause

Inbox is a window canvas: a singleton tab in the Editor, which the Agents window shows as the side panel to the right of the chats. It moved there from a full-surface custom view shortly before #337081 merged. The desktop layout never treated the move as a navigation away from the chat:

- Opening Inbox reveals the Editor while the chat is still active, and the layout saved that reveal as the chat's side-panel composition. Composition capture skipped only custom views, which covered Inbox before the move.
- Leaving Inbox re-shows the chats but leaves the Editor open with Inbox active.
- The canvas service reopens the Inbox tab into every chat's editor group, and several layout checks counted it as the chat's own editor. So a chat with nothing open still kept an Editor showing only Inbox, and a new draft's default Files tab opened behind it.

docs.title: build: cache the prepared WSL distribution in the Windows smoke job
docs.body:
The Windows x64 smoke job, in both CI and product builds, builds its WSL Dev Container distribution from scratch in every run. That takes about 8 minutes of what is often the slowest job of the CI build. On GitHub, the WSL smoke job already imports a prepared distribution that a separate daily job builds. This brings the same to Azure Pipelines without a separate pipeline or stage: the smoke job keeps the distribution in a pipeline cache itself.

### Changes

- `build/azure-pipelines/win32/steps/product-build-win32-test.yml`: three steps before Setup, with the same checkpoint condition:
  - Compute the UTC day for the cache key.
  - `Cache@2` restores `.build/wsl-distro-cache`, keyed on `"wsl-distro" | "v1" | "win32-x64" | test/smoke/wslDevContainer.ps1 | build/checksums/wsl.txt | build/.cachesalt | <UTC day>`.
  - On a hit, the restored VHD moves to where Setup imports it; nothing is saved after an exact hit. On a miss, `wslDevContainer.ps1 -Operation Prepare` exports the VHD into the cache folder, Setup imports a copy, and the cache's post-job step saves the original.
  - Setup now gets `WSL_PREPARED_DISTRO_VHD`, so it imports the VHD with `wsl --import-in-place`, and still builds the distribution when there is none or the import fails.
- `build/lib/test/testCheckpointTemplates.test.ts`: the WSL step sequence includes the new steps.
- `test/smoke/README.md` and the smoke-test

docs.body:
Fixes #346982

## Cause

The Remote Environments editor queued its choices, but the Remote Connections menus applied each choice right away. A choice made while another was still being applied acted on the transitional state. When Dev Tunnels was chosen while sharing via GitHub Environments was off, a quick GitHub Environments choice still read the connection method as GitHub Environments and turned it on. Saving Dev Tunnels as the method then turned GitHub Environments off again and started the Dev Tunnel. The menus also checked the active method rather than the choice just made.

## Changes

- Choices from the title bar and chat input menus and the Remote Environments editor go through one queue per window, so each is applied to the state the previous one left.
- A choice that a later one supersedes while it waits is skipped. It is not applied and not logged in `remoteConnections.selectMethod`.
- While choices are being applied, every surface shows the choice made last. Previously, only the editor showed its own pending choice.
- Each choice reads the current sharing state from the services when it is applied, rather than from a state source that can lag behind or be disposed with its toolbar. `previousMethod` in the telemetry is read at that point too.

docs.title: Ship @vscode/diff in the web and server node_modules
docs.body:
The diff editor loads `@vscode/diff` at runtime from `node_modules` (`externalLinesDiffComputer.ts`, via `resolveAmdNodeModulePath`), like `@vscode/tree-sitter-wasm` and `vscode-oniguruma`, so the bundler leaves it alone and the package can load its `.wasm` next to itself. Desktop ships the root `node_modules`, but web and server builds only ship the dependencies of `remote/web/package.json` and `remote/package.json`, and `@vscode/diff` was only in the root `package.json`.

So with `diffEditor.diffAlgorithm` set to `advanced-external` or `advanced-wasm`, the package fails to load on vscode.dev, Codespaces and the server, and the built-in algorithm is used instead (reported as `fallback: error` in `diffEditor.computeDiff`, added in #346266).

This adds `@vscode/diff` at the root's version to both manifests and the `remote` lockfile. The hygiene check (`checkPackageJSON` in `build/gulpfile.hygiene.ts`) keeps the versions equal to the root's.

Validation:
- `pnpm install --lockfile-only --frozen-lockfile` in `remote`: passed (lockfile up to date, supply-chain policies pass). The lockfile entry has the same integrity as the root lockfile's.
- Not run locally: a web or server build. To test, set `diffEditor.diffAlgorithm` to `advanced-wasm` in a vscode.dev or server build of this PR and open a diff; it should no longer log a fallback.

## Description

VS Code incorrectly increases indentation after pressing Enter at the end of a Ruby endless method definition.

Unlike regular Ruby methods, endless methods do not open a block and therefore should not increase the indentation level on the following line.

The issue reproduces with all extensions disabled, including in a newly created Ruby file.

## Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.145.2
- Commit: `c4453f8ea430795f941c1b2ff6c9321135a74a02`
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- Language: Ruby
- Extensions disabled: Yes

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch VS Code with all extensions disabled:

   ```sh
   code --disable-extensions --new-window
   ```

2. Create a new file and set its language mode to Ruby, or open an existing `.rb` file.
3. Enter the following code:

   ```ruby
   def endless_method = puts "Hello, World!"
   ```

4. Place the cursor at the end of the line.
5. Press Enter.

The cursor should be positioned at column 1, without additional indentation:

```ruby
def endless_method = puts "Hello, World!"
|
```

The `|` character represents the cursor position.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code increases the indentation level by two spaces:

```ruby
def endless_method = puts "Hello, World!"
  |
```

- All extensions are disabled using `--disable-extensions`.

docs.title: ci: let Copilot review pull requests whose head predates the pnpm store cache action
docs.body:
Copilot code review fails before it starts on any pull request whose head doesn't have `.github/actions/restore-pnpm-store`. Copilot runs `copilot-setup-steps.yml` from **main** against the **pull request head**. Since #347205 (Nov 9, 23:04 UTC), that file uses the local action, and a head based on an older main, or on release/1.146, doesn't have it:

```
Restore pnpm store cache
##[error]Can't find 'action.yml', 'action.yaml' or 'Dockerfile' under '/home/runner/work/vscode/vscode/.github/actions/restore-pnpm-store'.
```

## How often

Of the 109 open pull requests updated since #347205, 31 have a head without the action. 27 target main, 1 targets release/1.146, and 3 are stacked on other branches. Every `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` run since then:

| Head has the action | Runs | Passed | Failed at `Restore pnpm store cache` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Yes | 25 | 25 | 0 |
| No | 5 | 0 | 5 |

Rebasing fixes a main pull request, but release/1.146 doesn't have the action at all, so **no pull request into release/1.146 can get a Copilot review** until this lands or the action is backported.

## Change

The restore step runs only when the action is in the checkout. Otherwise pnpm installs without the cached store. The action already treats a cache failure as non-fatal, and no later step reads its outputs.

## Validation

`copilot-setup-steps` has a `push` trigger on its own pat

## Mechanism

`FloatingAuxiliaryBarController.animateFrame` picks the longer timings when `max(|rendered.width - compact.width|, |rendered.height - compact.height|) > 240`.

The test next to it, `measures a changed compact caption before choosing its motion distance and duration`, already sets the width from the measured caption (`compact.width + 230`) for this reason.

docs.title: Agent plugins whose only content is a Copilot extension (e.g. a canvas) are not sent to remote agent hosts
docs.body:
When a VS Code extension contributes an agent plugin (`chatPlugins`) and a chat runs on a remote agent host, the window sends the plugin to the host only if VS Code finds hooks, commands, skills, agents, instructions or MCP servers in it. A plugin whose only content is a Copilot extension, for example one that declares a canvas in `extensions/<name>/extension.mjs`, is never sent. Its canvas is missing from remote agent host sessions, while the same plugin works when installed on the host directly.

The filter is in `resolveCustomizationRefs` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts`. VS Code does not parse Copilot extensions, so such plugins look empty to it.

Expected: every installed plugin is sent to the agent host, which copies it and decides what it can use.

docs.title: build: start the Linux CI test jobs from workspace images
docs.body:
A pilot of the GitHub workspace images in the Azure Pipelines product build, for the **Linux CI test jobs only**. Every Linux CI test job installs all dependencies from scratch before it compiles and tests. With an image, the install steps only install what changed since the image. Windows is the next step once this has proven itself; product builds and other platforms are unchanged.

This PR now only contains the images. The CI test jobs already skip the build steps their tests don't need, since #347568. That also removes the step that failed on the image: the CI test jobs no longer generate the telemetry lists, whose rename across file systems failed with `EXDEV`. The job rebalancing that was on this branch was dropped.

### How it works

- **Image job** (`Linux (X64) - Image`, new in the Linux stage of CI builds):
  - Looks up the image of the current key.
  - When the cache doesn't have it, it mounts an empty ext4 volume over its checkout, runs the same setup steps as the test jobs in it, and packs it with the existing `image.ts` format. The cache saves it at the end of the job.
  - It installs without the distro and the other private repositories, so an image holds neither their sources nor their credentials.
  - It continues on error, so a failure never fails the build. The cache only saves after a job that fully succeeded.
- **Test jobs** (`VSCODE_WORKSPACE_IMAGE: use`)

docs.title: Agent host: send plugins without contributions VS Code parses, such as canvas-only plugins
docs.body:
Agent plugins can contain content that only the agent host's Copilot runtime understands, for example a Copilot extension that declares a canvas (`extensions/<name>/extension.mjs`). When a chat ran on a remote agent host, the window sent an installed plugin to the host only if VS Code had found hooks, commands, skills, agents, instructions or MCP servers in it. A plugin with only such an extension looked empty to VS Code and never reached the host, so its canvas was missing in remote sessions. The same plugin works when it is installed on the host directly.

With this change, `resolveCustomizationRefs` sends every installed plugin. The host copies the plugin (cached by the folder's modification time) and uses whatever it supports. Plugins found through prompt-file enumeration are still sent once.

Found while shipping a canvas-only plugin from an extension (the CDP viewer canvas in microsoft/vscode-packages#421).

Validation: `resolveCustomizationRefs.test.ts` passes (51 tests), including a new test for a plugin without contributions VS Code parses.

Fixes #347397

docs.title: sessions: Share SSH, WSL and tunnel agent hosts as GitHub environments
docs.body:
Adds a **Share {0} as GitHub Environment** row action to SSH, WSL and Dev Tunnel remotes in the Remotes editor. Sharing registers the remote's existing agent host as a GitHub environment with the user's GitHub account, so other apps that support GitHub environments can reach it. Once a remote is shared, the action changes to **Stop Sharing {0} as GitHub Environment**.

## How it works

- **Protocol:** two new VS Code-private AHP extension methods, `vscode/registerGitHubEnvironment` (account id + credential) and `vscode/unregisterGitHubEnvironment` (account id).
- **Status:** supporting hosts report their GitHub environment status under the namespaced `_meta` key `vscode.githubEnvironment` in the initialize and reconnect results, and broadcast changes with the `vscode/githubEnvironment/changed` notification. docs.title: UriTemplate: path-segment separator dropped for unexploded lists/maps and empty fragment returns '#'
docs.body:

- VS Code Version: main (commit 11f4a35a03dab71ab8275aed1b779148cf184719 / 1.147.0-dev)
- OS Version: Platform-independent (macOS / Linux / Windows)

### Summary

In `src/vs/base/common/uriTemplate.ts` (used by MCP resource template expansion and Agent Host changeset URIs), two RFC 6570 compliance bugs exist in `UriTemplate._expand`:

1. **Path-segment separator omission (`{/var,list}`)**:
   According to [RFC 6570 §3.2.6 (Path Segment Expansion: `{/var}`)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570#section-3.2.6):

   In `UriTemplate._expand`, scalar variables (`vals.push('/' + enc)`), exploded arrays (`vals.push(value.map(x => '/' + ...).join(''))`), and exploded maps (`pairs.push('/' + k + '=' + ...)`) receive a `'/'` prefix.
   However, **unexploded arrays** (line 224) and **unexploded maps** (line 186) are pushed to `vals` **without** a `'/'` prefix:
   ```ts
   // Line 186 (unexploded object):
   vals.push(joined);

   // Line 224 (unexploded array):
   vals.push(value.map(x => UriTemplate._encode(x, isReserved)).join(','));
   ```
   At the end of `_expand`, `filtered.join('')` joins segments with an empty string. If an unexploded list or map is preceded by another variable, the path separator is dropped:
