docs.title: Send the Copilot billable owner on core's assignments request
docs.body:
sends `github_core_copilotbillableentityid` on core's assignments request, from the optional `billable_owner` field in the `copilot_internal/user` entitlements (who pays for the user's Copilot). this is the same value the Copilot Chat extension sends (#346433), so experiments that randomize by company get the same variant in core and in chat.

- `IEntitlementsData` gets the optional `billable_owner` field.
- `GitHubCoreAssignmentsFilterProvider` adds the filter from the default account's entitlements, only when both `universal_key` and `account_type` are non-empty strings. a change in only this value fires `onDidChangeFilters`, so assignments refetch, and signing out clears it.
- github.com only returns the field when its flag is on for the user, so there's no client flag.

tests in `assignmentFilters.test.ts`.

docs.title: Compare Models: keep Open Comparison visible outside collapsed tool steps
docs.body:
## Problem

When an agent creates a model comparison, the Open Comparison link is buried inside collapsed tool steps. The comparison can launch successfully while appearing not to have been created because its primary navigation action is hidden.

## Requested behavior

Show a deterministic, client-rendered Open Comparison action at the top level of the originating response, outside collapsed thinking/tool steps and the completed-work disclosure. Keep execution details collapsible, preserve focus in the original chat, and retain the action when restoring history after reload. The action should support keyboard navigation and activation without depending on the model echoing a link.

docs.title: base: fix UriTemplate path separator and empty fragment expansion (#347406)
docs.body:
Fixes #347406

### Summary of Changes

1. **Path-segment separator omission (`{/var,list}`)**:
   In `src/vs/base/common/uriTemplate.ts`, `isPath` (`{/var}`) previously omitted the `'/'` prefix for unexploded arrays and map values. When an unexploded list or map was preceded by another variable (e.g., `{/var,list}` or `{/list1,list2}`), segments were joined without a path separator, producing `/helloa,b` instead of `/hello/a,b`.
   - Prepends `'/'` to unexploded array and map values when `isPath` is true, conforming to RFC 6570 §3.2.6.

2. **Dangling `#` on undefined fragment expansion (`{#undef}`)**:
   In `isFragment` (`{#var}`), `joined = prefix + vals.join(',')` was executed without verifying `vals.length > 0`. When all variables in the expression were undefined or empty, it returned `'#'` instead of `''`.
   - Added check `vals.length ? prefix + vals.join(',') : ''`, conforming to RFC 6570 §3.2.4 & §3.2.1.

### Testing

- All existing test cases in `src/vs/base/test/common/uriTemplate.test.ts` continue to pass.
- Added regression tests covering:
  - `{/var,list}` -> `/value/red,green,blue`
  - `{/list,var}` -> `/red,green,blue/value`
  - `{/var,keys}` -> `/value/semi,;,dot,.,comma,,`
  - `{#undef,null}` -> `""`

docs.title: VS Code - Workspace Trust Bypass via Prototype Pollution in Workspace Configuration
docs.body:
## Summary

Configuration merging and dotted-key expansion could read inherited object properties or treat `__proto__` as a prototype setter instead of ordinary configuration data. Configuration supplied by a workspace must not modify shared object prototypes or inherited state used by Workspace Trust.

### Patches

Use own-property checks during configuration merging and dotted-key expansion, and safely store special property names as ordinary data.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0f9fbffbe15469faaee522ed37024b2e17b3158a
- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e64c53effb75eee25fc54c5636eb58a835e47874

docs.title: VS Code - Workspace Trust Bypass via Settings Group Key Override
docs.body:
## Summary

Workspace Trust interpreted a missing or non-boolean effective value of `security.workspace.trust.enabled` as disabled. Malformed configuration must not disable Workspace Trust.

### Patches

Keep Workspace Trust enabled unless its effective configuration value is explicitly a boolean.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/99c4193564f32d93b80ad3b47c0be99b9135e1f6

docs.title: VS Code - Security Feature Bypass via Inherited Publisher Names in Allowed Extensions Policy
docs.body:
## Summary

The allowed-extensions configuration used an ordinary object, allowing inherited property names to participate in publisher lookups. The publisher-trust check also treated a non-boolean allowlist result as approval. Only explicitly allowed extensions and publishers should receive policy-based approval.

### Patches

Build the allowed-extensions lookup without a prototype, and bypass the publisher-trust prompt only when the allowlist check returns `true`.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e82ead06d9417ed5228dcc96859085e0c5ef8233

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via Extension Text Rendered as Markdown
docs.body:
## Summary

Extension gallery display names, descriptions, versions, and installation-status text could be interpreted as Markdown in extension status messages and hovers. Gallery-provided text must render as plain text rather than introducing links, commands, icons, or other Markdown content.

### Patches

Escape untrusted gallery text before inserting it into extension status messages and hover Markdown.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6471d0d67349fe86bd56fe994d9c599684e76af8

docs.title: VS Code - Command Injection via Crafted Publisher Names in the Extension Trust Dialog
docs.body:
## Summary

The extension publisher-trust dialog inserted gallery-provided publisher and extension display names into Markdown and trusted all command links. These names must not introduce executable command links into the trust dialog.

### Patches

Escape gallery-provided labels and restrict trusted command links to the product's `extension.open` command.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b31ca92facb67c96a0136ffb94bc4744431b8099

docs.title: VS Code - Workspace Trust Bypass via Unregistered Experiment Override Settings
docs.body:
## Summary

Unregistered settings, including `experiments.override.*` settings, could be read from an untrusted workspace. Restricted Mode must ignore these workspace-provided values.

### Patches

Skip unregistered settings in untrusted workspace and folder configuration, and notify configuration listeners when trust changes add or remove those settings.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7a1a8e46fff5f4b06dc830d61ed2988513035d48

docs.title: VS Code - Workspace Trust Bypass via Restricted Settings Written as Flat Dotted Keys
docs.body:
## Summary

Configuration keys written below a registered object setting could miss the registered ancestor's restriction, scope, and exclusion rules. A dotted child key must not bypass the restrictions of its registered parent in an untrusted workspace.

### Patches

Apply the closest registered ancestor's configuration rules to dotted child keys, ignore unregistered settings in untrusted workspaces, and notify listeners when trust changes affect the configuration.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7a1a8e46fff5f4b06dc830d61ed2988513035d48

docs.title: CSS injection via font settings
docs.body:
## Summary

Font-family and font-size configuration values reached generated CSS for inline suggestions, token styling, and notebooks without sufficient validation. Configuration values must not introduce additional CSS declarations or rules into the workbench.

### Patches

Sanitize font-family values before generating CSS, validate token font-size multipliers, restrict the affected inline-suggestion font setting, and require finite numeric notebook font sizes with safe defaults.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/bcfb213aac110676ca62712f8176295344de3272
- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4df406260645b536702e028a356abac2c3b102ae

docs.title: VS Code - Information Disclosure via Images on UNC Paths in Rendered Markdown
docs.body:
## Summary

On Windows, media served through the `vscode-file:` protocol could access UNC hosts without passing through the UNC restrictions enforced by Node.js file access. Rendered media must respect the configured UNC host allowlist.

### Patches

Check UNC access restrictions before serving media through the `vscode-file:` protocol, including case-insensitive host matching and rejecting malformed UNC paths.

The fixes are included on the public [release/1.145 branch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/release/1.145) for **VS Code 1.145.3**.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/da88f7969dbfd1070b07bf6543580feda2e08b32

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via JavaScript Debugger Auto-Attach
docs.body:
### Summary

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions where JavaScript debugger auto-attach settings from an untrusted workspace could influence which executable VS Code launched during startup. This could allow a malicious repository to run attacker-controlled code before Workspace Trust protected the workspace.

### Details

An attacker would need to convince the user to open a malicious folder or repository. Starting a debug session or running a task was not required.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fix (f25c662c6bfead64d1296c5e5d0669cbff91fa5c) updates the bundled JavaScript debugger so startup auto-attach no longer trusts workspace-controlled executable lookup configuration in an untrusted workspace.

### Workarounds

Do not open untrusted folders or repositories. Disable JavaScript automatic attach when working with untrusted content, and do not grant Workspace Trust until the repository contents have been reviewed.

### References

- The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f25c662c6bfead64d1296c5e5d0669cbff91fa5c
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-3grj-pfwj-fffm
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-70094

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via Network Workspace Trust Bypass
docs.body:
### Summary

A Workspace Trust vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions when opening an HTTP(S) Workspace Configuration File. VS Code could classify the resulting network-backed workspace as trusted and apply process-starting workspace settings before the user made a trust decision.

### Details

An attacker would need to convince the user to open a crafted link to a remote Workspace Configuration File. Workspace settings such as MCP server definitions could then start an attacker-controlled process.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fix (d8e03ca86c6ef9ae33c5f288d5394d91d2b36ccf) mitigates this by applying normal Workspace Trust rules to HTTP and HTTPS workspace resources and requiring an explicit trust decision.

### Workarounds

Do not open remote `.code-workspace` links from untrusted sources. Download and review workspace configuration files before opening them locally, and do not grant Workspace Trust to unreviewed content.

### References

- The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d8e03ca86c6ef9ae33c5f288d5394d91d2b36ccf
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-g3fj-wc2g-v3j5
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-119985

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via MCP Elicitation Notifications
docs.body:
### Summary

A vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions in the fallback notification path for MCP elicitation requests. Server-controlled message content could be interpreted as an interactive VS Code command link, allowing a malicious MCP server to cause command execution if a user activated the crafted notification.

### Details

An attacker would need to control a connected MCP server and convince the user to click the malicious link in the resulting notification.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fixes (305e2483c2aea24ffe21eb085e9fb6025e542d18 and e3a49623dd798f2df3283b700b3d1b8c0779ffbb) mitigate this by rendering elicitation messages as literal text and validating the request payload before displaying it.

### Workarounds

Only connect to trusted MCP servers, and do not activate links in notifications produced by an untrusted server.

### References

- The patches for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/305e2483c2aea24ffe21eb085e9fb6025e542d18 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e3a49623dd798f2df3283b700b3d1b8c0779ffbb
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-66hq-jw93-462h
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-120779

docs.title: VS Code - Command Execution via Agent-Originated Local Commands
docs.body:
### Summary

A security feature bypass exists in the VS Code Agent Host in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions. Local-command syntax originating from an agent message could be treated as if it had been entered directly by the user and could execute without the expected terminal approval.

### Details

An attacker would need to influence an agent's child prompt, typically through untrusted repository instructions or other prompt content, and the user would need to grant the related session tool operation.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fix (0b7cb30553712c2e385ade16a2e2e9aae0979b77) mitigates this by preserving message origin and limiting local-command handling to messages that actually originated from the user.

### Workarounds

Use the Copilot harness instead of the Local harness where available. Keep terminal approvals enabled and do not grant session-wide tool permissions for repositories with untrusted instructions.

### References

- The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0b7cb30553712c2e385ade16a2e2e9aae0979b77
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-w9fm-7vcm-cvq4
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-120782

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via Unvalidated MCP SSE Endpoints
docs.body:
### Summary

A vulnerability exists in the legacy SSE transport used by VS Code's MCP client in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions. A remote MCP server could supply a new transport endpoint that VS Code used without sufficiently validating its origin and protocol, allowing follow-up requests to be directed to an unintended destination and potentially exposing credentials or enabling further code execution.

### Details

An attacker would need to convince a user to connect VS Code to a malicious or compromised MCP server.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fix (1ea9a4c1a39be2bd7e090751281d5e720ec5d239) mitigates this by validating server-provided SSE endpoints before VS Code establishes the follow-up transport.

### Workarounds

Only connect to trusted MCP servers. Disable or remove affected legacy SSE servers until the update is installed, and prefer a trusted transport configuration.

### References

- The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1ea9a4c1a39be2bd7e090751281d5e720ec5d239
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-4x35-6qr8-ww48
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-119983

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via serve-web Release Downgrade
docs.body:
### Summary

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the VS Code `serve-web` request router in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions. An unauthenticated request could select and start an older VS Code web server version under the current installation's account and connection-token configuration, reintroducing the security behavior of an obsolete release into an otherwise updated deployment.

### Details

An attacker would need network access to the `serve-web` endpoint and would need to convince a previously authenticated user to visit a crafted link.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fix (e45c3db29aa2936b2fb81167da3e0ecceaed6053) mitigates this by authenticating requests before resolving or starting a selected release and rejecting cross-site cookie authentication.

### Workarounds

Keep `serve-web` bound to localhost and do not expose it directly to untrusted networks. Protect reverse-proxied deployments with an additional authentication layer, and do not open unexpected `serve-web` links from untrusted pages.

### References

- The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e45c3db29aa2936b2fb81167da3e0ecceaed6053
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-xfg5-fq3p-cx69
- MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/upda

docs.title: VS Code - Remote Code Execution via Malicious MCP Installation Links
docs.body:
### Summary

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions where a crafted MCP installation link could include unsafe input definitions or variable values that were not rejected before installation. If installed, those values could cause VS Code to resolve a command-backed input and execute a command with the user's permissions.

### Details

An attacker would need to convince the user to open a malicious MCP installation link and approve the installation.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. The fixes (6f1f0c423526126fc70c0945d5b6f277985c9cb1 and 82e93d62dceb39f9e596250e477744124c2a2201) mitigate this by validating MCP install-link inputs, rejecting unsupported command-backed variables, and making the configuration being installed more explicit.

### Workarounds

Only install MCP servers from trusted sources. Do not open untrusted `vscode:mcp/install` links, and review the displayed server configuration before approving installation.

### References

- The patches for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6f1f0c423526126fc70c0945d5b6f277985c9cb1 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/82e93d62dceb39f9e596250e477744124c2a2201
- The security advisory can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-crhv-2887-p3xr

docs.title: Delete/Backspace intermittently fails in agent question inputs
docs.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not collected
- VS Code Version: Reported version not collected; investigated current main
- OS Version: macOS; exact version not collected
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent questions, free-text/custom answers
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not collected
- Logs: Not attached

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have an agent ask a question that accepts a free-text/custom answer.
2. Focus the question input, type an answer, and try deleting text.
3. Intermittently, Delete/Backspace does not edit the answer. Focus appears to be in both the question input and the chat composer.

docs.title: Markdown editor: render <details>/<summary> as collapsible sections
docs.body:
The rich Markdown editor (`vscode.markdown.editor`) shows `<details>`/`<summary>` HTML as raw source. Documents that use them, for example agent bug-fix runs that collapse the original bug report once a fix starts, can't collapse anything in the editor.

The editor should render `<details>` with a `<summary>` as a collapsible section, as GitHub does:

- Collapsed by default without `open`, expanded with `<details open>`.
- Expanding and collapsing in the editor doesn't change the file; a separate control toggles `open`, which changes the default.
- The body stays editable Markdown, and the `<details>`/`<summary>`/`</details>` tags appear as muted markup while the caret is in the section.

Implemented in `@vscode/markdown-editor` by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/428; VS Code needs to adopt the published package.

docs.title: test: resume and parallelize the WSL smoke host package downloads
docs.body:
The Windows x64 smoke step `Prepare WSL Dev Container smoke tests` timed out in three product builds today while the Azure Ubuntu mirror was degraded (494568, which passed on a job retry, 494570 and 494706). It gates every Windows x64 artifact of an official build.

## Mechanism

`wslDevContainer.ps1` downloads the apt packages on the host before apt installs them in the distribution (#345873). While the mirror is degraded it serves some package files at under 100 KB/s, or stalls on them, while its index files stay fast. The host loop then:

1. tried each package one after another, so the stalls added up;
2. gave each package two fresh attempts at 1 MB/s for 15 s, each **starting from byte 0**, so a slow connection lost everything it had fetched;
3. used `archive.ubuntu.com` as the third attempt, which answers **403** to the build agents in every failing log;
4. stopped after 4 minutes and left what it didn't get to apt, which has no minimum speed and keeps a slow connection until the step's 15-minute timeout.

In 494706 the host got 32 packages, but containerd (28 MB) and docker.io (36 MB) failed all three attempts. apt in the distribution then fetched containerd at about 86 KB/s (5.5 min), and docker.io was still downloading when the step timed out.

docs.title: build: don't report a skipped release as released
docs.body:
When the quality is frozen, `releaseBuild.ts` skips the release but then printed `Build successfully released` anyway, because that line ran on any successful exit. On a frozen quality, the `Release build` step of the scheduled 05:00 and 17:00 UTC builds reads as released even though nothing was. That cost us about an hour today, chasing why an insider "released" but never reached users.

Now `main` returns whether it released or skipped:
- **Released:** unchanged, prints `Build successfully released`.
- **Skipped (frozen):** prints `Build NOT released: quality <quality> is frozen`, adds a warning to the build summary saying it needs a manual release once the quality is unfrozen, and tags the build `release-skipped-frozen`, so it's easy to query.

The step still succeeds when skipped, as before, and the forced path (`product-release.yml` with `VSCODE_RELEASE`) never checks the freeze, so it's unchanged.

Context: roblourens hit this as this week's endgame champ. `build/azure-pipelines/**` is owned by lszomoru (CODENOTIFY), and joaomoreno wrote most of `releaseBuild.ts`.

Validation: eslint and tsc are clean on the file. Nothing in this repo or our tooling matches on the old success line.

## Summary

Prevent unrelated changes from a terminal `git pull` from appearing as agent Keep/Undo hunks in the editor.

A disk reload can replace one broad range spanning pending agent edits and unrelated upstream changes. The shared edit tracker treats that replacement as overlapping the agent edit, leaving the review baseline stale.

- If a precise comparison is unavailable, suspend editor review with the existing synchronization warning and recovery path instead of applying an incorrect baseline. File contents are preserved. docs.title: VS Code - Information Disclosure via Integrated Browser File Uploads
docs.body:
### Summary

An information disclosure vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.145.2 and earlier versions where the integrated browser’s file-upload tool could upload local files without the expected path-based approval. This could expose sensitive file contents to an attacker-controlled website.

### Details

An attacker would need to influence an agent using the integrated browser, for example through malicious page content, and cause it to upload local files. The upload tool did not apply the approval checks used by other tools when accessing files outside the workspace.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.145.3**. It applies path-aware approval to browser uploads while respecting existing explicit pre-approval. It also rejects empty, relative, and malformed upload paths before offering folder approvals or selecting files.

### Workarounds

Avoid using agent-driven integrated browser tools with untrusted websites or content until the update is installed.

### References

- The patch can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c5d31d10dce41176ce7f9ba4b3c69032422b03e5
- An advisory for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-f56j-7499-5hch
- MSRC details can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-102230

Makes the full hygiene check approximately 5x faster (69s to approximately 12-17s on a local

  it reads from disk and does not see later changes to them.

Fixes #347446

## What was wrong

When an MCP skill loads, the Copilot runtime tells the model to read the skill's supporting files (for example `template.md`) with its `read_resource` built-in tool. That read is checked against the manifest the host holds. But the Agent Host sends the runtime an `availableTools` allow-list (`COPILOT_ENABLED_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES`) that had `skill` and not `read_resource`. ### Steps to reproduce

docs.title: Model router: display name, context size, and a quieter routing line
docs.body:
Additions to model routers (`.model-router.yaml`, behind `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled`).

## Changes

- **`display-name`.** A router file can set the name the model picker shows in place of its file name. The chat's routing line and the router's notices use the same name.
- **`context-size: default | long`.** A route, or the whole router, can ask for a model's larger context window. It applies only to models that offer two sizes; a route that asks for `long` on a model with one size gets a warning from `check_model_router` and is left alone. The routing line shows the size the router asked for, such as "1M". The check tool lists each model's context sizes and whether the larger one is billed at a higher rate.
- **A chat on a long window keeps it.** The window is read from the chat's routed turns, so it holds when another router picks the next model and after a turn on a model with one size. A model the user picks by hand resets it.
- **No routing line after the first turn of a `switching: first-turn` router.** Such a router routes only the first turn, so later turns no longer show a "stayed on" line, or a "picking a model" row while the turn starts. Routers with `switching: auto` are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled` and add a router under `~/.agents/model-routers/` with `display-name: My Router`, and `context-size: long`

docs.title: Always emit compressed chunks for request.option.tools telemetry
docs.body:
## Problem

Tool definitions logged as `request.option.tools` routinely exceed the 8,192-character per-property limit. `multiplexProperties` already handles oversized values by keeping the first 8,192 characters in the original column and emitting the full value gzip + base64 compressed under the `<key>Chunk`, `<key>Chunk_2`, … family. Downstream consumers that read only the original column therefore see truncated, unparseable JSON.

## Changes

Add the tool-definition key to `ALWAYS_COMPRESSED_CHUNK_KEYS`, matching `messagesJson`, `messageText`, `diffsJSON` and `prompt`. The compressed chunk family is now always emitted, even for short values, so the backend can always read tool definitions from one place without checking the value's size.

- **Agent host** (`agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.ts`): adds both `request.option.tools` and `request_option_tools`. The agent host forwards Copilot SDK telemetry properties verbatim and does not sanitize keys, so either spelling may appear.
- **Copilot extension** (`telemetry.ts`): adds the same keys to keep both implementations aligned. In the extension, keys still contain dots when chunked and are sanitized to underscores at send time, so the wire columns are `request_option_tools` / `request_option_toolsChunk*`.

The original column's behavior is unchanged: it still carries the raw value, or its first 8,192 characters.

## Summary

docs.title: Feature Request: separate Confirm Before Close into separate Confirm Before Quit and Confirm Before Window Close settings
docs.body:
I often work with multiple VSCode windows and want to be able to close a window quickly without a confirmation using `Cmd + W` after closing all editors.  But if I set **Confirm Before Close** to `never`, VSCode quits immediately if I accidentally press `Cmd + Q`.

They should be separate settings.  Accidentally quitting is a lot more of an interruption than accidentally closing a window.

I can at least work around this sort of with

```
  { "key": "cmd+q", "command": "-workbench.action.quit" },
  { "key": "cmd+q cmd+q", "command": "workbench.action.quit" }
```

But the current design is inadequate and an option to confirm before quitting the entire app but not before closing a single window would be better.

docs.title: canvases: avoid rescanning completed history for open requests
docs.body:
Fixes #347519

`getOpenRequests` in `agentHostCanvas.ts` walked the whole chat history backward on every chat-state change, including each streaming delta, to infer which `open_canvas` calls opened which canvas. A canvas opened from the UI has no matching tool call, so the walk could never stop early and always visited every completed turn.

### What changed
- The active turn is scanned first (it still wins over completed turns, and the latest part still wins).
- The result for completed turns is cached in a `WeakMap` keyed by the `chat.turns` array. The chat reducer allocates a new `turns` array whenever completed history changes (turn end, resume, truncation, turns loaded), and streaming or tool-call updates only touch the active turn. A new array is a cache miss; nothing is retained strongly.
- The cached scan is resumable (`nextTurnIndex`) and keeps the early exit: once every requested canvas instance is resolved, older completed turns are not read, and a later request for more instances continues from where the scan stopped. So a cache miss costs no more than the previous implementation.
- Request ids, the Running/Completed/Cancelled status filter, `pending`/`succeeded` and the consumer equality function are unchanged, so reveal, focus, dismiss and restore behave as before.

Explicit open-intent protocol work is out of scope.

docs.body:
agentHost: route early subagent permissions to the subagent chat

A Copilot SDK subagent can send a permission request before the runtime bridges
the tool.execution_start event of that tool call to the parent session. The
host set parentToolCallId only from the tracked tool start. Thus the approval
went to the parent chat, and the subagent chat showed the tool as running with
no approval prompt. The permission stayed pending until the user aborted.

- Record the agent ID from each permission.requested event that the handler
  must answer.
- If the tool start is not tracked yet, use this agent ID to find the
  parentToolCallId of the pending_confirmation signal.
- Remove the recorded agent ID when the request completes or when pending
  permissions are denied.
- Add tests for the session routing and for the side-effects behavior that
  keeps the approval pending in the subagent chat.

docs.body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested; the repro requires a registered canvas provider. The repeated work is in the core canvas implementation.

### Steps to reproduce

Streaming updates should not repeatedly scan unchanged completed history. Canvas request status, reveal, focus, dismissal, and restoration behavior should remain unchanged.

docs.body:
Follow-up to a review comment on #347474 (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/347474#discussion_r4531498141), for model routers (`.model-router.yaml`, behind `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled`).

## Problem

A turn sent on a model router that makes no pick runs on the chat's current model. That happens when the router file is invalid or missing, when none of its models are available, or when the routing call fails.

While the host is running, such a turn's selection is still the router, so the chat's long context window and the router's last pick both hold. docs.body:
Fixes the main CI unit-test cascade in [495093](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=495093): every Electron and Browser unit job on every OS times out after about 70 failures.

## Mechanism

`scheduleAtNextAnimationFrame` (`dom.ts`) sets a per-window `animFrameRequested` flag and calls `window.requestAnimationFrame`. That flag only clears when the frame fires.

The four `AutomationsCardsWidget` tests use sinon `useFakeTimers()`, which also fakes `requestAnimationFrame`. Since #347444, the final `setRuns` in `run feedback survives acknowledgement and refresh until the new run session appears` splices the run-session list after the last `tickAsync`. That splice calls `eventuallyUpdateScrollDimensions` → `scheduleAtNextAnimationFrame`, which requests the frame from the **fake** clock. `clock.restore()` then drops that frame, the flag stays `true`, and no later test in the same renderer ever gets an animation frame.

## Change

A router file can be written as `playbooks` in place of `routes`, for users who think in kinds of work rather than in models:

version: 1

docs.title: chat: fix image pills flickering in sticky scroll
docs.body:
Image attachment pills in the sticky request row flicker between the thumbnail and the file-media icon while a response is being produced.

## Cause

The sticky row is rebuilt from scratch whenever its request row changes: when the response gains a content reference, when it completes, and on a re-render. Each rebuild creates the image pill anew, and a new pill:

- starts as the icon and only swaps to the thumbnail asynchronously, even when the thumbnail is already encoded and cached;
- gets an object URL of its own, so the image has to load again after the swap;
- for an image that only carries a resource, as in an agent host's history, reads the file first, which keeps the icon up for several frames.

## Change

- `src/vs/workbench/browser/chatImagePreview.ts`: a thumbnail that is already encoded is shown synchronously, and the images showing a thumbnail share one object URL, so an image that is rendered again is available at once. The URL is revoked once the thumbnail has left the cache and no image shows it. The cache now holds the latest thumbnail per cache key, so a thumbnail can be found before the bytes of the image are known.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts`: while the bytes of a resource-only image are being read, the pill shows the thumbnail of an earlier render instead of the file icon.

docs.body:
Adopts two Copilot SDK capabilities in the Agent Host. Both shipped in `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.32-preview.0, which main already uses, so this PR has no SDK bump, no new settings and no change to the generated AHP protocol types. Runtime side: github/copilot-agent-runtime#36401 (message source) and github/copilot-agent-runtime#34030 (initial permission mode).

## Message provenance

The Copilot provider sent every message without a `source`, so the runtime treated automation kickoffs and agent-to-agent messages as if the user had written them. The host now resolves who authored each message from its own state, and the provider maps that to the SDK `source`:

| Message | SDK `source` |
|---|---|
| A person's message or steering, or an artifact prompt action a person chose | omitted (the runtime's default, a person) |
| The kickoff of an automation run | `automation-<automation resource>` |
| An Agent Merge repair prompt | `automation-vscode.agentMerge` |
| A message another agent sent with `create_session` or `send_message` | `agent-<sending chat>` |
| Any other host notification, and any message whose author the host cannot identify | `system` |

- The identity comes from the session origin, the Agent Merge metadata and the delegation metadata. It never comes from message text, URI shape or a per-send ID.
- An agent keeps one ID across its kickoff, queued and steering messages

docs.title: sessions: give the held-session order test one clock
docs.body:
Fixes an order-dependent flake in `Sessions - SessionsList › groupSessionsForList › inbox lists held sessions directly without changing their custom membership`, added in #347484. It failed in a def 700 Flaky Tests run ([495184](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=495184)) with:

```
{"rows":["b","a"],"membership":"saved"} deepStrictEqual {"rows":["a","b"],"membership":"saved"}
```

## Mechanism

The test builds `a` and `b` with `buildTestSession(spec)`, whose `now` defaults to `Date.now()`, so each session reads the clock separately. The list sorts by `SessionsSorting.Created`, newest first, with a stable tie. Usually both reads land in the same millisecond, the tie keeps `[a, b]`, and the test passes. When the millisecond ticks between the two calls, `b` is newer, and the rows come back `[b, a]`.

## Proof

Building `b` one millisecond later (`buildTestSession(..., Date.now() + 1)`) fails locally with exactly the CI assertion above.

## Fix

Both sessions come from one `now`, and `b` is created a minute earlier, so `[a, b]` follows from the session data instead of a tie. Test-only. The assertion and the behavior under test are unchanged.

## Validation

- `sessionsList.test.ts`: 502 passing in Chromium and 502 in WebKit.
- The test 10 times in a row in Chromium: passed every time.
- eslint is clean.

> Authored with Copilot

docs.title: Fix Copilot Agent Host model switches that require compaction
docs.body:
Fixes #347559.

When an existing conversation does not fit the newly selected model, the runtime returns `confirmation_required` and keeps the previous model active. The SDK's `setModel()` discards that result, so Agent Host currently records the requested selection as applied and can send the next turn to the old model.

Use the structured `rpc.model.switchTo` result, resolve a required-compaction confirmation once, and update applied selection only after the runtime commits the requested model. Compaction gets a bounded inference-sized deadline; ordinary control RPCs keep their short deadline. Rejected, deferred, mismatched and cancelled outcomes block continuation.

The switch has its own cancellation lifetime because selection runs before `send()` resets the preceding turn's abort token. Abort/disposal stop waiting, cancelled in-flight operations require resynchronization, and timeout cleanup releases cancellation listeners even if an RPC never settles. Existing Auto, reasoning and context-tier behavior is covered.

A picker-driven switch is treated as intent to compact when required. This adds no provider-specific behavior, setting, SDK upgrade or AHP change.

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`

Sandbox grant confirmations expose opaque absolute `.copilot/session-state/<SDK ID>` paths. These make it difficult to identify which session owns the requested storage and which file or directory the agent wants to access.

## Desired behavior

Display session-storage paths using a reusable, sandbox-independent helper, initially adopted only by sandbox confirmations. For example:

This tracks a presentation feature, not a change to permission scope or enforcement. Keep existing Input and terminal presentation; Input already exposes the original tool arguments. Do not add a separate Full Path disclosure or expander. Broader adoption of the helper is outside this issue.

docs.title: Model router: tell the routing decision what comes with a request
docs.body:
Builds on #347526. Model routers (`.model-router.yaml`, behind `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled`).

## Change

A router's routing decision sees only the user's message today. A short message such as "fix this" or "review" says little on its own. The decision is now also told a few facts about the turn:

- **What is attached:** how many attachments of each kind (image, document, selection and so on), and how many lines are selected. A message that is only an attachment, with no text, is now routed by it instead of going to the first route.
- **How the user asked the agent to work:** Plan or Autopilot mode, and the custom agent they chose.
- **Where the work happens:** the workspace folder's name and its GitHub repository, how many files have uncommitted changes when there are ten or more, and whether the branch has an open pull request. These are read for the folder the chat runs in, which for a peer chat can be another one than its session's, and a pull request counts only when it belongs to the folder's current branch.
- **What each model is:** its cost category and context window, next to the route it belongs to.

This also lets a route's `when` refer to those facts, which could not work before:

```yaml
routes:
  - model: claude-sonnet-5
    when: Any request that none of the other routes covers.
  - model: claude-haiku-5.5
    when: The request comes with an image, such as

docs.title: agentHost: hosts enable multipleChatProviders during initialize instead of after a reconnect
docs.body:
Lets a VS Code client tell an Agent Host about `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` during `initialize`, so turning multi-harness on no longer forces a reconnect. The default stays off; turning it on in Insiders is a follow-up once a published host includes this.

- With the setting on, the client sets `_meta['vscode.multipleChatProviders']` in `initialize`, and the host turns its gate on before answering, so the handshake already advertises `multipleChatProviders`. Previously the client re-initialized each remote connection (closing its transport) once its mirrored setting reached the host: an SSH host without an SSH config host can't reconnect, and a Dev Container connection lost the authentication in flight.
- The flag follows the same rules as a client `RootConfigChanged` setting the property: it is ignored on unauthenticated and passive relay lanes, and while the property is read-only or owned by the extension's root config overlay.
- Hosts that ignore the flag behave as before (the client re-initializes once).

Builds on #347377 (experiment-controlled settings).

### Validation

- eslint, hygiene, `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js'`: 17720 passing, 75 pending (includes a regression test for direct and relay lanes)

docs.title: dev: Load nested ESM packages correctly through the node_modules redirector
docs.body:
When running the server out of sources (e.g. `server-main` with `--agent-host-port` as a dev remote agent host), the remote agent host fails to register as a GitHub environment:

```
TypeError: hpke.DhkemX25519HkdfSha256 is not a constructor
    at createHpkeCipherSuite (out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlAuthentication.js)
```

The dev-only node_modules redirector in `bootstrap-import.ts` maps `@hpke/core` to its `exports["."].import` entry (`esm/mod.js`), but derived the module format from the package's root `package.json`, which has no `type`. The ESM marker lives in a nested `esm/package.json`, so the entry was loaded as CommonJS and its named exports were lost. Built servers don't use the redirector and are not affected.

Changes:
- Determine the format from the `package.json` closest to the entry, stopping at the package root, like Node.js does.
- Redirect to the package's real path, like Node.js' default resolution. Otherwise the now-ESM entry can't resolve its own dependency (`@hpke/common`) from pnpm's symlinked location.

Validation:
- Imported every root `package.json` dependency through the compiled redirector before and after the change: the only difference is `@hpke/core`, which now exposes its named exports. The same four packages fail to import in both runs (type-only, asset-only or browser-only packages).

docs.body:
### Description

Installed agent plugins end up in two separate locations:

.copilot\installed-plugins
agentPlugins\…\<hash>

As a result, the agent has to search both directories to discover a plugin’s files (instructions, prompts, agents, skills, etc.), which makes plugin resolution more complex and error-prone.

#### Expected behavior
Plugins are installed into a single, well-defined location, so the agent (and the user) only needs to look in one place.

#### Actual behavior
Plugins are split between two folders with different layouts (plain name vs. hash-based), and the agent has to search both.

#### Impact

Unnecessary overhead and potential inconsistency when the agent looks up plugin content.
Confusing for users who want to inspect, debug or manually edit installed plugins.
Risk of duplicates or stale copies, e.g. after an update or uninstall.

docs.title: build: only publish CI log artifacts when jobs fail
docs.body:
The 1ES pipeline templates run SDL binary analysis (AntiMalware, secret scanning, PREfast, TSA upload, SDL log publishing) for every `templateContext.outputs` entry, using the output's `condition` as the condition for those steps. The CI test jobs publish `.build/logs` on every run, so every green CI job paid for those scans. The crash-dump and `node_modules` outputs, which already use `failed()`, skip them.

This changes the `Publish Log Files` output of the CI test jobs (`product-build-{linux,darwin,win32}-ci.yml`) to publish only when the job does not succeed:

- Linux and macOS: `succeededOrFailed()` → `failed()`
- Windows: `always()` → `not(succeeded())`, so logs of cancelled or timed-out jobs are still published

Product builds (`*-test.yml`) are unchanged. The smoke-tests skill now notes that CI log artifacts only exist for failed jobs.

**Trade-off:** green CI runs no longer upload test logs to Azure DevOps. Nothing in the repository consumes them; they are used for debugging failures, which still publish them.

**Expected impact** (from recent CI build timelines): the injected binary analysis takes about 80 s per Windows CI job and about 30 s per Linux CI job, and is negligible on macOS. Windows jobs are almost always on the critical path, so the build should finish over a minute sooner, with a corresponding reduction in agent time.

docs.title: Allow VS Code Team Tools to use any API proposal
docs.body:
Fixes #347598

Product builds only let an extension use the API proposals listed for it in `product.json#extensionEnabledApiProposals` (in `microsoft/vscode-distro`). Internal extensions that adopt new proposals often, such as VS Code Team Tools, need a distro change for every new proposal.

This PR hard-codes a small list of extensions that may use every API proposal they declare in their own `package.json`, in every build:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/extensionsProposedApiExceptions.ts
export const extensionsAllowedAnyApiProposal: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
	'ms-vscode.vscode-team-tools',
]);
```

- The list lives in its own file, owned by @alexr00 via `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so adding another extension requires API owner review. It deliberately is not a `product.json` setting, so a distro change alone cannot grant an extension all proposals.
- `ExtensionsProposedApi` checks this list before the `product.json` list. Unknown proposal names are still dropped with an error. All other extensions behave as before.
- New unit tests in `extensionsProposedApi.test.ts`.

Follow-up: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-distro/pull/1485 removes Team Tools' now redundant `extensionEnabledApiProposals` entry (which would otherwise make the `package.json` linter report its other proposals). It must merge after this PR.

docs.title: sessions: keep chat composer visible above on-screen keyboard on tablet viewports (#347570)
docs.body:
Fixes #347570

### Problem
In the web Sessions/Agents window (`/agents`) on Android or iPadOS tablets (viewport width 640px–1024px, classified as `tablet`), opening the on-screen keyboard caused the chat composer to remain at the bottom of the layout viewport, hiding it behind the virtual keyboard.

While #332146 addressed this for `phone` viewports, the fix was gated strictly on `viewportClass === 'phone'` in two places:
1. `Workbench.registerLayoutListeners`: only triggered `this.layout()` on `visualViewport` `resize` if `this.layoutPolicy.viewportClass.get() === 'phone'`.
2. `Workbench.layout()`: only computed `_mainContainerDimension` via `getMobileViewportDimension` if `currentClass === 'phone'`.

On tablet-class viewports (`640 <= width < 1024`), the layout viewport remained unadjusted and the visual viewport resize was ignored, obscuring the composer beneath the virtual keyboard.

### Solution
- Updated the `visualViewport.resize` listener in `Workbench.registerLayoutListeners` to trigger `layout()` whenever `this.layoutPolicy.viewportClass.get() !== 'desktop'` (handling both `phone` and `tablet` viewports).
- In `Workbench.layout()`, compute `this._mainContainerDimension` using `getMobileViewportDimension(...)` whenever `currentClass !== 'desktop'` while maintaining `PHONE_LAYOUT` toggling specifically for `phone`.
- Added unit tests in `mobileVisualViewport.test.ts` ve

docs.title: sessions: side pane keeps its frame when it is shown again
docs.body:
In the Agents window, toggling the side pane closed and open again (Toggle Side Panel) leaves the side pane card 2px too large. Its right and bottom borders run under the Session Activity Bar column and past the bottom of the window. This is easiest to see in a high contrast theme.

### Cause

`MainEditorPart.layout` subtracts the side pane's frame inset, which `getSidePaneFrameInset` reads from the container's `noeditorpane` class. `setEditorHidden` and `_setAuxiliaryBarHidden` show the grid node first, and the grid lays the part out synchronously. Only afterwards do they call `_updateEditorPaneVisibilityClass()`. So the reveal is laid out while `noeditorpane` is still set: the inset is 0 and the 300×1032 cell gets 300×1032 content instead of 298×1030. Nothing lays it out again. The Sessions Part's right margin (`getSessionsPartCardMarginRight`) reads the same class.

This became visible with #347310, which made the side pane frame depend on that class. The ordering itself is older.

### Fix

Update the class from the editor part's `onDidVisibilityChange`. `SplitView` fires it after it records the node's new visibility and before it lays out the views, so the class is correct for the layout. ## Bug

In a chat window (session or chat **Open in > New Window**), swap the chat and editor parts by dragging the editor part's grabber to the left of the chat. Then hide the editor and show it again. The editor comes back on the **right**, the default side, instead of where the user put it.

docs.body:
A chat link opened from a canvas in a chat window now opens in that chat window, by the same rules as clicking that link in the chat window's chat view.

## Repro

1. Open a chat in its own chat window (Open in > New Window).
2. Open a canvas in that chat window's editor area.
3. In the canvas, use a button or link that opens another chat.

docs.title: agentHost: treat dormant canvas extensions as enabled and settled
docs.body:
The Copilot runtime can now start an extension lazily ([github/copilot-agent-runtime#28873](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/28873)). An extension that declares its tools and canvases in an `extension.json` sidecar with `"initialization": "module"` is advertised without starting its process, and it starts on first tool use or canvas open. Until then, `session.extensions.list` reports it as `dormant`, a status that means the extension is enabled.

VS Code mapped `dormant` to `unknown`, as [#347239](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/347239) notes. As a result, the Canvases view labeled these canvases **Not Active** although they are ready to open. It also never pruned their stale cached canvases.

### Changes

- The agent host and the AHP client pass `dormant` through instead of turning it into `unknown`. Older clients still map it to `unknown`, and hosts that never send it are unaffected.

  - **Confirming an enable after a reconciliation error.** An enabled lazy extension stays `dormant` after reconciliation, so it now counts as applied instead of failed.
  - **Merging duplicate inventory entries.** When the runtime lists one ID twice as `running` and `dormant`, the merged status is now `running` instead of `unknown`. Other combination

docs.title: chat-lib - fix pipeline
docs.body:
The Linux and Windows jobs of the `chat-lib` Azure pipeline fail in **📂 Extract chat-lib**. Copilot and chat-lib are now members of the root pnpm workspace, so `pnpm rebuild` loads the root `.pnpmfile.mjs`. Its `updateConfig` hook passes the root's `nativeBuild` settings (Electron runtime, target, and `disturl`) to every install script. `@parcel/watcher` and `keytar` then build from source against Electron and request the Electron headers from `electronjs.org`, which network isolation blocks on those agents. The macOS job passes because it can download them.

chat-lib runs in Node.js, so the rebuild now passes `--ignore-pnpmfile` and builds the native modules for the running Node.js. The preceding `pnpm install` keeps the pnpmfile: it runs with `--ignore-scripts`, and the pnpmfile only sets environment variables for scripts, so it doesn't change the installed layout.

The same change applies to the `chat-lib` and `chat-lib next` pipelines (`build-chat-lib.yml`, `test-chat-lib.yml`, `npm-package-next.yml`) and the `test-chat-lib` GitHub action.

## How to test

- `chat-lib - Test (Linux)` and `chat-lib - Test (Windows)` on this PR run the changed rebuild command: passed.
- Not yet run: the `chat-lib` Azure pipeline (definition 683) on this branch, which is the network-isolated environment that failed.

docs.title: terminal: use bracketed paste for inserted paths
docs.body:
Fixes #347647.

Dropped paths currently reach terminal applications as typed input, so paste-aware applications can miss them; Claude Code leaves a dropped screenshot path as text.

Pass `!shouldExecute` to `sendText` from `sendPath`, matching the existing `runCommand` policy:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/75436fa46d2d234409ae10401414954ddc9e1efb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L1073-L1075

This covers drops onto both the terminal and its tabs. Bracketing requires the application to enable the mode and `terminal.integrated.ignoreBracketedPasteMode` to be off. The shared `sendText` guard also makes existing paste callers, including `runCommand`, honor that setting. Run Active File and shell quoting retain their behavior.

### Prior discussion

In [#153592](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/153592#issuecomment-1169174534), Tyriar identified paste wrapping as a way to avoid triggering keybindings. #154567 applied it broadly; #154958 reverted that after the control-sequence regression in #154863, requiring an opt-in. #316098 subsequently reused the non-executing-text policy.

This applies that existing opt-in at the path-insertion boundary: dropped paths gain paste semantics while Run Active File and control-sequence input keep their existing behavior.

### Validation

- Reproduced the drop/paste byte difference in VS Code 1.145.2

docs.body:
## Summary

- start the Mark as Done confetti animation when an individual session archive is requested
- start the matching accessibility signal at the same optimistic point
- preserve post-confirmation, post-success animation timing for group actions
- preserve existing post-success behavior for unrelated menu action animations

## Root cause

Marking an Agent session as done updates the session's archived state optimistically. The Sessions list reacts to that state change immediately and removes the row from its active section.

The confetti animation followed a different timeline. The shared `MenuEntryActionViewItem` captured the button's position on click, awaited the complete archive command, and only then created the animation overlay. By that point, the optimistic list update had already removed the row. The visual confirmation therefore appeared later at the former button position, disconnected from the action that caused it.

In the supplied recording, the first visible confetti appeared approximately 0.82–1.01 seconds after mouse-up. The accessibility confetti signal also ran after the archive await, so its timing would diverge once the visual animation became optimistic.

## Fix

The shared menu action retains its post-success behavior and exposes the resolved click animation through a protected getter for specialized view items.

Fixes #347669

## Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9f54646-7896-4dba-ac4d-d7df91bf1be1

## After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f1c45f2-9575-4fa6-a4e5-346532e643cb

In the Agents window, when two chats of one session are shown side by side as chat groups in a pane (for example a nested chat opened beside its parent), the mode and approvals pickers of **both** chat inputs showed the values of the chat that had focus last. Focus the nested chat (Interactive) and both say Interactive; focus the parent (Autopilot) and both say Autopilot. Choosing a value in the unfocused chat acted on the other chat too. Two different sessions side by side were not affected.

**Cause:** the pickers read `ISessionHost.chat`. A chat group created its chat view in a scope that only overrides the context key service, so they got the pane's host, whose chat is the pane's single chat and follows the focused group.

**Fix:** `ChatGroupView` gives the chat view it creates for a started chat a `SessionHost` that shows the group's own chat. That host is nested in the pane's host (`parent`) and is not registered. So commands, which find hosts by `commandContext`, pane activation (`activateHostPane` walks `parent`) and host lookups still find the pane, and the group's header and tab bar keep the pane's host. docs.body:
When two chats of the same session are shown side by side in one session pane (for example a nested chat opened beside its parent), both chat inputs show the mode and approvals of whichever chat had focus last. Two different sessions side by side are not affected.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the Agents window, start a session in **Autopilot**.
2. Start a nested session from it (**New Nested Session**, ⌘T), switch it to **Interactive**, and send a message.
3. In the sessions list, right-click the parent session and choose **Open in** > **Split View**, so both chats show side by side in one pane.
4. Click into the nested chat's input, then into the parent's.

## Expected

The nested chat's input shows **Interactive** and the parent's shows **Autopilot**, whichever has focus.

## Actual

Both inputs show the focused chat's mode: focus the nested chat and both say Interactive; focus the parent and both say Autopilot. The approvals picker reads the same state, so choosing a value in the unfocused chat changes the other chat.

## Video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6b07521-53f3-4fe5-965e-83b08ad24309

Part 1 shows two different sessions side by side (correct). Part 2 shows two chats of one session side by side (wrong). The yellow "Really: …" labels mark each chat's actual mode.

## Summary

Update the shared signing wrapper for the stdin authentication contract used by EsrpCodeSigning 6.1.3 and ESRP CLI 6.0.26.

- Replace encrypted token/key files with `systemAccessTokenSource: "stdin"` and a newline-terminated token on a dedicated pipe.

- Preserve Windows signing stall detection and macOS download-stall resubmission, delivering authentication separately to every new process.
- Cover Windows, macOS, and Linux signing entrypoints, including macOS resubmission, with fake-process regression tests.

Snap packaging is intentionally unchanged; its Store connectivity failure should be retried before making a separate change.

The pipeline requests `EsrpCodeSigning@6`, allowing Azure Pipelines to pick up newer minor and patch versions without a repository change. The previous task/CLI combination (6.1.1 / 6.0.12) accepted encrypted token files; the newer combination (6.1.3 / 6.0.26) requires the system access token on stdin. Our custom signing wrapper still used the token-file contract, which dates back to November 2024, so the tool update made that existing wrapper incompatible across platforms.

docs.title: Fixes #347662: chat windows: terminals take their saved height back as the window grows
docs.body:
Fixes #347662

### Repro
Chat window with the terminals under the editor → Chat Only → make the window shorter than the terminals' height → show the editor (the terminals are squeezed) → make the window taller: the terminals stay squeezed until reload, although the saved height is intact. This happens for a height the user dragged and for the default height alike.

### Root cause
`PartGrid` keeps the current size of a `keepsSize` cell (the terminals) on resize, so once the terminals were squeezed, nothing re-applied their height when the room came back. The behavior is long-standing (the `keepSizes` logic comes from #346039).

### Fix
`ChatWindowGrid.layout()` gives the terminals their preferred height back when the window grows and they are shorter than it. The preference is the height the user gave them; when the user never set one, it is the default height the terminals had before they were squeezed (remembered while they are visible, forgotten when they hide). No `PartGrid` API change.
- Only when the terminals' own line is a column, so `height` is really their axis (a terminals cell moved into a horizontal row would otherwise resize the whole row and squeeze an unrelated part).
- Not while a sash drag is in progress.
- Only when the window grows, so an arrangement change (such as a part dropped at an edge) that shrinks the terminals on purpose isn't undone by the next layo

docs.title: agentHost: let the setup write settle in the shared content revision test
docs.body:
Fixes the main CI failure since #347393 merged (13:11 UTC Nov 11): `CopilotAgent › publishes shared content revisions through customizations and preserves them across enablement` failed in macOS arm64 `Unit (node.js)` in 5 of 6 main CI runs and in Windows `Unit (Electron)` in 4 of 6 (495325, 495336, 495375, 495408, 495417). It never failed on Linux.

## Mechanism

The test writes `.plugin/plugin.json` through `createInMemoryFileService` and then creates the agent. `InMemoryFileSystemProvider` reports writes later, through `_fireSoon` on a 5 ms `setTimeout`.

While settling, each plugin controller's `_readRuntimePluginContents` registers a recursive watcher on the plugin root. Its `onDidFilesChange` handler calls `invalidateRuntimePluginContents()`, which generates a new content revision, then runs an unawaited `publishWhenSettled()`.

So the result depends on whether the setup write's ADDED event lands before or after those watchers exist:
- **Before** (most local runs, Linux): nothing happens, and the test sees exactly the 4 publishes it expects.
- **After** (slower agents): the revision changes behind the test, and each controller publishes once more. That gives the two CI shapes: extra `{ enabled: false, revision }` entries (macOS node), or the last two entries carrying a different revision than `afterInstall` (Windows Electron), and `activationPreserved: false` in 495325.

In a request bubble with inline attachment pills (`chat.inlineAttachments.enabled`), the labels of pills and slash commands sat below the baseline of the request text beside them: pills by about a pixel and slash commands by about two at the default font size. docs.title: Model router: one list of routes, with optional names and guidance
docs.body:
Builds on #347526 and #347565. Model routers (`.model-router.yaml`, behind `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled`).

## Change

A router could be written in two ways: as `routes`, or as `playbooks` with `roles` (preview). The second way needed five more keys (`playbooks`, `main`, `roles`, `uses`, and a role's `agent`), and its own code to add helper agents to a session. This change makes a router one list of routes, as simple or as detailed as the user wants:

```yaml
version: 1
description: Opus for feature work and bug fixes, Haiku for quick questions.
routes:
  - name: feature
    model: [claude-opus-5.5, claude-opus-5]
    when: Building something new or changing behavior across files.
    effort: high
    guidance: Plan first. Before you finish, have the code-review agent check the change.
  - name: quick
    model: claude-haiku-5.5
    when: Questions, lookups and small one-file edits.
```

- A route needs only `model` and `when`, as before.
- `name` (optional) is shown in the chat's routing line. Routes with a name are told apart by it, so two of them can use the same model, for example at two effort levels. A route without a name is still identified by its model.
- `guidance` (optional) says how the user wants that kind of work done. It is given to the main agent of a chat whose first message is routed there, in the system message, and can name skills and custom agents to u

docs.body:
Main CI has been failing since 495435 (`5cfb03d692`) on all three OSes, in Electron and Chromium unit. Reruns can't fix it, so every official build from that commit on fails as well.

```
AI customization shortcuts header › "before each" hook for "keeps both edges clickable while the hover remains inset"
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'managementSections')
```

docs.title: [Perf] agentHost: fix heap OOMs from history restore and Codex output streaming
docs.body:
The Agent Host process crashes with V8 heap out-of-memory errors. Investigation found two places where it builds up unbounded data within seconds.

## Copilot: restoring session history

Restoring a Copilot chat (`readCopilotSessionEvents`) pages through the runtime's whole persisted event log and holds every event in memory before rebuilding turns. The runtime returns stored binary assets inline, including in `hook.start` events, which repeat tool arguments and results. In long sessions, hook and permission events can make up most of the returned data. This happens on resume, so a host that crashes here can crash again on every restart while a window reopens the chat.

Nothing that consumes the restored events reads hook or permission events, so they are now filtered out of each page as it arrives, alongside the system messages that were already filtered. Images in tool results are unchanged.

## Codex: streamed command output

Every Codex command or file-change output delta republished the complete accumulated output in a `ChatToolCallContentChanged` action, so data dispatched, serialized and queued for each client grew with the square of a command's output. While output streams, only the newest inline-limit (80k) characters are now shown. That text is built from the previous bounded text so the full output isn't copied on every delta. docs.title: Fixes #347661: Chat windows: restore Chat Only mode after relaunch
docs.body:
Fixes #347661

### Problem
Chat window → Chat Only → quit → relaunch comes back Side by Side. Arrangement and sizes are restored; only the mode is lost.

### Root cause
While a restored chat window opens its main-part editors, each `EDITOR_OPEN` event was treated as a user open: `trackMainPartEditors` called `_showMainPart()` → `showBoth()`, overwriting the remembered mode. Defect since the feature was introduced (c8110cefee9, #345683).

### Fix
- Restored editors are opened one by one; a synchronous per-call marker (`restoreMainPartEditor`) makes only the open events fired by the restore itself not count as user opens. The marker is cleared before any async wait and on throw, so a real user open right after (or during) the restore still shows the editor, including for the same shared cached input.
- A window whose main part restores empty shows Chat Only transiently, without saving it as the mode. The saved mode is kept, so the first editor opened later brings it back.

### Tradeoffs (disclosed)
- Restoring editors one by one replaces the batched `openEditors`, so tab title updates are O(N²) in the number of restored editors of one window, once per window open.
- When the saved active editor is not the first, the first editor activates transiently before the saved one.
- Restored editors now honor the saved active editor (the old batch forced all but the first inactive).

docs.title: auth: Replace dynamic auth client rejected during silent refresh
docs.body:
Refs #321834

### Problem

Some authorization servers expire dynamically registered OAuth clients, for example after about a day. When that happens:

1. A background (silent) token refresh gets `invalid_client` from the token endpoint.
2. Because the refresh is silent, `DynamicAuthProvider` intentionally does not register a new client. It logs `Client ID (...) was invalid while silently refreshing the token.` and drops the token.
3. When the user signs in, there is no token left to refresh, so the error is never seen again. VS Code opens the authorization page with the rejected client ID.
4. The authorization server shows an error page instead of a sign-in prompt and doesn't redirect back to VS Code, so VS Code can't react. The user has to run **Authentication: Remove Dynamic Authentication Providers**, which removes every dynamic provider, not just the broken one.

### Fix

- When a silent refresh gets `invalid_client`, `DynamicAuthProvider` records the rejected client ID.
- At the start of the next `createSession`, if the current client ID is the one that was rejected, it registers a replacement before opening the browser, then clears the record.

This keeps the existing rules:

- A silent refresh still never registers a new client. The existing test `does not rotate the client while silently refreshing a token` is unchanged.
- A client is only replaced after the server has r

docs.title: Register test iframes with their own window IDs
docs.body:
Test-only alternative to #347523 for the stale animation frame problem.

## Mechanism

`scheduleAtNextAnimationFrame` in `dom.ts` keeps its queue and its "frame requested" flag per window ID. Iframes that tests create are never registered, so their windows have no `vscodeWindowId` and all of them share the same `undefined` slot. When a test removes its iframe while a frame is still pending for it, that frame never runs, the flag for the shared slot stays set, and every later test iframe in the same renderer stops getting animation frames.

Main CI runs the whole unit suite in one renderer, so this shows up there and in product builds depending on test order, for example the auxiliary-window clipping assertions in `WorkbenchSizeService` and `OverlayWebview` (the WebKit failures in build 495183). PR CI only runs affected tests, so it rarely sees it.

- New `registerTestIframe(iframe)` helper in `src/vs/base/test/browser/testWindow.ts`. It gives the iframe window a unique ID with `ensureCodeWindow` and registers it with `registerWindow`, which is what the auxiliary window service does for real windows. Disposing the registration fires `onDidUnregisterWindow`, which clears that window's animation frame state.

- **Re-evaluate only on added or removed sessions.** A chat window chat re-ran its session lookup (`getSessionForChatResource`) on every `onDidChangeSessions` event, including each change while any session's turn streams. docs.title: Workbench: let a workspace folder switch to an alternate location
docs.body:
## Summary

Lets a single-folder workspace switch its folder to an **alternate location** while the workspace keeps its **identity**: the folder's own location at the time the window opened it. This is phase 1 (session-only). Persistence across reload/restart (P2) and the Agents provider/trigger (P3) are follow-ups.

Issue: no tracking issue (internal design work); this PR is part of a stack with #347766 (persistence) and #347767 (working sets).

### Concept
- `IWorkspaceFolder.uri` is where the folder is now. `WorkspaceFolder`/`IWorkspaceFolderData` are unchanged.
- `IWorkspace.uri` (required, declared right after `id`) is the workspace's own location in every state: the configuration file for multi-root, the folder's own (primary) location for single-folder, `undefined` for empty. Unlike `folders[i].uri` (where a folder is now) it does not change at an alternate location. `Workspace` stores it (derived when omitted), `update()` copies it and `toJSON` includes it; `toWorkspaceIdentifier(workspace)` derives the identifier from `configuration`/`uri`. The extension host payload is unchanged.

Follow-up to #342963. `agentHost.processError` tells us how the agent host process died (exit code, Electron reason, stderr fatal signature, exit path), but not what the host or the machine was doing. ## Cause

[Mermaid 12.0.0](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.0.0) made ELK the default layout for flowchart, state, class, ER, requirement and use case diagrams. # Support repository-defined ambiguity resolution and approval workflows

## Summary

Allow repositories to customize, extend, or replace the default `ask_user` experience with repository-defined Skills and approval protocols.

Repositories can already influence how work is performed through instructions and Skills. The same should be possible for how ambiguity is resolved, approvals are obtained, and human-AI decisions are made.

## Background

I have been using a custom ambiguity-resolution protocol since before `ask_user` existed.

Over time that protocol evolved into a repository Skill called
`gated-alignment`. It has served as the primary human-in-the-loop workflow
for AI-assisted changes and has required very little evolution over time.

The protocol was designed around a simple observation: ambiguity resolution
is not just about collecting an answer from the operator. It is an
opportunity for the AI and the human to develop a shared understanding of
the problem before deciding how to proceed.

When ambiguity is encountered, the Skill requires the model to present:

- multiple viable options
- rationale for each option
- trade-offs
- expected impacts
- a recommendation

This gives the operator a much better understanding of what is actually
being decided and what alternatives exist.

More importantly, it also improves the quality of the model's reasoning.

docs.title: Control both origin hashes in the WebviewElement stale-mount test
docs.body:
Fixes the macOS arm64 WebKit unit failure in main CI build 495597: `WebviewElement ignores an earlier mount whose origin hash finishes after a remount` failed with `afterSecondMount: 0` (expected 1). The test was added today in #346646.

## Mechanism

The test delays the first `mountTo`'s origin hash with a deferred, but the second `mountTo` falls through to the real `parentOriginHash`, which uses `crypto.subtle.digest`. The test then waits a single `timeout(0)` before counting `src` updates. The digest resolves on its own schedule, and on WebKit it isn't always done after one macrotask, so no `src` was set yet.

## Change

Test-only. Both mounts now get deferred hashes. The test completes the second one first, checks that it set `src` once, then completes the stale first one and checks it's ignored. Ordering is now set by the test, not by digest timing. The product change from #346646 is unchanged.

## Validation

Local Electron runs of `webviewElement.test.ts`:
- With this change: 45 passing, 8 runs in a row.
- Product guard from #346646 removed (`this._mountId === mountId` check): the test fails, so it still covers the fix.
- Real digest slowed by 20 ms to simulate WebKit: the test on `main` fails with the same `afterSecondMount: 0` as 495597, and this version passes.
- eslint and `tsc --noEmit` are clean for the touched file.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineer

docs.title: agentHost: recover queued Mission Control prompts after reconnect
docs.body:
Queued Mission Control prompts can retain a disposed connection's credential source and fail with `Authentication connection has ended` before reaching the provider.

Keep unsent prompts pending until their original relay client authenticates with the same principal on a writable connection and successfully resubscribes to the exact chat. Capture credentials before consuming the message; disposed scopes remain unusable, and other clients or chats cannot become fallback sponsors.

Pending messages also prevent idle session eviction. Credential sources without a renewal path retain the normal visible send-failure behavior instead of blocking the queue indefinitely. Credential events retry only messages already waiting for authentication and do not restart queues paused by cancellation, failure or rejection.

Regression coverage exercises disconnected queues and late steering, authenticated reconnect and fresh initialization, owner/client/chat/passive-connection isolation, credential capture, listener cleanup, and pending intent surviving idle release and residency pressure. A live Mission Control UI flow was not run.
