docs.title: Workbench: keep the folder location across reload and restart
docs.body:
Replaces #347752, which was closed by an accidental merge into its base branch; no code reached main.

 

Stacked on #347736 (base is its branch).

Persists the alternate folder location of a single-folder window across reload and restart.

- The window state and the load configuration carry `{uri, label, providerId}` per window (restore-last-session only, never for remote windows).
- The window starts directly at the alternate location: `WorkspaceService.initialize` gets the primary and the alternate. Nothing is trusted at startup; trust is whatever is already persisted for that URI. The location is statted first, and a missing one starts at the primary.
- `FolderLocationPersistenceContribution` re-validates through the providers, waiting up to ~10 s for them to register. If no provider confirms it, the window returns to the primary and notifies. Until confirmed, the status entry, `${folderLocation}`, Explorer label and command center stay hidden.
- The last location is also remembered per primary folder in main-process state (written on every switch, cleared on return to the primary or a failed restore). A fresh open of that folder (`code <folder>`, recents, File > Open) starts at its last location and goes through the same stat and provider validation, with fallback to the primary plus a notification. Opening a worktree path directly is an ordinary folder open of that path.

docs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Agent-generated on behalf of @sbatten (AI assistant using Copilot SDK in VS Code). Draft until @sbatten reviews it.

Fixes #347580

## What

Extension commands contributed to the chat input toolbars, such as `chat/input/status`, did nothing when clicked, and no error was shown. This PR makes them run, in both the Chat view and the Agents window composer.

## Why

The toolbars passed a context holding the live `ChatWidget` to every menu command. Built-in commands run in-process and worked. For an extension command, the arguments are serialized to the extension host, and `ChatWidget` refers back to itself (`ChatWidget` → `ChatInputPart` → `ChatWidget`). `JSON.stringify` therefore threw before the request was sent, and `ActionRunner` swallowed the error. - Its `toJSON` serializes to the chat view context that chat title menus already send.

- RPC, `MainThreadCommands` and the extension host are unchanged. The extension host already replaces chat view contexts with `null` for extension commands, so these commands now run and receive `null`, as chat title menu commands do.

docs.title: chat: Don't offer Copilot Max an upgrade for models it lacks
docs.body:
Fixes #346540

## What

When curated Copilot models are missing from a Copilot Max subscriber's model list, the Chat model picker shows them under **Upgrade for More Models** with **Upgrade** links. Max is the highest individual plan, so this PR shows those models as **Unavailable** instead, with no upgrade prompt.

## Why

`getUnavailableReason` gave every plan except Business and Enterprise the `upgrade` reason, so Max was treated like Free or Pro. Max subscribers were told to upgrade to models their plan couldn't unlock, which sends them to a dead end.

## How

- `getUnavailableReason` returns a new `unavailable` reason for Max. Other plans are unchanged.
- `createUnavailableModelItem` handles every reason in one exhaustive `switch`. `unavailable` gets a plain label and an untrusted hover with no command link. The "Upgrade for More Models" heading already appears only when every reason is `upgrade`, so Max no longer gets it.
- Adds snapshot tests for Max, Pro, Pro+ and the Business update and admin cases, plus a `PickerMaxPlanMissingModels` component fixture.

This changes only how missing models are labelled. Why the reporter's account was missing them wasn't reproducible and isn't addressed here.

default account accepts a session with only one of these scopes. Thus, users with an old session

- 49 insertions

## Changes Made

- Accumulate successful retained-history deletions in batches of 50 before persisting durable state.
- Flush the final partial batch before completion or failure.
- Keep backend deletion I/O outside the automation mutation queue.
- Add a 100-session storage-write regression.

## Measurements

For deleting 100 retained sessions, the deterministic regression counts full durable-state storage writes:

- Before: 102 storage writes
- After: 4 storage writes

docs.title: chat: wait on the host frame in the WebKit HTML preview layout tests
docs.body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-engineering#4577

Fixes the main CI failure in [495712](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=495712): on macOS WebKit unit, two `ChatMarkdownContentPart › HTML previews` tests from #347388 time out.

- `keeps a viewport-height body minimum stable while auto-sizing`
- `preserves body grid layout, ID selectors and sticky navigation`

## Mechanism

Both tests await `frame.contentWindow!.requestAnimationFrame(...)` on the preview iframe. The iframe is created with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and without `allow-scripts`, matching the preview's no-script policy. **WebKit never runs animation frame callbacks for a document that can't run scripts**, so the promise never resolves. Chromium does run them, which is why PR CI and the Chromium and Electron runs passed.

A probe in the WebKit unit runner shows it directly. After 500 ms, the iframe's rAF callback had run:

| iframe sandbox | WebKit | Chromium |
|---|---|---|
| `allow-same-origin` | **no** | yes |
| `allow-same-origin allow-scripts` | yes | yes |
| none | yes | yes |

The neighbouring HTML preview tests use the same iframe setup but await only `load`, so they pass.

## Fix

These two tests now wait on the host window's animation frame (`mainWindow.requestAnimationFrame`). That frame also renders the same-origin iframe, and the layout reads that follow are synchronous anyway.

docs.title: Route commands to the last activated window in hidden mode
docs.body:
Refs https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344174#issuecomment-6787149834

With `--hidden-window`, no window ever gets DOM focus, so `getActiveDocument()` always falls back to the main window. After `workbench.action.moveEditorToNewWindow`, the active editor group stays in the main window, and `workbench.action.closeActiveEditor` closes the main window's editor instead of the moved one. This was listed as a known limitation in #344174.

In hidden mode:
- When an element gets focus in some window, or `IHostService.focus()` targets a window (except notify-only focus requests), that window becomes the fallback active window. `getActiveDocument()` returns it instead of the main window when no window has focus.
- `moveTop()` doesn't change the fallback, because opening an editor with `preserveFocus` also moves its window to the top without activating it.
- `EditorParts` announces the active group again when the fallback window changes, so `vscode.window.tabGroups.activeTabGroup` follows it.

Visible mode is unchanged: the fallback only takes effect after the hidden-mode host service enables it.

### How to test

On macOS, run an extension test with `--hidden-window` that runs these steps. Each cell is `vscode.window.tabGroups.activeTabGroup.viewColumn` after the step, except the last row, which says which editor `closeActiveEditor` closed:

    ./scripts/code.sh --extensionDevelo

docs.body:
Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#4561

Fixes the second `CopilotAgent` flake from #347393: `discovered SDK customizations › plugin uninstall waits for superseding discovery scans to publish`. It failed in macOS arm64 `Unit (node.js)` in main CI 495325 and [495728](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=495728), each time with one extra empty publish:

Display lightweight per-response performance metadata directly in the Chat response footer (similar to OpenCode), showing:
- **Model name** used for the turn (shortly if the name is too long, like in my case: `OpenCode Go/Beam Free (OpenCode Go/opencodego:beam-free::session-2026-05-21-b) • 0 credits`)

`DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 · 7m 3s · 9.9 tok/s`

### Motivation
VS Code already captures `completion_tokens`, `duration`, and TTFT internally (visible in **Developer: Show Chat Debug View** and OpenTelemetry exports), but users have no quick, at-a-glance way in the Chat UI to compare inference speed across models/providers (e.g., Copilot vs. BYOK/local models) or see how long an agent turn took.

### Suggested Implementation
- Render a compact, muted metadata line next to the response action bar (copy/feedback icons) once streaming completes.
- Make it configurable via a setting (e.g., `chat.showResponseStats`) so users who prefer a minimal UI can toggle it off.

docs.title: Align animated menus and action widgets to device pixels
docs.body:
Fixes #347796

## What

With Modern UI and motion on, the open animation of title bar menus, context menus and action widgets (for example the chat pickers) could end with some or all rows snapping by one device pixel.

## Why

These surfaces open by animating `transform: scale(0.97 → 1)` on a child of a positioned container. While the transform is active, Chromium paints the content from a pixel-snapped offset. Once the animation ends, it paints the content at its exact device-pixel offset. When the container is on a fractional device pixel, which is common (for example the View menu sits at `top: 28.5px` below the title bar at DPR 1), the two can round rows differently. Rows then move by one device pixel in the frame after the animation finishes.

## How

New helper `DOM.alignToDevicePixels(element, direction?)`:
- It measures the element and nudges its inline px `left`/`top` (or `right`/`bottom` when those are the anchored insets) so the element starts on a whole device pixel.
- It takes into account the window's `devicePixelRatio` and CSS zoom, including zoom on shadow hosts.
- It ignores offsets within Chromium's layout precision (positions are floored to 1/64 CSS px), so calling it again doesn't move the element.

Where it is called:
- **`ContextView.doLayout()`** (context menus, dropdown menus, action widgets) uses the same rounding, but computes it from the geometry it

docs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #341887 for the answer-folding case in #334073.

With `chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses`, a completed response keeps a final `Markdown -> one tool call -> Markdown` tail visible and folds only the work before it. That match required the three parts to be adjacent. A reasoning part next to the tool call, which is common when the model thinks before its closing text, defeated it, so the detailed answer was folded with the earlier steps.

- Let the gap between the last two Markdown runs hold exactly one tool call plus any reasoning, before or after it. The answer, the tool call, its reasoning, and the closing text stay visible; everything above the answer folds.
- Leave every other gap alone. Two or more tool calls, no tool call, or any other part kind (file edits, questions, notifications) still fold everything above the last Markdown run.
- Don't count Markdown that holds only edit code blocks as the answer. It renders as edit pills inside the tool chain, so keeping it kept the whole chain out of the disclosure and the response did not collapse.
- Wait for every Markdown part in the preserved tail to finish its incremental reveal before collapsing. Only the first part was checked, so with a preserved tail the work could fold while the closing text was still appearing.

docs.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/305875

- Re-evaluate cols and rows in `TerminalInstance._resize()` from the last `layout()` dimension instead of measuring the container with `getComputedStyle`.

docs.title: Preserve the collaborative, in-editor experience: feedback on Local vs. Copilot harness
docs.body:
Hi team,

I'm an AI development engineer, and I've been using VS Code for several years. It's my favorite tool, and I want to start by genuinely thanking you for building it. The fact that I care enough to write this feedback reflects how much I rely on it.

My daily workflow involves chatting with the agent in the right-hand panel of the editor, using agent mode to delegate parts of my work. I see it as an assistant rather than an autopilot: it picks up part of a task while I continue working, and after it finishes, I often go in and adjust or refine parts of its work by hand. We help each other. That back-and-forth interaction is what makes the experience valuable to me.

To me, the essence of the Local harness is exactly that — a human and an AI working together, rather than an AI fully replacing the human. I understand the intention to converge on the Copilot harness over time, and I'm not asking you to stop improving it. However, the difference in the actual experience matters: Local feels like a plugin that works naturally within VS Code, while the new harness feels more like calling another application from within VS Code. That distinction makes the workspace feel less continuous.

A concrete example I've encountered recently is running terminal commands.

With Local, the agent's commands run in an integrated terminal that I can reveal, watch, scroll through, and reuse.

docs.title: Fix menu and widget open animation 1px jump (#347796)
docs.body:
Fixes #347796

### Cause
When menus (title bar menus, context menus), action widgets (e.g. the agent picker), and anchored quick inputs open with motion enabled, they run a CSS animation that scales from `0.97` to `1` (such as `context-view-menu-motion-open`, `action-widget-scale-open`). While a `transform` is present, Chromium composites the element as a transformed GPU layer at its exact floating-point position without pixel snapping. Once the animation finishes and the transform is removed, Chromium switches to normal paint rendering and snaps elements to integer device pixels.

If the top-level container or an anchor lands on a fractional device pixel (e.g., `titleBoundingRect.left` / `bottom` or floating-point anchor offsets), the element sits on a half-pixel boundary during the animation. When the transform ends, Chromium's rasterizer snaps the coordinates to the device pixel grid, causing a visible 1-device-pixel jump.

### Fix
Snap positioned menu containers and context views to the device pixel grid (`Math.round(v * devicePixelRatio) / devicePixelRatio`):
- Added `snapToDevicePixels(window: Window, cssPx: number): number` helper in `dom.ts`.
- In `contextview.ts` (`doLayout`), snap `top` and `left` of the context view to device pixels.
- In `menubar.ts` (`showMenu`), snap `menuHolder` `left`, `right`, and `top` to device pixels.
- In `menu.ts` (`_layoutSubmenu`), snap

docs.title: chat: show mode and permissions tooltip on keyboard focus (#347807)
docs.body:
Fixes #347807

### Summary
When navigating to the combined Mode and Permissions picker (or separate mode/permission chips in the chat input toolbar) with the keyboard (Tab), the tooltip (e.g. `"Pick Mode and Permissions, Autopilot, assisted permissions"`) did not appear. Keyboard-only and sighted keyboard users could not see the control's purpose without pointer interaction.

### Root Cause
Both `AgentHostChatInputPicker` and `AgentHostSessionEnumPicker` used `this._hoverService.setupDelayedHover(trigger, ...)`. `setupDelayedHover` listens exclusively to mouseover events, so it never triggers when keyboard focus moves into the element or its child buttons (`modeButton`, `permissionsButton`), and does not listen for `Escape` dismissal.

### Fix
Switch to `this._hoverService.setupManagedHover(getDefaultHoverDelegate('element'), trigger, hoverContent)`:
- Captures `FOCUS_IN`, `FOCUS_OUT`, and `Escape` on the trigger container, displaying the tooltip when keyboard focus enters the control or either of its split buttons.
- Keeps the tooltip visible while the control retains keyboard focus.
- Pressing `Escape` closes the tooltip without shifting keyboard focus.

### Validation
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostModePicker.test.ts` (30/30 passing).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatInputPicker.test.ts`

docs.title: agentHost: fix Keep and Undo getting stuck after forking a chat
docs.body:
Fixes #345857

After a chat was forked, Keep and Undo in the pending file changes bar could fail for good with "another chat in this session also changed it". Each chat of a session records its file edits in its own database, and edits are only ordered within a database. The Working Set treated the latest Keep in database order as covering every chat, and both operations rejected any file that more than one chat had edited.

## Changes

- **Keep is scoped to the chat that recorded it.** A Keep now covers the edits before it in its own chat, and the copies of those edits that a forked chat holds. The new `workingSetSources.ts` decides, per file, which chats still have unkept changes. The Working Set, Keep and Undo all use it.
- **Keep** records in every chat that has unkept records of the file, instead of rejecting the file. Keeping a single hunk needs the unkept changes to come from one chat.
- **Undo** works when one chat has unkept changes to the file, including when another chat's changes to it were kept before. It is still rejected when several chats have unkept changes to the file, which Keep clears. Before it changes the file, a Working Set Undo now checks the file's records in every chat, so it doesn't revert a change that was kept meanwhile.
- **Forks.** Records that a fork only copied from its parent no longer count as the fork's own edits when discarding from the Work

The GitHub Copilot Trust Center currently distinguishes between:

2. Other GitHub Copilot access and use, for which Inputs and Outputs may be retained for up to 28 days by default.

- is initiated and displayed in VS Code;
- uses the same GitHub authentication context as VS Code Copilot Chat;

docs.title: sessions: render native visual components in chat responses
docs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #347388. Render explicit, closed `vscode-ui` fences in assistant responses as native, VS Code-rendered components in the Agents window: columns and stack layout, text, metric, badge, table, bar chart, and disclosure. The agent supplies content, data, and composition; VS Code owns every component's implementation and appearance. There is no webview, and nothing in a block is executed.

- **Format.** A fenced block of JSX-like tags with quoted literal attributes only. A versioned, typed schema and a strict parser live in `common`, so they are testable without a DOM. Anything outside the catalogue is rejected with the line and a reason: unknown components or attributes, HTML tags, expressions in braces, `style`, `class`, comments, and loose text. A block is bounded to 32,000 characters, 2,000 components, 8 levels of nesting, 12 columns and 100 rows per table, and 24 bars per chart.
- **Rendering.** A native chat content part renders a block once its closing fence arrives, while the rest of the response keeps streaming. Until then, and whenever a block does not validate, it stays an ordinary code block; an invalid block also shows a short reason. Agent strings are set as text, never as HTML. Charts are drawn by the host from validated numbers.
- **Appearance.** The agent picks semantic variants, such as a positive tone. The stylesheet maps them to theme tok

docs.title: Chat: name pasted images after their source file
docs.body:
When an image is pasted into the chat input, the attachment is always named **Pasted Image** (then *Pasted Image 2*, *Pasted Image 3*, ...), even when the image comes from a file on disk. With several images attached, it is hard to tell them apart, and the name the user chose for the file is lost.

Pasted images often do come from a file:
- a file copied in Explorer/Finder, or
- a screenshot tool that saves the capture and puts the file on the clipboard (e.g. ShareX on Windows).

In those cases the paste event carries the file, and VS Code already resolves its path. For example, a ShareX paste arrives as `ShareX_Region_capture_1.png` with its full path.

**Proposal:** name the attachment after the file (file name only, not the path), e.g. `diagram.png`, and keep it unique with a counter before the extension (`diagram 2.png`). Images without a file on disk (raw clipboard bitmaps) keep the name *Pasted Image*.

In those cases the paste data transfer already carries the file with its resolved path (`IDataTransferFile.uri`, set from `webUtils.getPathForFile`).

This PR names the attachment after that file (base name only, never the path), e.g. `diagram.png`. If the name is already attached, a counter is inserted before the extension (`diagram 2.png`, `diagram 3.png`). Environment:
- Windows cloud desktop (IDD indirect display driver, not hardware vGPU)
- VS Code: 1.146.0
- computer-use-plugin version: 0.1.97

2. Trigger any action that requires screenshot
3. The plugin can enumerate GraphicsCaptureItem successfully, but fails at Direct3D11CaptureFramePool.Create()

Telemetry: follow untitled documents from creation to save or close
docs.body:
We can't tell today what new untitled files are used for. Existing telemetry only counts single steps per day (`editorOpened` with scheme `untitled`, `setUntitledDocumentLanguage` for manual language picks, `workbenchEditorReopen` for editor switches) and nothing connects them to one document. So we can't answer, for example:

- how new files are created (Ctrl+N, tab bar double-click, extension API, ...),
- how often the empty editor hint is shown, not just clicked, and whether people type first or use the hint,
- which language and editor a new file ends up in (e.g. Markdown in the text editor vs. Markdown Preview vs. Markdown Editor),
- whether new files get saved, discarded, or stay open as scratchpads.

This matters for improving the empty editor hint and for offering the new Markdown Editor (and other editors such as a chat editor) from new files.

**Proposal:** give every untitled document a random `untitledDocumentId` that survives window reloads, send events for its lifecycle (created, first edit, ended), and add that id to language change, hint and editor switch events, so all events of one document can be grouped in one query.

docs.title: Proposed API: let extensions contribute buttons to the title bar of the editor and Agents windows
docs.body:
Extensions can't add buttons to the title bar. Neither the editor window's title bar nor the Agents window's title bar is a contributable menu, so an extension feature that should always be one click away (for example, reporting a bug for an agent to fix) has to live in a view title, the status bar or the command palette.

Proposal: a proposed API `contribTitleBar` with two menus:

- `titleBar`: buttons in the editor window's title bar (the existing global title bar toolbar, next to the layout controls).
- `agents/titleBar`: buttons in the Agents window's title bar, left of its built-in buttons.

```json
"menus": {
  "titleBar": [{ "command": "myExtension.report", "group": "navigation" }],
  "agents/titleBar": [{ "command": "myExtension.report", "group": "navigation" }]
}
```

docs.title: Proposed API: contribute buttons to the editor and Agents window title bars

- `titleBar`: buttons in the editor window's title bar. This is the existing `MenuId.TitleBar` toolbar next to the layout controls, which core already uses for e.g. the notifications bell. `navigation` items show as buttons, the rest go to its overflow menu.
- `agents/titleBar`: buttons in the Agents window's title bar, left of its built-in buttons. This is a new `MenuId.AgentsTitleBar`, rendered as its own toolbar that takes part in the title bar's overflow handling.

```json
"contributes": {
```

## Summary

Allow users to configure preferred accounts for MCP authentication using `mcp.authentication.loginHints`, with provider defaults and per-server overrides.

```json
    "microsoft": "me@company.com"

  "servers": {
```

Account preference precedence:

3. Authentication provider default
4. Existing session-selection behavior

docs.title: agentHost: settle in-memory file events before creating the agent in CopilotAgent tests
docs.body:
Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#4561

Follow-up to #347698 and #347795. It closes the rest of the late-write class in `copilotAgent.test.ts` instead of fixing one test at a time.

## Problem

`InMemoryFileSystemProvider` reports writes a few ms later, in one debounced batch. Many `CopilotAgent` tests write plugin or customization files and then create the agent. When that batch lands **after** the agent's plugin watcher registers, the watcher calls `invalidateRuntimePluginContents()` and an unawaited `publishWhenSettled()`, so customizations republish in the middle of the test. Whether it lands before or after depends on agent speed. Three tests have failed on CI this way:
- `publishes shared content revisions…`, fixed in #347698
- `plugin uninstall waits for superseding discovery scans…`, in #347795
- `runtime-first native MCP inventory…`, in #347795

20 more tests in this file use the same setup without any guard.

## Change

A small helper, `settleFileEvents(fileService)`. If the in-memory provider still has a buffered batch, it waits for that batch's `onDidChangeFile`, which the file service has already forwarded by then. Otherwise it returns right away. It's called right before the agent is created in each of the 20 tests. Test-only.

It waits on the provider's own event rather than `fileService.onDidFilesChange`, so a test that stubs the file service event can't hang it

docs.title: test: run the changed unit test files of a pull request alone
docs.body:
## What

A unit test run loads every test file before running any. So a test file can pass only because another test file of the run loads a module that registers what it reads, such as a `*.contribution.ts`. It then fails when it runs alone, or when a pull request's [test plan](../blob/main/build/ripple/README.md) selects it without that other file, typically in an unrelated pull request. Two recent examples:

- #347696 moved the registration of the session chat view editor out of a module's load-time code. `chatEditor.test.ts` kept passing in full runs because `chatWindowContribution.test.ts` registers it, and failed in #347680, which only touches quick input.
- `promptTemplatePlaceholder.test.ts` read a command that only the Agents window's chat contribution registers (fixed in #347853).

This adds a check that catches such test files in the pull request that changes them:

- **`--isolate`** for the Electron unit test runner (`test/unit/electron/index.js`, `runEachFileAlone` in `test/unit/parallel.ts`): runs every test file of the run (`--run`, `--runList`, `--runGlob` or all) alone in a fresh window, as many at once as `--workers` allows. docs.title: Feature Request: Agents Overview Dashboard
docs.body:
I would like the Agents window to provide an overview dashboard where users can easily monitor and manage all their agents in one place.

Ideally, this overview would include:
- **Running agents:** See which agents are currently working, their progress, and what task they are handling.
- **Completed agents:** Easily identify finished tasks and access their results.
- **Quick actions:** Interact with agents directly from the overview (e.g. open the conversation, review results, continue working, or start a new task).
- **Agent status:** Have a clear visual distinction between running, completed, waiting for input, and failed agents.

The goal is to make managing multiple agents at the same time much easier, without having to open individual conversations to understand what's happening.

In the future, it would be amazing to see this evolve into something more visual and playful, perhaps a pixel-art-inspired, gamified dashboard where agents are represented as characters working on different tasks.

However, I'm not asking for anything that ambitious right now. Even a simple, clean overview with agent statuses and quick actions would be a huge improvement.

Currently, the Agents landing page feels primarily focused on starting a new chat, rather than providing a centralized place to monitor and manage ongoing agent activity.

docs.title: Agents window: let an automation's runs continue the same chat
docs.body:
Every run of an automation in the Agents window starts a new chat. A recurring automation can't build on what its earlier runs said, and History fills up with one chat per run.

Some automations are meant to be one ongoing conversation: for example, a daily status report that should compare today with yesterday, or a daily language lesson that shouldn't repeat the words it already taught. Today each run starts from nothing.

## Proposal

An opt-in option for each automation, **Same Chat**. When it's on, each run sends the automation's prompt in the chat of its previous run instead of starting a new chat.

- It's off by default, so existing automations keep starting a new chat for each run.
- In the automation dialog it's a switch next to **Run in the Cloud**. Cloud runs can't continue a chat, so while Run in the Cloud is on, the switch is off and disabled, with the reason "Not available in the cloud".
- If you're chatting in that chat when a run starts, the run waits for your turn to finish.
- A run starts a new chat when the previous one is gone or archived, or when a setting that a chat keeps from its creation changed, such as the folder, mode or approvals. Archiving or deleting the chat starts over.
- History lists a chat shared by several runs once.

docs.title: build: allow the Copilot SDK plugin dot files in the macOS universal ASAR merge
docs.body:
Since #347800 (Nov 12 05:33), the Copilot SDK platform package keeps the dot files of `plugins/browser-use` (`.mcp.json`, `.release-target`, `.plugin/plugin.json`). The macOS universal merge rejects them, so `macOS (UNIVERSAL) - Sign` › `Create Universal App` fails in every official build from `d0e3b45e89` on, for example the 11:00 insider [495870](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=495870):

```
Error: Detected unique file "@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-x64/plugins/browser-use/.mcp.json" ... not covered by allowList rule
```

A failed universal stage fails Publish, so the build doesn't release.

## Cause

`vscode-universal-bundler` 0.1.3 checks each ASAR entry that only one arch has with `minimatch(file, singleArchFiles, { matchBase: true })` (minimatch 9.0.9). Without `dot: true`, `**` doesn't match dot files or folders, so `**/@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-*/**` covers `plugins/browser-use/dist/browser-mcp.cjs` but none of the 4 dot entries.

## Change

- Add `**/@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-*/plugins/*/.*` and `**/@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-*/plugins/*/.*/**` to `singleArchFiles`. Nothing else in the merge changes.
- Move the pattern to an exported `DARWIN_UNIVERSAL_SINGLE_ARCH_FILES` constant so it can be tested.
- `build/lib/test/createUniversalApp.test.ts` checks the pattern with the bundler's own minimatch, called the way the bundler calls it:
  - t

docs.title: fix: match a URI's windowId to its window exactly
docs.body:
Fixes #345470

`URLHandlerRouter.routeCall` picks the window for a URI carrying `windowId=<id>` by testing ``new RegExp(`window:${windowId}`)`` against each connection's context. The pattern isn't anchored, so `windowId=1` also matches `window:10` through `window:19`, and the first match in `hub.connections` wins. When window 1 reloads, its connection is re-added at the end of the list, so a callback meant for window 1 reaches window 10 instead. This anchors the pattern, so only `window:<id>` itself matches.

**How to test**

The new unit test in `src/vs/platform/url/test/common/urlIpc.test.ts` routes `windowId=1`, `2` and `10` against windows 10, 1 and 21. Without the fix they reach windows 10, 21 and 10. With it, they reach window 1, the fallback router and window 10.

End to end, the steps in #345470 apply: open windows until one has id 10 or more, reload window 1, then open a URI built with `asExternalUri` in window 1 from a browser. It now reaches window 1.

docs.body:

Preserving the Copilot SDK's hidden plugin metadata exposed a mismatch in macOS universal packaging: the ASAR merger's existing SDK allowlist uses globs that do not implicitly match dotfiles. ## What

The VS Code pet could fall through a chat pill above the input when the pill belongs to an artifact whose integration shows state as extra sections (for example, a pull request pill showing `#123 | ✓ 6/6 | 💬 2`). - `getPillElements()` is unchanged, because compaction and focus restoration need the buttons.

## Problem
In the Agents window, with feedback comments on several files in the Changes editor, picking another file in the Changes file list (Details) moves the multi-diff editor to that file, but the feedback overlay's counter keeps showing the old position (for example `1/3`). The overlay doesn't listen to that event, so nothing updates the anchor. docs.title: Keep inline attachment pills within a row of the chat input
docs.body:
Fixes #346230

## Problem
In a narrow chat input, for example the Agents window with the chat column squeezed, an inline attachment pill with a long name (such as `#customer-subscription-billing-reconciliation.ts`) can be wider than the input. The pill's label had a fixed maximum width of 240px, so the pill ran past the right edge and the input scrolled sideways: the first characters of every line were clipped.

## Change
Each pill now caps its label at the width of the input's content. `_updateMaxWidth` takes the content width from the editor's layout info, minus the vertical scrollbar, the pill's padding and two characters' width of slack. The slack covers the space that wrapping at whole characters loses, plus room for the anchor to stay on its row. The result goes in the `--chat-inline-attachment-max-width` CSS variable, and the label's `max-width` becomes `min(240px, var(...))`. The pill recomputes it on every layout change. Wide inputs keep the 240px cap they had before.

docs.title: chat: place sticky working progress once per frame while streaming
docs.body:
Fixes #345825. Also addresses #345826, which has the same top frames reached through tree row insertion and scrolling.

## Problem
`ChatListItemRenderer.updateStickyProgress()` reads layout: through `isWorkingProgressOutsideViewport` it calls `getBoundingClientRect` on the tree, the sticky container and the inline anchor. While a response streams, it was called synchronously from:

docs.title: sessions: stop leaking a hidden terminal per new session
docs.body:
Fixes #347903

## Problem

In the Agents window, each new session leaves one hidden terminal alive: a `TerminalInstance`, an `XtermTerminal` and a bash pty. Deleting the session doesn't close it. On Insiders 1.147.0-insider (Linux), the loop *new session → send → new draft → delete session* adds one live shell process per iteration (1 → 12 over 12 iterations). The terminal is retained by `TerminalService._backgroundedTerminalInstances → TerminalInstance → XtermTerminal`. A 25-iteration heap snapshot diff shows `TerminalInstance`/`XtermTerminal` instances growing from 6 to 25.

There are two causes in `SessionsTerminalContribution`:

1. **Same-id replacement.** When a session is replaced by one with the same id, `_transferTerminals(from, to)` with `from === to` moves the tracked ids into the target set and then deletes the source entry, which is the same entry. The session ends up with no tracked terminals, so deleting it later closes nothing.
2. **Discarded drafts.** When a new-session draft is discarded, its entry in `_sessionTerminals` stays. Its terminal is never reused by the next session in the same cwd, so a new one is created, and the old one is never closed because the discarded draft is never "removed".

## Change

- `_transferTerminals` returns early when `fromSessionId === toSessionId`: the terminals already belong to the target.
- Listen to `onDidDiscardNewSession`

The Windows build job of the flaky-test pipeline (def 700) hands its workspace to the test jobs as `repo.zip`, and 7-Zip stores every junction as a copy of its target. ## Problem

In the Agents window sessions list, if the mouse enters a session row and leaves it again before the hover delay has passed, the session hover still appears after the delay and stays open, even though the mouse is on neither the row nor the hover. It closes only when the mouse goes back over the row or the hover. If the mouse rests until the hover is shown and then leaves, the hover closes as it should. docs.title: Avoid quadratic work when many text models are disposed at once
docs.body:
Fixes #332670

## What happens

Leaving an Agents session whose Changes view lists thousands of files (for example by clicking **New**) freezes the whole window for tens of seconds. With a 6,601-file change set, the window froze for **35 seconds** on main.

## Why

Leaving the session closes the Changes multi-diff editor. That disposes about 13,000 text models at once: an original and a modified model for each file. For **every** disposed model, two `onModelRemoved` listeners scan **all** the remaining models:

1. The extension-host document sync (`MainThreadDocumentAndEditorStateComputer`) recomputes its entire document and editor state.
2. The editor worker manager calls `getModels().length` to check whether it can stop the worker.

n removals × O(n) work each makes the burst quadratic.

## Fix

- `mainThreadDocumentsAndEditors.ts`: when a model is removed, drop just that model from the current state and send a one-document delta. The add path already works this way. The full recompute still runs when an editor shows the removed model.
- `editorWorkerService.ts`: check for an empty worker once per burst of removals, on the next tick, instead of once per model.

## Result

Same repro, longest renderer freeze after clicking **New**: **35,279 ms → 4,448 ms**.

In the videos, the renderer clock at the top of the window stops while the renderer is blocked.

docs.title: Chat scroll-down button forces a synchronous layout on every visibility toggle while a response streams
docs.body:
**Version:** VS Code Insiders 1.147.0-insider (0f38c8f0ffcd), and `main` at a60182f8a04
**OS:** Linux x64

### What happens

While a chat response streams in the Agents window (or in workbench chat) and the list follows the bottom, every scroll event calls `ChatListWidget.updateScrollDownButtonVisibility`. Each content-height increase briefly pushes the list off the bottom, and the auto-reveal then brings it back. So the "scroll down" button is toggled hidden/shown many times per frame. On every toggle, `updateScrollDownButtonPosition()` runs synchronously. It reads `getBoundingClientRect()` on the sticky progress row and the list container and `offsetHeight` on the button, right after DOM writes from the same scroll/reveal. Each of those reads forces a style recalc and layout.

The positioning result only matters for the frame that gets painted. Only the last toggle in a frame is ever visible.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start a session.
2. Send a prompt that produces a long, streamed markdown answer, and keep the list scrolled to the bottom while it streams.
3. Use a performance trace, or instrument `getBoundingClientRect`/`offsetHeight`, and attribute the reads to callers.

docs.title: Chat input pills: only rescan the row when its state changes
docs.body:
Fixes #347904

## Problem

`ChatInputPills` derives the pills row state (`visible`, `empty` or `hidden`) and applies it with `recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange`. That calls its handler on every update of the pill sources, even when the derived state is unchanged. While a response streams, the sources update with almost every chunk. Each handler call runs `DomScrollableElement.scanDomNode`, which reads `clientWidth`/`scrollWidth` and often forces a synchronous layout.

I measured this with a layout probe on Insiders 1.147.0 in the Agents window, using a mock LLM endpoint. Over one streamed response there were 320 rescans, 52 ms in total, and 43 of them forced a layout.

## Change

The state handler now runs in an `autorun` that reads the derived row state. The DOM work only happens when the state actually changes. Pill size changes are still rescanned by the row's existing resize observer, so overflow and scroll arrows keep updating when pills grow, shrink or are added. Focus restore on hide is unchanged.

A regression test checks that updating pill data without changing the row state no longer rescans the row.

Fixes #315740

## Problem

The Agents window has a single editor group and doesn't support splitting. Quick access still offers "Open to the Side" in Go to Symbol in Editor (`@`), Quick Open (`Ctrl+P`) and Go to Symbol in Workspace (`#`). Clicking it, or using Alt / Ctrl+Enter, does nothing visible.

docs.body:
Fixes #347906

## Problem

While a chat response streams, every scroll event re-evaluates whether the scroll-down button is shown. As the content grows past the bottom and is revealed again, the button toggles several times per frame. `updateScrollDownButtonVisibility` positioned it synchronously on each toggle. docs.title: Only compare the ancestors that changed when re-parenting a scoped context key service
docs.body:
Fixes #347900

### Problem
`ScopedContextKeyService.updateParent()` computed the changed keys by running `collectAllValues()` on the child before and after the re-parent and diffing the two objects. Each call walks the whole ancestor chain and spreads every ancestor's values, up to the root's cached `config.*` keys, into a new object. The old and new parents almost always share most of that chain (the chat widget, the part, the workbench root), so the keys those ancestors provide can't change.

In the Agents window, every chat code block re-attaches its editor's scoped context key service on each list re-render, so switching sessions pays this for every code block. A CPU profile of 12 session switches on Insiders showed `collectAllValues` at 130 ms self time (369 ms total), plus 71.5 ms in the `value` getter. The parent change listener used that getter to copy the child's whole `_value` object for a membership check.

### Change
- `Context.updateParent()` now returns the keys whose collected value changed. It only looks at keys defined by the ancestors below the first ancestor that the old and new parent share. If they share none, it falls back to collecting all values, as before.

docs.body:
Fixes #347905

## Problem

`ChatWidget.setReadOnly` always ends with `rerenderListIfConnected()`, which runs `ChatListWidget.rerender()`. That re-probes the height of every visible row and re-measures the sticky-scroll rows, all of it forcing layout. docs.title: Check the current origin survives a stale mount in the WebviewElement test
docs.body:
Follow-up to #347758. Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#4573

Supersedes the build-fix agent's draft #347760, whose extra assertion this ports.

## What's missing today

#346646 added two stale-mount guards in `WebviewElement.mountTo`: one skips `_initElement` for a superseded mount, the other skips writing `_encodedWebviewOrigin`. The `ignores an earlier mount whose origin hash finishes after a remount` test only catches the first. If the second guard is removed, the stale hash overwrites the origin that the current shell's `webview-ready` message is checked against, so the webview rejects its own shell, and the test still passes.

## Change

Test-only. After the stale hash completes, the test dispatches a ready event from the current mount's origin on a fresh `MessageChannel` and asserts the webview accepts it (`acceptedCurrentOrigin: true`).

## Validation

Local Electron runs of `webviewElement.test.ts`:
- With this change: 48 passing, 8 of 8 runs green.
- `_encodedWebviewOrigin` guard removed: fails with `acceptedCurrentOrigin: false` (the case the current test misses).
- `_initElement` guard removed: fails.
- Real digest slowed by 20 ms (the WebKit timing behind 495597): passes.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in the touched file.

docs.body:
Fixes #347859

### Context & Cause
In `src/vs/editor/editor.worker.start.ts`, `ctx.getMirrorModels` previously read the outer `webWorkerServer.requestHandler.getModels()`. However, `initialize()` creates `new WebWorkerServer(...)` which invokes the factory callback synchronously inside its constructor before `webWorkerServer` is assigned:
1. `const webWorkerServer = initialize(...)` was in the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) if `createClient(ctx)` called `ctx.getMirrorModels()` synchronously during startup (e.g. Volar / TypeScript language service initialization).
2. Furthermore, inside `initialize()`, the factory callback is executed *during* `new WebWorkerServer(msg => ..., factory)`, so `workerServer.requestHandler` is not yet assigned until the factory returns.
3. If an error was thrown inside `createClient(ctx)`, the worker was permanently wedged with `WebWorker already initialized!` on subsequent calls because `initialized = true` was never rolled back upon failure.

### Solution
1. Instantiate `const editorWorker = new EditorWorker()` within the factory before invoking `createClient(ctx)`, allowing `ctx.getMirrorModels()` to query `editorWorker.getModels()` immediately without TDZ or undefined reference errors.
2. Provide `EditorWorker.prototype.setForeignModule(client)` to attach the foreign client module after `createClient(ctx)` completes, before returning `editorWorker`.

docs.title: fix(notebook): don't block attaching cells on markdown renderer warmup
docs.body:
Fixes #347729

## Problem

A notebook opened in the foreground can show the toolbar and a progress bar but **no cells at all — code cells included — for 10–60 s** (sometimes longer) whenever its webview is slow to load the Markdown renderer. The window itself is idle meanwhile. This happens on machines whose CPU is busy with other normal-priority processes (antivirus scan, installer, indexer), with all extensions disabled.

## Root cause

`_warmupWithMarkdownRenderer` gates `_list.attachViewModel(viewModel)` — the only point where cells become visible in the list view — behind two **unbounded** awaits:

1. `await this._resolveWebview()` — resolves only when the webview posts `initialized` (end of preload script evaluation).
2. `await this._warmupViewportMarkdownCells(...)` → `initializeMarkup(...)` — resolves only when the webview posts the `initializedMarkup` ack, which is sent after the webview has loaded the Markdown renderer and pre-rendered the viewport's Markdown cells.

Neither wait has a timeout, and the code comment's expectation is 'around 200ms'. When webview process/content loading is starved by CPU contention, the user stares at an empty editor for as long as the load takes. If the webview never finishes loading, cells never show at all.

docs.title: search: preserve whole word boundaries for non-ASCII characters (#347926)
docs.body:
Fixes #347926

### Context & Cause
In `src/vs/base/common/strings.ts`, `createRegExp` handles `options.wholeWord` by checking `!/\B/.test(searchString.charAt(0))` and `!/\B/.test(searchString.charAt(searchString.length - 1))` to decide whether to wrap the pattern in `\b` word boundaries.

However, in JavaScript regular expressions, `\B` defaults to ASCII word boundaries. For any non-ASCII character (Cyrillic `дать`, Greek `και`, Arabic `من`, Hebrew `עם`, etc.), JavaScript treats the character as a non-word character (`\W`), so `/\B/.test(char)` evaluates to `true` (i.e. not an ASCII word boundary). Consequently, `!/\B/.test(...)` returned `false`, and `\b` was never prepended or appended to the search pattern.

When searching files without open editors, `ripgrepTextSearchEngine` converts `query.isWordMatch` queries into regex via `createRegExp(query.pattern, !!query.isRegExp, { wholeWord: query.isWordMatch })`. Because `\b` was omitted, Ripgrep was invoked with `--regexp <pattern>` (without word boundaries), causing it to match substrings within longer non-ASCII words (such as `дать` inside `воздать` or `και` inside `καιρός`).

### Solution
1. Update `isWordBoundaryCandidate` in `src/vs/base/common/strings.ts` to test `!/\B/.test(char) || /[\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}\p{Pc}]/u.test(char)` (including Unicode letters, marks, numbers, and connector punctuation), handling surrogate pairs and f

The Sessions view groups agent sessions by workspace folder. When work spans folders, its sessions are scattered:

- one task touches two repositories, so its sessions appear in two groups;

This depends on client-editable session tags in the Agent Host Protocol: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#594.

Follow-up to #347629.

The Copilot runtime can start an extension lazily ([github/copilot-agent-runtime#28873](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/28873)). An extension that declares its canvases in an `extension.json` sidecar with `"initialization": "module"` starts on first use.

docs.body:
On a page taller than its view, the integrated browser's **Add Full Page Screenshot to Chat** (shown when `workbench.browser.experimentalUserTools.enabled` is on) could return an image that repeats the top of the page instead of showing all of it.

This fix was part of #347643 and is split out into its own PR, as requested in review there.

### Why it happens

A full-page screenshot temporarily enlarges the page beyond its view. If the view is shown, hidden or moved meanwhile, or another screenshot is taken, that ends early, and the rest of the image repeats the top of the page. This happens routinely:
- The browser's Add to Chat menu and the Command Palette cover the page, so the page is hidden while they're open and shown again as they close, just as the capture starts.
- The workbench takes a placeholder screenshot of the page every second while it's visible, and another one whenever it's shown or hidden.

### Fix

A small helper, `BrowserViewCaptureGate`, coordinates this for the main-process `BrowserView`:
- Screenshots of a view are taken one at a time, in order.
- While a full-page screenshot is taken, showing and moving the view wait. Once it's done, they're applied in order, before the next screenshot. They're dropped if the view is disposed meanwhile.

docs.title: terminal: preserve model configuration for background completion notifications (#347928)
docs.body:
Fixes #347928

### Problem
When a command runs in a background terminal, the completion or input-needed steering request sent to the chat session resumes the same agent context by capturing `userSelectedModelId`, `modeInfo`, and `userSelectedTools` from `lastRequest`. However, `userSelectedModelConfiguration` (such as context size or thinking effort) was omitted from `sendOptions`.

As a result, `ChatServiceImpl.sendRequest` falls back to the model's global configuration via `this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(options.userSelectedModelId)`. On chats configured with custom context sizes (such as 1M context chats), this fallback causes aggressive pruning of chat history and subsequent provider errors or cost spikes due to history mismatch.

### Solution
1. In `RunInTerminalTool._registerCompletionNotification`:
   - Include `userSelectedModelConfiguration` in `sendOptions`.
   - Read `lastRequest.modelConfiguration` (falling back to `sessionRef.object.inputModel?.state.get()?.modelConfiguration` if not set on the request).
   - If `lastRequest` is undefined, also populate `userSelectedModelId` and `userSelectedModelConfiguration` from `sessionRef.object.inputModel?.state.get()`.
2. Added unit tests in `runInTerminalTool.test.ts`:
   - Verifying that background completion notifications preserve custom model configuration (such as `contextWindow` and `thinkingEffort`)

docs.body:
**Status: awaiting owner signing.** Unsigned draft.

Since the Copilot SDK 1.0.3x bumps, every `automation/bump-copilot-sdk-*` PR (for example microsoft/vscode#347784) fails `Copilot - Test (Linux)` and `chat-lib - Test (Linux)`. Both fail while building `kerberos@2.1.1` with node-gyp on `fatal error: gssapi/gssapi.h: No such file or directory`, in 26 jobs across 5 bump branches.

**Why:** `kerberos` is an optional peer of `proxy-agent-negotiate`, which the `http-proxy-agent` and `https-proxy-agent` that `@vscode/test-web` uses depend on. Then `pnpm --filter copilot-chat --filter @vscode/chat-lib rebuild` compiles `kerberos`. Every other Linux test job gets `libkrb5-dev` through `install-linux-packages`, but these two only install `xvfb libgtk-3-0 libgbm1` (Copilot), or nothing (chat-lib).

- `pr.yml`: `Copilot - Test (Linux)` also installs `libkrb5-dev`.
- `test-chat-lib` action: a Linux-only step installs `libkrb5-dev` with `apt-retry.sh`, as other jobs do.

docs.title: Support window.prompt() in the integrated browser
docs.body:
Electron hardcodes `window.prompt()` to throw, so any page that uses it breaks in the integrated browser.

This PR replaces `prompt` in the browser view preload so it blocks the page and asks the workbench, which shows an input dialog. Agents can answer it too.

- The page blocks on a synchronous message to the main process, like a native prompt.
- The workbench shows the prompt in a dialog. If nothing can show it or answer it (hidden, no external agent), it returns `null` right away.
- Agents see it as a normal CDP dialog (`Page.javascriptDialogOpening`/`Closed`, `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`), so `handle_dialog` and Playwright work. Accepting without text returns the default value. Whoever answers first wins, and the other side's dialog closes.
- Prompts are settled when the page navigates or reloads, the raising frame navigates or is removed, or the view goes away.
- The agent tab now detects a closed dialog through CDP rather than a probe script. The probe returned early for prompts from out-of-process frames (for example sandboxed iframes with an opaque origin), so agents couldn't answer them.

This does not add rate limiting for pages that spam prompts.

Tested on Linux only, and not with a real chat agent. Unit tests for prompt tracking, and integration tests driving `handle_dialog` for text, default and dismiss, plus a sandboxed iframe case.

docs.title: smoke: retry transient update server failures within a bounded time
docs.body:
Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#4593

Hardens smoke against the update service degradation that has been failing main CI smoke since about 14:00 UTC on Nov 12 (495948, 495977, 496037), and PR smoke across the Dev Container, SSH and WSL suites. The service is `update.code.visualstudio.com`: its release listings are slow or return 502/504, and CLI downloads sometimes return 504 after 60 s. The owner has been notified. 1. **Windows smoke `"before all"`: `Could not fetch releases from update server`** (`main.ts`). The stable release lookup was `retry(() => fetch(...))`. `retry()` only retries **thrown** errors, and a 502/504 *resolves* with `!ok`, so the first bad response failed the run. parameter properties, which JavaScript class field semantics initialize after the fields. It

docs.body:
Fixes #338065.

Keep rapid Markdown editor deletions, cursor actions, and typing in input order without hardcoding default shortcuts or bypassing user keybindings. Starting with `one`, Backspace, Backspace, `e`, `n` should produce `oen`, rather than having delayed deletions remove the newly typed letters.

The opt-in webview bridge captures keyboard events for one-use dispatch through the existing keybinding service. Both keydown and keyup join the editor's ordered input stream, including single-modifier chords, and share workbench hold-mode handling. Keybinding decisions start after focus-context acknowledgement without waiting for each document edit to round-trip through the extension host; their results are applied in input order.

The editor uses its text-input transport to keep native input offsets separate from asynchronous model changes, including interior and ranged IME composition carets. docs.body:
Part of #345427. Stacked on [#347354](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/347354); the diff against that branch is this PR's change.

Extensions can contribute a resource to every chat with the proposed `chatResources` contribution point ([#347330](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/347330), merged). Until now the resource was only listed in the chat's Artifacts pill, so the user had to pin it and choose **Show Above Chat Input** in every chat. For a resource such as a per-chat todo list, the extension knows it belongs above the input. This PR lets the contribution say so.

 

## The contribution

```json
"chatResources": [
	{
		"id": "todos",
		"label": "Todos",
		"resource": "chat-todos:/${agentSessionId}.todo.json",
		"mode": "aboveInput"
	}
```

debug: keep disassembly rows correct when sources are unavailable
docs.body:
Fixes #347953

## Problem

When a source file referenced by a `disassemble` response is unavailable, some rows in the Disassembly view display the address, bytes, and text of an unrelated instruction. Scrolling away and back replaces one incorrect instruction with another.

## Root cause

In `InstructionRenderer.renderElementInner`, `createModelReference` is awaited **before** the instruction text is written into the row template. For a `file` resource that does not exist, the text model resolver rejects (`textFileService.files.resolve` throws `FileNotFound`), so everything after the `await` — including `templateData.instruction.innerText = sb.build()` — is skipped, and the rejection escapes `renderElement` unhandled because the table renderer interface is synchronous.

The table reuses row templates while scrolling, so the affected row keeps whatever the previous element had rendered: address, bytes and instruction text of an unrelated instruction. Each scroll cycle reuses the row for a different previous element, which is why the displayed wrong instruction changes when scrolling.

The staleness guard added in #192831 runs after the await and only handles a *resolved* reference; it cannot help when the promise rejects.

- `renderElementInner` now renders the instruction (address, bytes, text) and the row background **before** loading the source. That data depends o

docs.title: Disable background throttling only for agent-shared browser views
docs.body:
Hidden integrated browser views are throttled by Electron, so animation frames stop. When an agent opens a page in a background tab, actions like click time out waiting for the page to become stable.

This PR turns background throttling off only for views owned by or shared with an agent, and restores it when sharing ends.

- Agent-owned or agent-shared views keep rendering while hidden, so stability checks complete
- The setting is re-applied whenever a document is ready. Electron ignores it for a view that has never been shown if it's set before the first frame exists, which is exactly the background-tab case
- User-only background tabs keep default throttling

Doesn't change `visibilityState`: hidden pages still report hidden, they just keep producing frames.

Tested: reproduced in a standalone Electron 43 harness (hidden view, rAF probe). Throttled: rAF stalls. Setting applied only at construction: still stalls, even after navigating. Re-applied on dom-ready: rAF runs, including after a cross-site navigation. Not run inside VS Code itself.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332409

docs.title: Tree view: TreeDataSource batching resolves children from the wrong batch, leaving expanded nodes empty (shared batch/batchPromise fields)
docs.body:
Sorry for AI description. I'm seeing this bug with my extension for a long time already. I'm not on freshest version, but code analysis shows that nothing changed substantially in main, so it 99.9% still happens.

---

 
 
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (it needs an extension-contributed tree view; the built-in References view uses the same code path, see #232709)

- VS Code Version: 1.143.1 (e646868227c3e3a9e3f24277c8c7220be42c0be7, stable). The affected code is unchanged on `main` (checked at a717861c).
- OS Version: macOS 26.7.2, local extension host

## Summary

`TreeDataSource.getChildren` in `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/views/treeView.ts` batches the `getChildren` calls of one tick into a single `$getChildren` RPC. The pending batch and its promise are kept in two **shared instance fields** (`batch`, `batchPromise`). Each caller schedules its own `setTimeout(0)` and keeps only its `indexInBatch`. If any new `getChildren` call starts a new batch between two sibling timer callbacks of an older batch, the shared fields are reset and the later siblings resolve `result[indexInBatch]` against the **new** batch: an empty array when that batch is shorter (the guard from #232720 turns the out-of-range read into `[]`), or another node's children when it is not.

That interleaving is not exotic. It happens deterministically whenever a batch is served

The CI builds of `main` and `release/*` now run in the CI build pipeline (definition 727, `product-build-ci.yml`, #347822). Until now the product build pipeline (definition 111) also ran a CI build for every batch of commits, so each commit was built and tested twice. - `product-build.yml`: `trigger: none` instead of `batch: true` on `main` and `release/*`. Definition 111 takes its CI trigger from the YAML (its definition has no UI override), so this stops its CI builds.

docs.title: cli: prevent duplicate GitHub environment supervisors
docs.body:
Follow-up to #347703.

Repeated `code agent host --github-environment` commands start independent background supervisors that share one persisted environment identity but advertise different encryption keys. Clients can then reject authentication because the host answering the relay does not match the keys published by the latest heartbeat.

Hold the existing cross-process file lock for the GitHub environment supervisor's lifetime, scoped to the backend server data directory. Reject duplicate starts before prompting for credentials and recheck in the supervisor to cover concurrent first starts. Separate server data directories remain independent; ordinary local agent-host startup is unchanged.

Live validation on macOS with the rebuilt CLI: concurrent initial starts admitted one supervisor; repeated starts, foreground mode, and alternate CLI/registry directories were rejected. The remaining host answered initialize once, completed encrypted authentication, and retained matching keys across a heartbeat. All test hosts and environments were removed. Windows live validation was not run.

Checks passed: `cd cli && cargo build --locked --bin code`; `cd cli && cargo test --locked --lib commands:: --no-fail-fast` (61 tests); `cd cli && cargo clippy --locked --lib --quiet`; `cd cli && rustfmt --check --edition 2021 src/commands/agent_host.rs`.

(Written by Copilot)

docs.title: Problem with integrated browser cellartracker.com
docs.body:
Some sites block the integrated browser, probably because its user agent includes the `Code/` and `Electron/` tokens. CellarTracker is one example: searches return a blank protection-script page. Today the only way to change the user agent is the per-tab "Emulate User Agent..." command, which isn't persistent and can't be set per workspace.

This PR adds a `workbench.browser.userAgent` setting as a workaround for these sites.

- The setting can be set per workspace, and applies to open and new browser views, including popups.
- Its default is the real default user agent, so there's something to base a change on. Leaving it at the default keeps following Electron across updates; a customized value stays pinned.
- Device emulation still overrides it, and clearing the emulation falls back to the setting.

This PR does **not** change the default user agent, and I haven't verified that a Chrome user agent fixes CellarTracker. Client hints (`Sec-CH-UA`) still use Electron's brands, so some sites may still block the browser. Dropping the Code/Electron tokens by default is a possible follow-up.

Tested with a new unit test for the user agent precedence, plus lint and a client build. Not tried against the real site.

Ref: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344854

docs.title: build: drop interrupted Node.js compile cache writes before validating
docs.body:
Fixes the `NODE-COMPILE-CACHE-TEMP-ENTRY` flake: `Build client` fails in CI test jobs with

```
Error: Node.js compile cache generation produced unexpected shared-process cache entries in …/node-compile-cache/shared-process/v24.22.1-arm64-7034790f: 6664eb6b.cqknyl.
```

It has hit 4 times since Oct 20 (488834, 489047, 492985, 496291), about once a week, always in `shared-process` and always with one `<hash>.<6 chars>` file.

## Mechanism

- Node's compile cache writes each entry to `<entry>.XXXXXX` with `uv_fs_mkstemp` and then renames it into place (`src/compile_cache.cc`). A `<hash>.<random>` file is a write that never reached its rename.
- During generation, each utility process calls `markNodeCompileCacheReady()`, which runs `flushCompileCache()` and writes `.ready`. With `eager: true`, it keeps compiling after that, and Node flushes again on exit.
- `app.ts` waits for every `.ready` marker and then quits. If a process is stopped while its exit flush is writing, the temporary file stays behind, and `validateNodeCompileCache` rejects the whole cache. The shared process is the busiest after ready, which is why it's always the one.

## Fix

Before validating each cache directory, remove files that match the temporary pattern `^[0-9a-f]{8}\.[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$`, and log what was removed. The rename never happened, so the entry's last completed write, from the ready-time flush, is i

docs.title: sessions: stop PR artifact workspace settings from flooding the session channel
docs.body:
Fixes #347984

## What changed

The GitHub pull request artifact workspace-settings synchronizer could send a stream of `session/configChanged` actions for the same session and artifact, alternating between two working directories. Each write makes the host rewrite the session `_meta`, so a sustained alternation overflowed the session's state-channel queue and closed the shared Agent Host connection.

- **One writer per session/artifact.** Before this change, every live reference installed its own synchronizer with its own duplicate check, so two references with different contexts overwrote each other on every re-evaluation. `AgentHostArtifactIntegrations` now shares a single writer across all live references. It publishes the most recently acquired reference's context, falls back to the previous one when that reference is released, and is disposed with the last reference.
- **Publish only settled values.** A changed value is sent only after it stays unchanged for 250 ms. A context that keeps alternating is never sent, and a value that reverts to the last published one cancels the pending write. Reconnects, replaced session config, and settings edits still publish as before, just after the short delay.

## How it was verified

Reproduced in Code OSS (Agents window, local Agent Host) with dbgjs by hooking the live connection:
- Before: alternating one reference's working directo

docs.body:

## Repro steps

1. In a Git repository, change a file and run `git stash` to create stash A (`stash@{0}`).
2. Run **Git: View Stash...** and pick stash A. A multi-diff editor titled `Git Stash #0: ...` opens.
3. Leave that editor open.
4. Make different changes and run `git stash` again. Stash B is now `stash@{0}`, and A is `stash@{1}`.
5. Run **Git: View Stash...** and pick stash B (`#0`).

`CommandCenter._viewStash` built the multi-diff editor's source URI from the stash index (`git-stash:` URI with ref `stash@{N}`). `MultiDiffEditorInput.matches()` identifies an editor by that source URI. The editor title actions (`git.stashApplyEditor`, `git.stashPopEditor`, `git.stashDropEditor`) resolve the stash from the same URI in `getStashFromUri`, parsing `stash@{N}` back into an index. A stale editor

docs.title: Git - don't use an unresolved upstream as the Source Control Graph's remote ref
docs.body:
Fixes #261561

## Repro steps

1. Create a repository whose branch tracks a ref that is not a local branch, using the local repository as the remote:
   ```sh
   git init -b main repro && cd repro
   git commit --allow-empty --allow-empty-message -m ''
   git update-ref FOO HEAD
   git config branch.main.remote .
   git config branch.main.merge FOO
   git commit --allow-empty --allow-empty-message -m ''
   git status   # "Your branch is ahead of 'FOO' by 1 commit."
   ```
2. Open the `repro` folder in VS Code.
3. Open the Source Control view and look at the Graph.
4. 🐛 The Graph shows "The selected source control provider does not have any source control history items." It should show the two commits.

## Root cause

- For `merge = FOO`, `git for-each-ref` reports `%(upstream:remotename)` = `.` and `%(upstream:remoteref)` = `FOO`. `Repository.getBranch()` assumes `remoteref` starts with `refs/heads/` and strips 11 characters, so `HEAD.upstream` becomes `{ remote: '.', name: '' }`.
- `getHEADRef()` then tries to resolve `refs/heads/`, which fails, so `HEAD.upstream.commit` stays `undefined`.
- `GitHistoryProvider.onDidRunWriteOperation()` still turns the upstream into `currentHistoryItemRemoteRef` with id `refs/heads/`. The graph passes that id in `historyItemRefs`, so `git log ... --stdin` fails with `fatal: bad revision 'refs/heads/'`. `provideHistoryItems()` catches the erro

docs.body:
Fixes #284185

## Repro steps

1. Open a Git repository (for example `<parent>/app`).
2. Run **Git: Create Worktree...** (also available from the Repositories view), pick **Create new branch...** and enter `feature-one`.
3. When asked for the worktree path, choose a folder other than the suggested `<parent>/app.worktrees/feature-one`, for example `<parent>/custom-worktrees/feature-one` (type it or use the folder button).
4. Run **Git: Create Worktree...** again with branch `feature-two`.

## Root cause

Before #278107, the `git.createWorktree` command saved the parent folder of the worktree the user created under the `worktreeRoot:<repository root>` global state key whenever it differed from the stored value. The refactor moved this into `Repository.createWorktree()` and changed the condition to `defaultWorktreeRoot && !pathEquals(newWorktreeRoot, defaultWorktreeRoot)`. While nothing is stored yet, which is the case for every repository after the refactor, `defaultWorktreeRoot` is `undefined` and nothing is ever written. As a result, the first custom location is never remembered and the command keeps suggesting `<repo>.worktrees/...`.

docs.body:
In an agent host session, the editor's Keep and Undo could disappear for a file that the working set above the chat input still listed as pending. They only came back once the agent edited that file again.

The editor review marked a file as undone on its own whenever a change the session didn't record returned the document to its baseline. Stashing the file's changes does that, and so does undoing the reload of the agent's edit in the editor. The host decides what is kept or undone in these sessions, and it still listed the file, so the editor and the working set disagreed. Restoring the content didn't bring the changes back either, because the review counted the restored text as the user's.

Fixes #244698

When a terminal line has the same path more than once with different line numbers, like `foo/file1.txt:1 foo/file1.txt:20`, clicking the second link opens (or searches for) `foo/file1.txt:1`. These are search links, and `TerminalSearchLinkOpener` takes the line/column from the first link parsed from the context line whose path the clicked text starts with, which is always the first occurrence.

docs.title: fix: resolve non-ASCII route segments
docs.body:
## Summary

I encountered this in an App Router project on Next.js 16.4.2: naming a route directory `교사-월급-계산기` caused a direct request to `/교사-월급-계산기` to return HTTP 404. Renaming the directory to its percent-encoded equivalent made the same URL return HTTP 200.

A reduced example is:

```text
app/교사-월급-계산기/page.tsx
```

Route definitions retain Unicode names, while HTTP requests contain UTF-8 percent escapes. The filesystem route lookup and static route comparison did not consistently recognize these as the same route. Dynamic route regexes also matched only the literal Unicode static segments. After resolving the route, segment cache key generation could additionally throw because `btoa()` was called on the Unicode segment directly.

This change:

- Resolves percent-encoded non-ASCII static pathnames to their filesystem route definitions, preserving ASCII escapes such as `%2F` and `%25`.
- Makes both regular and named route regexes accept literal Unicode and percent-encoded static segments, including lowercase hex escapes. Dynamic captures are left untouched for the existing parameter decoder, avoiding an additional decode of the entire request pathname.
- Encodes segment cache keys as UTF-8 bytes before base64url encoding.
- Adds App Router and Pages Router coverage for direct requests, prerendered pages, client navigation, reloads, existing percent-encoded directory names,

docs.title: turbo-persistence: bounds-check SST block reads
docs.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #100313, which validates the block directory size and the index block range when an SST is opened.

Reads of every other block still trusted the block directory offsets, and the block CRC does not cover them. The bounds guards only existed behind the `strict_checks` feature. Without it, a corrupt offset for a key or value block had these effects:

- **mmap:** an out-of-bounds slice panic.
- **File mode:** an out-of-range `block_offsets[i]` panic, or an allocation of up to 4 GB before `pread` failed.
- **`sst_inspect`:** unchecked slicing, plus an `assert_eq!` on the decompressed length.

This adds a shared `StaticSortedFileMetaData::block_range` check that runs on every block read, whatever the feature set. It rejects:

- `block_index >= block_count`, before the directory is read;
- ranges that are reversed or too short for the 8-byte block header (using checked arithmetic);
- ranges that extend past the data section into the directory or beyond the end of the file.

All readers now use this check: the mmap reader, the shared file-mode reader used by lookups and by iteration, the open-time index validation, and `sst_inspect`. The redundant `strict_checks` guards are removed, and the feature itself is kept. File-mode allocations are now bounded by the size of the data section. docs.title: turbo-persistence: cover block lengths in CRCs
docs.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #100313.

The 8-byte headers of SST blocks and blob files store `[uncompressed_length][crc32]`, but the CRC only covered the payload. A corrupted length therefore passed the checksum check and could:

- make a reader allocate a decompression buffer of up to 4 GB;
- flip whether a block is treated as compressed (`0` means uncompressed).

The CRC now covers the four big-endian length bytes followed by the on-disk payload. `checksum_block(uncompressed_length, data)` hashes both incrementally with `crc32fast::Hasher`, so no extra copy is made.

Readers verify this checksum before using the length to allocate decompression output or to choose the decompression path. That covers:

- SST lookups in mmap and file mode, plus file-backed decoded iteration and the index block read with `pread`;
- blob reads;
- `sst_inspect`.

The index block's checksum is now verified before its sentinel check, so a corrupted index length is reported as a checksum error.

The on-disk layout is unchanged, but the meaning of the checksum changes. Caches written by older builds fail validation and are treated as cache corruption.

Iteration still passes medium value blocks to compaction as raw bytes without decompressing them. Their original length and CRC are preserved through the copy, so a corrupted block is detected when the copied value is read. The README documents the new checks

## Summary

Stacked on #100294.

Documents in the OpenTelemetry guide that spans created while `instrumentation.ts` loads or inside `register()` don't automatically join a request trace:

- Spans started before the tracer provider is installed (e.g. at module top level before `registerOTel()`) are not recorded.

It also clarifies the existing sentence so it refers to spans created while handling a request, and recommends creating request-scoped spans in request-handling code.

```
docs.title: turbo-persistence: faster key block sorting
docs.body:
## Summary

`KeyOnly` key blocks with 4-byte and 8-byte keys were stably sorted as `&PendingEntry`, reading both keys through their entries on every comparison. Each key is now read once into a dense `(key << bits) | index` integer, and those integers are sorted unstably. The index keeps equal keys in their original order, preserving the stable order needed for tombstones. In the original profile, this roughly halved the sort of a full 4-byte-key block (6.96 → 3.78 µs).

This also adds tests for `MergeIter`, covering ordering, newest-first equal keys, multi-value groups, input errors, and randomized comparisons against a sorted reference.

AMQF fingerprint construction is unchanged. I compared `sort_by_key` against the existing `sort_unstable_by_key` there; on a full compaction of 16Mi 8-byte-key / 4-byte-value entries over 32 commits, the difference wasn't statistically significant (5.66 s vs 5.90 s, `p = 0.22`).

## Summary

Compaction iterated its input SST files through an mmap with `MADV_SEQUENTIAL`. This does not fit the block layout pattern (which tends to be ValueBlock, ValueBlock, KeyBlock....) because iteration starts from key blocks, so the readahead isn't well targeted.  OS level reclaim can recover this memory but it isn't eager and we _know_ after reading a block that we don't need it any more.

`StaticSortedFileIter`, which only compaction uses, now always reads blocks with `pread` into owned buffers, independent of the overall database's `AccessMode`, so an open input file holds only the blocks it currently uses. 

This also enhances SharedBytes with a mechanism to be constructed from an `uninit` buffer (useful for decompression and `pread` targets).  This unifies a few codepaths and allows us to avoid some small buffer copies.
```
